chapter.firsttorch.welcome.title: Welcome
chapter.firsttorch.welcome.description: Learn how the native First Torch course works before you unlock its First Steps lessons.
quest.firsttorch.welcome.welcome.title: Welcome to First Torch
quest.firsttorch.welcome.welcome.descrip:
Welcome! First Torch teaches Minecraft in small, practical steps. You do not need prior knowledge or need to remember everything at once.

This Welcome chapter is already available in the native alpha. Its cards explain how to read, complete, and claim lessons.

Proof action: after reading this card, press Confirm task. It gives exactly 5 experience points once you complete it; these are points, not five whole levels.
quest.firsttorch.welcome.overview.title: Chapters and Overview
quest.firsttorch.welcome.overview.descri:
At first, only Welcome is shown. Further chapters appear as soon as you can begin one of their tasks. Started and completed chapters stay visible so you can read their lessons again.

Click a quest card to expand its reading column on the right; the chapter icons compact so the text has room. Select Overview to restore the full path. The mouse wheel scrolls long text in the right-hand details column. There is no map dragging or zooming.

Search finds tasks in chapters that are already visible. The cup at the top right opens your trophy collection; Esc returns from there to quests.

Proof action: open this card, scroll its details with the mouse wheel, then choose Overview and confirm this task.
quest.firsttorch.welcome.reading.title: Reading a Quest
quest.firsttorch.welcome.reading.descrip:
A selected quest opens its explanation in the right reading column. Read the goal, the reason, the practical steps, and any safety advice there. Escape closes First Torch.

In an ordinary single-player world, reading pauses the game. A multiplayer server and a world opened to LAN keep running, so stand somewhere safe before you read.

Proof action: select this card, read the safety note, then press Confirm task at the bottom.
quest.firsttorch.welcome.paths.title: Prerequisites and Locks
quest.firsttorch.welcome.paths.descripti:
Arrows show prerequisite relationships. A lock means a required earlier quest is not complete yet; finish its task and the next card becomes available.

This Welcome path branches after the first card, then joins again at Ready for First Steps. Completing that final card reveals First Steps and unlocks its first lesson. Further chapters appear according to their own prerequisites; you do not need to finish every optional exercise first.

Proof action: inspect one arrow or lock on the overview, then confirm this task.
quest.firsttorch.welcome.tasks.title: Tasks and Confirmations
quest.firsttorch.welcome.tasks.descripti:
For this Welcome chapter, every task is manual: press Confirm task only after you have done the proof action in the card.

Native inventory tasks check an exact item and count, or every item in a named item group, without consuming anything. Once the server records completion, it stays complete even if you later remove the item. Other automatic task types are not available yet.

Proof action: explain to yourself the difference between a manual confirmation and a non-consuming inventory check, then confirm this task.
quest.firsttorch.welcome.rewards.title: Claiming Rewards
quest.firsttorch.welcome.rewards.descrip:
A completed quest with rewards has one Claim rewards button at the bottom of its details. Claim the whole reward batch there; rewards are not claimed from icons and there is no unclaimed marker on the overview.

The first Welcome quest pays its five experience points once only. Item rewards need enough free inventory space for the entire batch; make space first, then try again.

Proof action: return to Welcome to find its bottom Claim rewards button, claim its 5 XP if you have not already, then confirm this task.
quest.firsttorch.welcome.opening.title: Opening First Torch Again
quest.firsttorch.welcome.opening.descrip:
By default, press the key directly below Escape and left of 1 to open First Torch. Its printed symbol depends on your keyboard layout. You can change this under Options → Controls → Key Binds → First Torch. Choose any free key that feels comfortable.

Escape closes the screen. The native alpha has no physical book item, book recipe, or replacement recipe yet.

Proof action: close First Torch with Escape, reopen it with your opening key, then confirm this task.
quest.firsttorch.welcome.ready.title: Ready for First Steps
quest.firsttorch.welcome.ready.descripti:
You now know how to use First Torch: read a lesson, check its prerequisites, confirm a task and claim a reward.

Completing this card reveals First Steps in the chapter list. After the first mouse lesson, you can begin your first shelter or practise the optional movement exercises. Further tasks follow their own arrows. You can reopen the introduction at any time.

Proof action: check that all six middle Welcome cards are complete, then press Confirm task to finish the introduction.
chapter.firsttorch.first_steps.title: First Steps
chapter.firsttorch.first_steps.descripti: Learn the mouse buttons, then optionally practise jumping, sneaking, sprinting, and sprint-jumping. The separate shelter and tool routes start from Your Hands and Mouse Buttons; they do not wait for the movement exercises. Complete Welcome first to begin.
chapter.firsttorch.first_shelter.title: Your First Shelter
chapter.firsttorch.first_shelter.descrip: Turn wood into planks, set up a crafting table and shovel, then make an emergency shelter and sleep safely. This route begins from Your Hands and Mouse Buttons and can run alongside the optional movement exercises.
chapter.firsttorch.safe_home.title: A Safe Home
chapter.firsttorch.safe_home.description: Make a wooden pickaxe, collect stone, then build stone tools, a furnace, chest, and torches into a safe home. Some cards point back to your shelter route; follow their individual prerequisites.
quest.firsttorch.first_steps.hands.title: Your Hands and Mouse Buttons
quest.firsttorch.first_steps.hands.descr:
Goal: learn the two most important mouse buttons.

By default, your character holds items in the right hand. You can see that hand at the lower-right of the screen.

Left mouse button = attack button. Use it to attack or break a block. To break a block, keep holding it until the block breaks completely.

Right mouse button = use button. Use it to interact with a block or place the item in your hand.

If you are left-handed, you can change the main hand in the settings. Key bindings can be changed under Options → Controls.

Reward: Two Apples give you a little time until a later lesson teaches you how to find food reliably.

Proof action: after reading, press Confirm task.
quest.firsttorch.first_steps.jump.title: Jumping over Obstacles (optional)
quest.firsttorch.first_steps.jump.descri:
Optional movement practice. Goal: jump onto one full block in a safe place.

The default jump key is Space. Hold W to move forward and briefly press Space to jump onto a block in front of you.

Practise in daylight on flat ground without a ledge, Lava, or another hazard. Place one ordinary full block on the ground and use it for the exercise.

Important: You automatically walk up slabs and stairs. You do not need to jump over them. An ordinary full block is taller and requires a jump.

Do not jump unnecessarily on dangerous ground. A missed jump or a long fall can cost health.

Proof action: after you have safely jumped onto one full block, press Confirm task.
quest.firsttorch.first_steps.sneak.title: Sneaking Safely (optional)
quest.firsttorch.first_steps.sneak.descr:
Optional movement practice. Goal: practise sneaking and stop safely at a block edge.

Hold Left Shift to sneak. Your character moves more slowly and crouches slightly.

Practise first on a harmless platform only one block high. Hold Left Shift and move slowly toward its edge. While you keep sneaking, you normally do not simply walk over the block edge.

Take care: You can walk down slabs and stairs while sneaking. Their lower edge does not stop you like the edge of a full block does. Always check the route beneath your feet.

Sneaking is not complete fall protection. Enemies, Water, and other forces can still move you, and a block that disappears can no longer support you. Never rely on the key alone beside a real drop.

Proof action: after trying sneaking at a safe edge, press Confirm task.
quest.firsttorch.first_steps.sprint.desc:
Optional movement practice. Goal: sprint once along a short, clear route.

Hold W to move forward and also press Left Control. Alternatively, press W twice quickly and keep holding it after the second press.

Practise in daylight on a flat, open route. Sprinting moves you noticeably faster, but it also uses food more quickly.

You cannot sprint when your Hunger is very low. Sprinting also ends when you run into an obstacle or release the forward key.

Do not sprint blindly across unknown ground, beside a ledge, or into a dark cave. The extra speed leaves less time to react.

Proof action: after you have sprinted under control along a short, clear route, press Confirm task.
quest.firsttorch.first_steps.sprint_jump:
Optional movement practice. Goal: perform one sprint-jump along a clear, flat route.

Begin sprinting as before. Briefly press Space while sprinting, then slow down under control after you land.

Sprint-jumping moves you forward quickly, but it uses food particularly fast. Slabs and stairs are often calmer and more efficient for ordinary paths.

Practise only on well-lit, flat ground with plenty of clear space. Keep away from ledges, Lava, deep Water, and anything you cannot land on safely.

Reward: Two Apples replace a small part of the food you used. Five XP points recognise completing the movement practice.

Proof action: after one safe sprint-jump, press Confirm task.

quest.firsttorch.first_steps.planks.desc:
Goal: turn any log into four wooden planks.

1. Walk to a tree and point the crosshair in the centre of the screen at its trunk.

2. Hold the left mouse button. Wait until the cracks finish and the log block breaks.

3. Walk over the small dropped log. It is picked up automatically and appears in your hotbar or inventory.

4. Press E. Pick up the log with the left mouse button and place it in any one of the four Crafting spaces. It does not matter which space you use.

5. Four planks appear in the result slot on the right. Click them, then click an empty inventory slot. Shift + left-click moves them directly into your inventory.

The task completes automatically when four planks of any wood type are in your inventory. Mixed wood types count together too.
quest.firsttorch.first_steps.crafting_ta:
Goal: craft a Crafting Table and place it on the ground.

1. Press E. Put one wooden plank in each of the four spaces of the small 2 × 2 crafting grid. Click the Crafting Table in the result slot and place it in your hotbar.

2. Keep the Crafting Table in your inventory briefly so its automatic task can complete. Close the inventory with E. Select the Crafting Table in your hotbar with the mouse wheel or its number key. You can now see it in your right hand.

3. Point the crosshair at a clear ground block directly in front of you and press the right mouse button. The Crafting Table now stands there.

Press the right mouse button on the placed Crafting Table again. This opens the large 3 × 3 crafting grid.
quest.firsttorch.first_steps.pickaxe.des:
Goal: craft a Wooden Pickaxe.

1. Open the Crafting Table. Put two planks vertically in its 3 × 3 grid. Any column works. Take the four sticks from the result slot.

2. Open the placed Crafting Table with the right mouse button. Fill the entire top row with three planks. Put one stick in the exact centre and a second stick directly below it.

3. Click the Wooden Pickaxe in the result slot and place it in your hotbar.

A pickaxe mines stone and ore. Using the wrong tool can be very slow and may destroy the drop.
quest.firsttorch.first_steps.shovel.desc:
Goal: craft a Wooden Shovel and use it to break one easy-to-reach Dirt block.

A Shovel is the suitable tool for Dirt, Grass Blocks, Sand, Gravel, Clay, and Snow. Some of these blocks can also be broken by hand or another tool, but a Shovel is much faster.

Do not use the Pickaxe for this work. It is intended for stone and ores; it works slowly on soft ground and loses durability unnecessarily. An Axe will later handle wood.

Open the Crafting Table. Put one Wooden Plank in the top-middle slot. Put one Stick directly below it and a second Stick in the bottom-middle slot. Take the Wooden Shovel from the result slot.

Select the Shovel in the hotbar and hold the left mouse button to break a Dirt block at the surface. Never dig straight down beneath your feet.

After trying the difference in breaking speed, press Confirm task.
quest.firsttorch.first_steps.cobble.desc:
Goal: mine at least eight Cobblestone with your Wooden Pickaxe.

Collecting stone works almost exactly like collecting wood: look at the block, hold the left mouse button, and pick up the dropped item. The important difference is the tool.

1. Select the Wooden Pickaxe in your hotbar. You must be able to see it in your hand.

2. Find grey stone on a hillside or near the surface and point the crosshair at it.

3. Hold the left mouse button until the stone block breaks completely. Walk over the dropped Cobblestone; it is picked up automatically again.

Repeat these three steps until eight Cobblestone are in your inventory at the same time. The task deliberately stays incomplete at 1 through 7.

Never dig straight down: you could fall into a cave, lava, or a deep hole.

Keep a clear route back to daylight. Eight Cobblestone is enough for the next essential block.
quest.firsttorch.first_steps.axe.title: Your First Axe
quest.firsttorch.first_steps.axe.descrip:
Goal: craft a Stone Axe and use it to break one reachable log block.

An axe is the suitable tool for logs, Wooden Planks, Crafting Tables, Chests, and many other wooden blocks. You can collect most of them by hand, but an axe is considerably faster.

Open the Crafting Table. Put Cobblestone in the top-left, top-centre, and centre-left spaces. Put one Stick in the centre and a second directly below it. The recipe may also be mirrored on the right side.

Take the Stone Axe from the result slot and select it in your hotbar. Point the crosshair at a reachable log and hold the left mouse button until it breaks. Clear a tree from the bottom upward and do not leave a floating treetop behind.

Take care: pressing the right mouse button on many logs only strips away their bark. This changes their appearance and uses durability. Continue to use the left mouse button for ordinary breaking.

The Pickaxe remains the correct tool for stone and ore. Tools wear down while working and break when their durability is exhausted.

After breaking one log block with the Stone Axe, press Confirm task.

Reward: Three Cobblestone replace the Axe material so that your eight Cobblestone remain available for the following Furnace.
quest.firsttorch.first_steps.furnace.des:
Goal: craft a Furnace.

1. Open the Crafting Table with the right mouse button.

2. Put Cobblestone in all eight outside spaces of the 3 × 3 grid. Leave the exact centre space empty.

3. Take the Furnace from the result slot and place it in your inventory or hotbar. Keep it there briefly so its automatic task can complete.

The top furnace slot holds what you want to cook or smelt. The bottom slot holds fuel. Planks and logs work, but coal and charcoal last longer.

Fuels burn for different lengths of time: two Sticks process one item. One Wooden Plank or log processes one item with a little burn time left. One Coal or Charcoal processes up to eight items.

Fuel keeps burning when the upper slot becomes empty. Put all ingredients in the upper slot first, then choose suitable fuel below so as little heat as possible is wasted.
quest.firsttorch.first_steps.chest.title: Your First Chest
quest.firsttorch.first_steps.chest.descr:
Goal: craft a Chest, place it, and practise storing an item.

1. Open the Crafting Table. Put eight Wooden Planks in every outside space of the 3 × 3 grid; leave the centre empty. Take the Chest from the result slot.

2. Keep the Chest in your inventory briefly so its automatic task can complete. Put it in your hotbar, select it, and place it on a clear floor block inside your shelter with the right mouse button.

3. Open it with the right mouse button. The upper spaces belong to the Chest; your inventory is below. Pick up an unimportant item with the left mouse button, then click an empty Chest space. Shift + left-click moves a stack directly between your inventory and the Chest.

4. Take the item out again and close the Chest with E or Esc. Then press Confirm task.

Important: Breaking a filled Chest drops its contents. Do not break it above Lava or while your inventory is nearly full.

Reward: 5 experience points for your first small storage station.
quest.firsttorch.first_steps.torch.title: First Torch
quest.firsttorch.first_steps.torch.descr:
Goal: make at least eight Torches.

A torch is crafted from one coal or charcoal above one stick. Each pair makes four torches.

No coal yet? Make Charcoal first:

1. Place the Furnace just like the Crafting Table, then open it with the right mouse button.

2. Put one log in the top slot. Put one wooden plank into the bottom fuel slot. Wait until the arrow fills.

3. One Charcoal appears on the right. Click it and place it in your inventory.

At the Crafting Table, put the Charcoal above one stick. Repeat the recipe twice to make eight Torches.

Place torches inside your shelter, around the entrance, and along paths you want to find again.

Reward: Two more Apples as a small reserve for your first night.
quest.firsttorch.first_steps.emergency_s:
Goal: immediately build a simple enclosed emergency shelter before darkness arrives.

Use the Shovel to dig a small room into a safe hillside, or build a shell from easily available solid blocks such as Dirt. Leave an interior at least two blocks wide, three blocks long, and two blocks high so a Bed and safe standing space will fit later.

Build solid walls and a roof without gaps at ground level. Leave only one entrance to walk through. Seal it completely from inside with solid blocks when the Sun is low or enemies appear. This emergency version does not yet need a Door or a Torch.

Stay inside after darkness arrives. Do not fight Skeletons or other enemies merely to continue the next quests. Continue the parallel tool route during daylight while remaining near the shelter.

When you stand in the interior with at least two blocks of height and can completely close its only entrance, press Confirm task.

Reward: Three blocks of White Wool. Claim them; together with three Wooden Planks, they let you craft your first Bed.
quest.firsttorch.first_steps.bed.title: Your First Bed
quest.firsttorch.first_steps.bed.descrip:
Goal: craft a White Bed, place it inside your emergency shelter, and sleep in it.

1. First claim the three blocks of White Wool from the shelter quest's reward. Craft at least three Wooden Planks as well.

2. Open the Crafting Table. Put three White Wool horizontally in one row and three Wooden Planks directly underneath. Take the White Bed from the result slot.

3. Place the Bed inside your shelter with the right mouse button. Leave some clear space above and beside it so you can get up safely.

4. Use the Bed at night with the right mouse button. You skip the night and set your respawn point there. If you die later, you appear beside this Bed as long as it still exists and can be reached. Your first successful sleep is detected automatically.

If it is still daytime, leave the Bed in place and continue the parallel tool route nearby. Return before darkness. Do not carry the Bed on an outing: without the Bed at home, your respawn point may be lost.

The task completes automatically as soon as you have successfully slept in a Bed.
task.firsttorch.4397f12a5db846e0.title: Slept in a Bed for the first time
quest.firsttorch.first_steps.shelter_upg: Upgrade the Emergency Shelter into a Home

Goal: turn the quick emergency shelter into a home suitable for continued use.

Expand the interior if needed. Keep solid walls and a complete roof, place the Bed and Chest safely inside, and use Torches to light both the interior and the area directly outside the entrance.

Build an entrance that can be closed reliably. A Wooden Door opens and closes with the right mouse button; solid blocks still work temporarily. Leave no other gaps at ground level.

Zombies and Skeletons can attack through an open or poorly protected entrance. Spiders can climb walls, so the roof must remain completely closed.

Set the checkmark when walls, roof, lighting, and entrance are safe and the Bed and Chest are protected inside.
task.firsttorch.1fa284b6c9d03e75.title: My shelter is enclosed, lit, and furnished
quest.firsttorch.first_steps.morning.des:
You now know the first survival loop: collect wood, make a Crafting Table and Shovel, prepare an emergency shelter and Bed before darkness, then use stone tools, a Furnace, Chest, and Torches to upgrade it into a safe home.

Stay near your shelter at first in the morning. Take spare blocks, tools, and torches, and remember where your shelter is. Food is taught in the next chapter; do not begin a long journey without it.

Mark this quest after you have reached a safe morning. The next chapter will teach food, health, mining, and the equipment that makes you more independent.

Reward: Three Bread help you begin the food chapter. The Lantern is your First Torch trophy—place it at your home if you like.
task.firsttorch.65b9134c7fda6803.title: I reached a safe morning
chapter.firsttorch.food.title: Food and Hunger
chapter.firsttorch.food.description: Find food, cook it safely, and keep a small reserve for the road.
image.firsttorch.hunger_and_eating.descr: The hunger drumsticks above the hotbar and a player eating food.
image.firsttorch.cooking_food.descriptio: A Furnace cooking raw Beef with fuel below it and cooked Beef in the result slot.
quest.firsttorch.food.hunger.title: Notice Hunger and Eat
quest.firsttorch.food.hunger.description:
Goal: find your hunger bar and eat one piece of food.

Above the right side of your hotbar are ten small drumsticks. They show your hunger, not your inventory. Running, jumping, and working gradually empty them.

Select Bread or an Apple in your hotbar. When the hunger bar is not full, hold the right mouse button until the eating animation finishes.

If the hunger bar is full, you cannot eat normal food—this is not an error. Save it for later. Hunger usually stays full on Peaceful difficulty.

You cannot sprint when only three or fewer drumsticks are filled. Do not wait until the bar is completely empty.

The task automatically detects the first time you eat something. If you already ate earlier, it may complete immediately. This optional quest does not block the following lessons; return later if your Hunger bar is full.

Reward: One Apple replaces a small part of the food used for the experiment.
task.firsttorch.6f20b4d98c315ea7.title: Eat something for the first time
quest.firsttorch.food.source.title: Your First Food Source
quest.firsttorch.food.source.description:
Goal: obtain at least one raw ingredient for the Furnace.

Choose whichever option is available near you:

• Cows drop raw Beef, pigs drop Porkchops, chickens drop raw Chicken, and sheep drop raw Mutton. Animals flee when attacked—stay behind them and use the left mouse button.

• Cod and Salmon swim in rivers or oceans. Attack them only from a safe bank or shallow water; do not risk drowning for one meal.

• Potatoes sometimes grow on village farms. Take only a few and replant some. Kelp grows in many bodies of water and can also be dried.

The task automatically accepts any of these raw ingredients. You do not need all of them.
task.firsttorch.09e4a72d5c813bf6.title: Hold one raw ingredient for the Furnace
quest.firsttorch.food.cook.title: Cook Food Safely
quest.firsttorch.food.cook.description:
Goal: cook your raw ingredient in the Furnace.

1. Place your Furnace in a safe location and open it with the right mouse button.

2. Put raw meat, raw fish, a Potato, or Kelp in the upper slot.

3. Put Coal, Charcoal, or Wooden Planks in the lower slot. The flames show that the Furnace is working.

4. Wait for the arrow to fill completely. Take the finished food from the right and move it into your inventory.

The picture uses Beef as an example. The other listed ingredients work the same way. Cooked meat usually restores more hunger and is safer than raw meat.

Reward: One Charcoal for your next Furnace load.
task.firsttorch.2e73c5a09d164bf8.title: Hold one cooked food
quest.firsttorch.food.health.title: Hunger and Health Work Together
quest.firsttorch.food.health.description:
The hearts above the left side of your hotbar show health. Food does not fill hearts directly; it fills the hunger bar on the right first.

When at least nine of the ten hunger drumsticks are filled, lost health begins to recover automatically after a short time. Healing uses some hunger again.

If you are hurt, move somewhere safe first. Eat until the hunger bar is almost full, then wait. Do not keep fighting with only a few hearts.

Mark the quest when you understand the difference between hearts and hunger.
task.firsttorch.18c6f2a75d409be3.title: I know the difference between health and hunger
quest.firsttorch.food.risky.title: Not Everything Edible Is a Good Idea
quest.firsttorch.food.risky.description:
Some items can be eaten but may cause harmful effects:

• Rotten Flesh can cause extra hunger.
• Raw Chicken can cause extra hunger.
• Spider Eyes and Poisonous Potatoes can poison you.
• Pufferfish are especially dangerous and can cause severe poisoning.

Do not eat these as a beginner. Store them separately or throw them away if they make your inventory confusing.

Mark the quest when you know which four groups to avoid for now.
task.firsttorch.43d1a8f70c625be9.title: I recognise risky food
quest.firsttorch.food.reserve.title: A Small Food Reserve
quest.firsttorch.food.reserve.descriptio:
Goal: hold at least four cooked foods in your inventory at the same time.

Obtain and cook more ingredients with the same routine. Cooked meat, cooked fish, Baked Potatoes, and Dried Kelp are accepted and may be mixed.

Four pieces are not a permanent food supply. They are a small reserve while the next lessons teach health, protection, and safe mining.

Do not leave all your food in a distant chest while travelling. Keep a small reserve in your hotbar so you can select it quickly when danger appears.

Reward: One Cookie to celebrate your first self-gathered food reserve.
task.firsttorch.3d85f1c70a624be9.title: Hold 4 cooked foods in your inventory
chapter.firsttorch.ores.title: First Ores
chapter.firsttorch.ores.description: Retreat safely, make a Stone Pickaxe, and collect your first Iron or Copper.
image.firsttorch.stone_pickaxe.descripti: Crafting recipe for a Stone Pickaxe: three Cobblestone across the top and two Sticks in the middle column.
quest.firsttorch.ores.retreat.title: Notice Damage and Retreat
quest.firsttorch.ores.retreat.descriptio:
The hearts above the left side of your hotbar show your health. They flash and some become empty when you are hit. Continuing to fight with only a few hearts is usually the worst choice.

Turn away from the enemy and sprint toward your lit shelter or along a route you know. Close the door or block the entrance. Do not flee blindly into a dark cave, deep water, or over a ledge.

Eat and let your health recover only after you are safe. Mark the quest when you know your route home and when to abandon a fight.
task.firsttorch.4e16b8c30d795af2.title: I know my safe route home
quest.firsttorch.ores.stone_pickaxe.desc:
Goal: craft a Stone Pickaxe.

Open the Crafting Table. Fill the entire top row with three Cobblestone. Then place two Sticks below each other in the middle column. Take the Stone Pickaxe from the result slot on the right.

Important: a Wooden Pickaxe can break Iron Ore, but it will not drop Raw Iron. You must use at least a Stone Pickaxe for Iron Ore.
task.firsttorch.57a0d4c91e326bf8.title: Hold a Stone Pickaxe
quest.firsttorch.ores.raw_iron.title: Your First Raw Iron
quest.firsttorch.ores.raw_iron.descripti:
Goal: collect at least one Raw Iron.

Iron Ore is a grey stone block with tan-coloured speckles. This quest's icon shows the real Iron Ore block from your game. If you use a different resource pack, the icon changes with it.

First look on an exposed rock face or around a shallow, clearly visible cave entrance. You do not need to enter a deep cave yet.

Hold the Stone Pickaxe in your attack hand, point at the Iron Ore, and hold the left mouse button. Walk over the dropped Raw Iron to move it into your inventory.

Keep daylight or your lit route home in sight. Never dig straight down beneath your feet—the next block could hide a cave or lava.
task.firsttorch.0d39a7e25c614bf8.title: Hold one Raw Iron
quest.firsttorch.ores.iron_ingot.title: An Iron Ingot
quest.firsttorch.ores.iron_ingot.descrip:
Goal: smelt your Raw Iron into an Iron Ingot.

Open your Furnace. Put Raw Iron in the upper slot and fuel in the lower slot. Wood or Sticks are enough for one Raw Iron; Coal or Charcoal can process up to eight items.

Wait until the arrow fills completely. Take the Iron Ingot from the slot on the right and move it into your inventory.
task.firsttorch.61e4a8c20d935bf7.title: Hold one Iron Ingot
quest.firsttorch.ores.raw_copper.title: Your First Raw Copper
quest.firsttorch.ores.raw_copper.descrip:
Goal: collect at least one Raw Copper.

Copper Ore is a grey stone block with orange and greenish speckles. This quest's icon shows the real Copper Ore block from your game and follows your active resource pack.

Copper often appears in larger veins, making it useful for your first Armour. Mine it just like Iron Ore with the Stone Pickaxe. A Wooden Pickaxe will not give you Raw Copper.

This branch now unlocks the Armour lesson, but not the Shield. A Shield still requires an Iron Ingot.
task.firsttorch.5b39d7f20e846ac1.title: Hold one Raw Copper
quest.firsttorch.ores.copper_ingot.title: A Copper Ingot
quest.firsttorch.ores.copper_ingot.descr:
Goal: smelt your Raw Copper into a Copper Ingot.

Put Raw Copper in the upper Furnace slot and fuel in the lower slot. Wait until the arrow fills completely, then take the Copper Ingot from the slot on the right.

The Armour lesson is now available. Keep this Copper Ingot as useful material for it.
task.firsttorch.7d5bf9042ea68c31.title: Hold one Copper Ingot
chapter.firsttorch.protection.title: Shield and Armour
chapter.firsttorch.protection.descriptio: Craft a Shield, learn the armour recipes, and practise avoiding danger.
image.firsttorch.shield.description: Crafting recipe for a Shield and its offhand slot beside the player inventory.
image.firsttorch.armour_recipes.descript: The four Armour recipes: Helmet, Chestplate, Leggings, and Boots.
quest.firsttorch.protection.shield.title: Your First Shield
quest.firsttorch.protection.shield.descr:
Goal: craft a Shield.

In the Crafting Table, place Plank – Iron Ingot – Plank across the top. Fill the middle row with three Wooden Planks. Finally, place one Wooden Plank in the bottom-centre slot.

You may mix Planks from different wood types. Then press E to open your inventory. Pick up the Shield with the left mouse button and place it in the single offhand slot beside your character, exactly as the orange arrow shows.

A Shield is especially useful because it can protect you while your attack hand still holds a tool or weapon.
task.firsttorch.12a6e3d80c754bf9.title: Hold a Shield
quest.firsttorch.protection.armour.title: How Armour Is Crafted
quest.firsttorch.protection.armour.descr:
Goal: learn the four Armour recipes.

The pictures use Copper Ingots because Copper is often found early. At every occupied slot, you may instead use Leather, Iron Ingots, Gold Ingots, or Diamonds. Use the same material throughout one Armour piece.

The four recipes are arranged in two columns: Helmet (5 pieces) at top left, Chestplate (8 pieces) at top right, Leggings (7 pieces) at bottom left, and Boots (4 pieces) at bottom right.

The recipe shape stays the same for these five materials. Chainmail Armour cannot be crafted normally, and Netherite Armour is upgraded from Diamond Armour later.

You do not need to craft an Armour piece yet. Mark the quest after looking at all four pictures and choosing one possible material.

Reward: 5 experience points for learning the four recipes.
task.firsttorch.29b7e4c10d836af5.title: I know the four Armour recipes
quest.firsttorch.protection.armour_slots:
Press E to open your inventory. Four vertical armour slots appear beside your character: a Helmet at the top, then a Chestplate, Leggings, and Boots at the bottom.

Armour protects you only while worn in the matching armour slot. Merely carrying it somewhere in your inventory is not enough. Drag a piece onto its matching outline; Shift + left click will often equip it automatically.

The small armour symbols above your hearts show your protection. Armour reduces damage but does not make you invincible. You do not need a complete set of Iron Armour yet—a Shield is a sensible first defence.

Mark the quest when you have found all four armour slots.
task.firsttorch.23b9f1c60d745ae8.title: I found all four armour slots
quest.firsttorch.protection.shield_pract:
Your Shield is already in your offhand. Your regular attack hand can still hold a tool or weapon at the same time.

Close the inventory and hold the right mouse button to raise the Shield. Face toward the danger and raise it early; you move more slowly while blocking.

A raised Shield blocks many attacks and projectiles from the front. It does not protect against attacks from behind, falling, fire, or drowning. An axe strike can disable it briefly.

Mark the quest only after placing the Shield in your offhand and raising it once.
task.firsttorch.34c7e2a90d615bf8.title: I raised the Shield from my offhand
quest.firsttorch.protection.avoid_danger:
There is no requirement to defeat every monster. Especially at the beginning, staying safe matters more than experience points or loot.

Travel during daylight when possible and remember your route home. Do not fight several enemies at once. Close a door, block an entrance, or retreat when your hearts are low.

Zombies and Skeletons usually burn in direct daylight, but can remain dangerous in shade. Spiders and Creepers do not burn. A Creeper can explode during the day too—keep your distance.

Mark the quest when you can deliberately avoid a danger and know a safe place to retreat to.

Reward: One Iron Ingot replaces part of the Iron used for your Shield and helps with your next equipment lesson.
task.firsttorch.45d1a7e80c936bf2.title: I can avoid an unnecessary fight
trophy.firsttorch.mining.title: Safe below ground
trophy.firsttorch.mining.description: You prepared carefully, explored underground safely, and returned home with a clear route.
chapter.firsttorch.mining.title: Safe Underground
chapter.firsttorch.mining.description: Prepare properly, make a safe staircase, mark your route, and return home in time.
image.firsttorch.safe_staircase.descript: A two-block-high staircase shaft with a clear, walkable route back to the surface.
image.firsttorch.torch_route.description: Torches on the right wall while going down appear on the left wall when returning home.
quest.firsttorch.mining.equipment.title: Your Underground Equipment
quest.firsttorch.mining.equipment.descri:
Goal: prepare before travelling farther underground.

Take two Pickaxes made from Stone, Copper, Iron, or a better material. If one Pickaxe breaks, the second can still clear a safe route home.

Also take at least 16 Torches and four cooked foods. Torches keep your route visible; food enables sprinting and helps your body recover lost hearts.

All three tasks complete automatically. The items are not consumed.
task.firsttorch.2b73e9f40d856ac1.title: Hold 2 suitable Pickaxes
task.firsttorch.3c84fa150e967bd2.title: Hold 16 Torches
task.firsttorch.4d950b261fa78ce3.title: Hold 4 cooked foods
quest.firsttorch.mining.staircase.title: Never Dig Straight Down
quest.firsttorch.mining.staircase.descri:
When you break the block directly beneath your feet, you cannot see what is below. You might fall a long way, land in a cave with enemies, or drop directly into lava.

Build a staircase instead: clear one block in front of you, then the block beneath it. Step down and repeat. Remove the block above your head when necessary so the passage remains two blocks tall.

Turn around occasionally. If you can see up the staircase toward the exit and walk back without jumping, your route remains usable.

Mark the quest after building at least five safe steps.
task.firsttorch.3f28dab50e749c16.title: I built at least 5 safe steps
quest.firsttorch.mining.torch_route.desc:
Dark areas can hide enemies and make the route home difficult to recognise. Place a Torch regularly before moving into the next dark area.

Use one consistent side rule: while travelling deeper, place Torches only on the right-hand wall. After turning around, the same Torches appear on your left—that side leads home.

The rule helps only when used consistently. Mark branches with two Torches beside each other, or block a route that you do not want to explore yet.

Mark the quest after placing five route Torches using the same side rule.
task.firsttorch.516afc702096be38.title: I placed 5 route Torches on the same side
quest.firsttorch.mining.falling_blocks.d:
Gravel and Sand do not float like Stone. When the block supporting them is removed, they fall. Several blocks may collapse together.

Never break the bottom of a Gravel pile while standing directly beneath it. A falling block can trap and suffocate you. Move aside, keep an open route behind you, and mine Gravel from above or from a safe distance.

If Gravel falls into your tunnel, step backwards and clear it only after you have room to breathe. Mark the quest when you can recognise loose blocks as different from solid Stone.
task.firsttorch.738c1e9242b8d05a.title: I recognise falling blocks as a danger
quest.firsttorch.mining.water_lava.title: Water and Lava in a Mine
quest.firsttorch.mining.water_lava.descr:
If Water or Lava flows into your tunnel after breaking a block, immediately move several steps back. Water can push or trap you underwater; Lava causes severe damage very quickly and can burn dropped items.

Stay on the safe side of the flow and place a Stone or Dirt block in front of the opening. Do not enter the liquid to search for its source. With Lava, do not stand directly at the edge either.

Listen while mining: flowing Water or bubbling Lava may be behind the next block. Mark the quest when you know that stepping back is always the first action.
task.firsttorch.25be301464daf27c.title: I know the first action for Water or Lava
quest.firsttorch.mining.return_home.desc:
A discovery is useful only when you bring it home safely. Turn back before both Pickaxes nearly break, your Torches run out, or only two meals remain.

Follow the Torches on your left and walk up the staircase. Do not run through unknown dark areas simply because the safe route feels long.

At home, store ores and other important finds in a Chest, replenish food and Torches, and repair or replace your tools. Only then begin the next journey.

Mark the quest after deliberately turning around and returning safely to your shelter at least once.

Reward: 10 experience points for your first safe mining journey.
task.firsttorch.47d0523686fc149e.title: I returned safely from a mining journey
trophy.firsttorch.iron_essentials.title: Iron essentials
trophy.firsttorch.iron_essentials.descri: You prepared an Iron Pickaxe and a renewable Water supply for safer exploration.
chapter.firsttorch.iron_essentials.title: Iron Essentials
chapter.firsttorch.iron_essentials.descr: Craft an Iron Pickaxe and Bucket, then practise safe Water handling.
image.firsttorch.iron_pickaxe.descriptio: Recipe for an Iron Pickaxe: three Iron Ingots across the top and two Sticks in the middle column.
image.firsttorch.bucket.description: Recipe for an empty Bucket: three Iron Ingots arranged in a V.
Two renewable Water-source layouts: a 2 × 2 pool and a 1 × 3 row, with safe collection positions shown.
Goal: hold six Iron Ingots in your inventory at the same time.

You already learned to smelt Raw Iron into Iron Ingots in a Furnace. Repeat that process until you have six Ingots: three for an Iron Pickaxe and three for a Bucket.

The task does not consume the Ingots. Wait for its checkmark before crafting; you can then make both recipes.
task.firsttorch.38bae5f71c946d02.title: Hold 6 Iron Ingots in your inventory at the same time
quest.firsttorch.iron_essentials.pickaxe:
Goal: craft an Iron Pickaxe.

The recipe has the same shape as your earlier Pickaxes; only the material is stronger. This time, use three Iron Ingots instead of Wooden Planks or Cobblestone.

An Iron Pickaxe mines faster and can collect valuable blocks such as Diamond Ore that would drop nothing when mined with a Stone or Copper Pickaxe. For an unfamiliar block, check which tool it needs before breaking it.

Keep using your cheaper Pickaxe for ordinary Stone and save the Iron Pickaxe for valuable ores. Take the Iron Pickaxe from the result slot so the task completes automatically.
task.firsttorch.5adc07193eb68f24.title: Obtain an Iron Pickaxe
Goal: craft an empty Bucket.

Open the Crafting Table. Put one Iron Ingot in the top-left space, one in the top-right space, and the third in the exact centre. The three Ingots form a V. Take the empty Bucket from the result slot.

A Bucket can hold Water, Lava, or Milk, among other things. Begin with Water in a safe place; Lava comes later.
task.firsttorch.7cfe293b50d8a146.title: Obtain an empty Bucket
quest.firsttorch.iron_essentials.water_b:
Goal: fill your Bucket from a Water source block.

Select the empty Bucket in your hotbar. Point the crosshair at a still Water block that is not visibly flowing and press the right mouse button. Only a source block can be collected; flowing Water cannot.

Then practise on a clear, level area: use the Water Bucket on the ground with the right mouse button. The Water begins to spread. Point at the original source block and press the right mouse button again to collect it back into the Bucket.

Do not try this inside your shelter or beside your Chest. Water can push items and flow down through openings.
task.firsttorch.2e104b5d72fac368.title: Obtain a Water Bucket
quest.firsttorch.iron_essentials.infinit:
Goal: build either a 2 × 2 or 1 × 3 Water source and collect Water without breaking it.

Choose a level position with a solid block beneath every Water space. Dig the shape only one block deep. Then collect Water twice from a natural lake or another large source; the setup needs two source blocks.

2 × 2: empty the first Water Bucket into one corner and the second into the diagonally opposite corner. Wait briefly until all four spaces are still. Water can then be collected from any space; the remaining source blocks renew it.

1 × 3: empty one Water Bucket into each outer space. This turns the middle space into a new source block. Collect Water only from the middle — removing either outer source can stop the row from renewing itself.

Orange marks the two positions where Water is poured. In the 1 × 3 version, the white middle space is the safe collection position.

Test the setup: fill the Bucket, wait a moment, and check that the Water surface becomes completely still again. Mark the quest only after collecting Water at least twice in succession without refilling the source.
task.firsttorch.61b53e8f29d7c4a0.title: Infinite Water source built and used successfully twice
quest.firsttorch.iron_essentials.helpers:
You now own an Iron Pickaxe for valuable ores, a Water Bucket, and a reliable Water source. Keep the Water Bucket in an easy-to-reach hotbar slot during mining trips.

Water can extinguish fire, create a safer distance from Lava, and help with a deep descent. This does not mean you should deliberately jump into Lava or practise dangerous falls. Stepping back remains the first safe action.

Mark the checkmark when both items are stored safely or prepared for your next trip.

Reward: 5 experience points for your new Vanilla tools.
task.firsttorch.40326d7f14bce58a.title: My Iron Pickaxe and Water Bucket are ready for the next trip
trophy.firsttorch.finding_home.title: A reliable way home
trophy.firsttorch.finding_home.descripti: You can recognise your home, use its coordinates, and understand a normal Compass.
chapter.firsttorch.finding_home.title: Finding Your Way Home
chapter.firsttorch.finding_home.descript: Mark your home, record its coordinates, and practise a safe return route.
quest.firsttorch.finding_home.landmark.d:
Goal: give your shelter a clear landmark.

A hole in a hillside or a small wooden hut can look like every other place from a distance. Mark the entrance with something that stands out nearby: for example a Lantern, several Torches, a short path, or two different block types.

During daylight, walk about 30 blocks away, turn around, and look for your home. Improve the landmark if you cannot find the entrance quickly.

Do not build a tall tower that forces you to jump down again. A good landmark is safe to reach from the ground.
task.firsttorch.27d9f3b61e84ac05.title: I recognise my home from about 30 blocks away
quest.firsttorch.finding_home.coordinate:
Goal: find the X, Y, and Z coordinates of your location.

Press F3. On some keyboards you must press Fn + F3. A screen of technical information appears. Find the line showing your position; it contains three numbers in X, Y, Z order.

X and Z describe your position across the world. Y is your height. X and Z are usually the most important numbers for finding your way home.

A minus sign is part of the number: X = -80 is a different place from X = 80. Close the information with F3 before walking again so you can see obstacles clearly.

Mark the checkmark when you have found all three numbers at your home.
task.firsttorch.49fb15d830a6ce27.title: I found X, Y, and Z at my home
quest.firsttorch.finding_home.record.des:
Goal: keep your home coordinates somewhere safe.

Stand directly in front of the entrance and record at least X and Z. Include any minus signs. Write the numbers on paper or on your phone, or take a screenshot with F2. Some keyboards require Fn + F2.

Example: Home X = 120, Y = 68, Z = -45. Those are not your numbers—use the values from your own world.

Do not keep the only copy inside a Chest in the world: if you become lost, that is exactly when you cannot reach the Chest.
task.firsttorch.6b1d37fa52c8e049.title: My real home coordinates are recorded outside the world
quest.firsttorch.finding_home.test_route:
Goal: deliberately return home using your landmark and coordinates.

Put valuable items in your Chest. Bring some food and several Torches. During daylight, walk about 50 blocks away from your home and remain in a safe, open area.

Look for your visible landmark first. If it is not enough, open F3 only while standing still and compare X and Z with your note. Move so that each number gets closer to its recorded value. Check only briefly and close F3 before walking again.

Coordinates show where the goal lies, not a safe route. Go around cliffs, deep water, Lava, and dark areas even when that temporarily moves one number in the wrong direction.

Mark the checkmark after you reach your entrance again.

Reward: 5 experience points and two Compasses for your first tested route home. Keep one for the next Compass and Lodestone lessons; the second can be used later for an optional map lesson.
task.firsttorch.0d3f591c74ea026b.title: I returned safely using my landmark and coordinates
quest.firsttorch.finding_home.compass.de:
Goal: understand a normal Compass before relying on it.

The Compass needle points towards world spawn. This is the world's starting area—roughly where you began when you first entered the world.

A Bed sets your personal respawn point, but it does not move world spawn. A normal Compass therefore does not point to your Bed or automatically point to your home.

The Compass can be useful when your home is near world spawn. For a home somewhere else, your visible landmark and recorded coordinates remain more reliable.

The two Compasses from the previous lesson support later Lodestone and map lessons. Mark the checkmark when you can explain where a normal Compass points—and where it does not.
task.firsttorch.40b7e2d96a1c58f3.title: I know the Compass points to world spawn, not to my Bed
trophy.firsttorch.lodestone.title: A fixed way home
trophy.firsttorch.lodestone.description: You made a Lodestone Compass and tested its reliable target at home.
chapter.firsttorch.lodestone.title: Lodestone
chapter.firsttorch.lodestone.description: Craft a Lodestone and bind a Compass to a reliable home target.
image.firsttorch.stonecutter.description: Recipe for a Stonecutter: three Stone along the bottom row and one Iron Ingot directly above the centre.
image.firsttorch.lodestone.description: Recipe for a Lodestone: eight Chiseled Stone Bricks around one Iron Ingot.
quest.firsttorch.lodestone.stonecutter.d:
Goal: craft a Stonecutter.

Smelt Cobblestone in a Furnace to make regular Stone. In the Crafting Table, place three Stone across the bottom row and one Iron Ingot in the centre directly above them.

A Stonecutter turns Stone into selected stairs, slabs, and decorative variants. It does not need fuel.

Wait for the checkmark before placing the Stonecutter near your home with right-click.
task.firsttorch.26f8dab53c917e04.title: Craft a Stonecutter
quest.firsttorch.lodestone.bricks.title: Eight Chiseled Stone Bricks
quest.firsttorch.lodestone.bricks.descri:
Goal: hold eight Chiseled Stone Bricks in your inventory at the same time.

Smelt eight Cobblestone into eight Stone in a Furnace. Then open the placed Stonecutter with right-click.

Put the Stone into the input slot on the left. Select Chiseled Stone Bricks from the displayed list of shapes and take the result from the right. Each Stone makes exactly one Chiseled Stone Bricks block.

Look for the square spiral pattern on the required block. Make eight and keep all of them in your inventory at the same time.
task.firsttorch.48badcf75e139026.title: Hold 8 Chiseled Stone Bricks in your inventory at the same time
quest.firsttorch.lodestone.craft.title: Your Lodestone
quest.firsttorch.lodestone.craft.descrip:
Goal: craft a Lodestone.

Place the eight Chiseled Stone Bricks in every outer slot of the Crafting Table. Put one Iron Ingot in the centre.

The task does not consume the Lodestone. Wait for the checkmark, then take it to your home.
task.firsttorch.6adcf0197035b248.title: Craft a Lodestone
quest.firsttorch.lodestone.bind.title: Bind the Compass to Your Home
quest.firsttorch.lodestone.bind.descript:
Goal: bind your Compass to a Lodestone at your home.

Place the Lodestone directly by your home with right-click. Then hold the normal Compass in your main hand and right-click the Lodestone. This turns it into a Lodestone Compass; that step is detected automatically.

This Compass now points to that exact Lodestone while you are in the same dimension. Your Bed remains your respawn point—the Lodestone is only this Compass's target.

Do not break the Lodestone after binding the Compass. Without its target block, the needle can no longer guide you home reliably.

Test it during daylight: walk about 30 blocks away, watch the needle, and return safely to the Lodestone. Then mark the checkmark.

Reward: 5 experience points for your first personal home-finding Compass.
task.firsttorch.3e1045dab479f68c.title: Bind a Compass to your Lodestone
task.firsttorch.1cfe123b9257d46a.title: My Lodestone Compass guided me safely home
trophy.firsttorch.maps.title: A map for the neighbourhood
trophy.firsttorch.maps.description: You created a local map and learned how a Cartography Table can expand it.
chapter.firsttorch.maps.title: Maps (Optional)
chapter.firsttorch.maps.description: Create a local map and learn how to expand, copy, or preserve it.
image.firsttorch.map_recipe.description: Recipe for an Empty Map: eight Paper around one Compass.
image.firsttorch.cartography_table_guide: Cartography Table combinations for expanding, copying, and locking a Filled Map.
quest.firsttorch.maps.create.title: Create Your First Local Map
quest.firsttorch.maps.create.description:
Goal: craft an Empty Map and open it at your home.

This side lesson is optional. Use the second Compass from the route-home reward and keep the other for the Compass and Lodestone lessons.

Place three Sugar Cane horizontally in one row of the Crafting Table. They make three Paper. The Map and Cartography Table need ten Paper altogether—four batches using three Sugar Cane each provide twelve.

Next, place eight Paper around one Compass. Take the Empty Map from the result slot.

Stand outside at your home and use the Empty Map with right-click. Only then does it become a Filled Map with a fixed mapped area. North is at the top, east on the right, south at the bottom, and west on the left. Your bright player marker shows your position and facing direction.

The automatic task observes that you hold a Filled Map; it cannot tell where you opened it. Hold the Map while exploring so new areas are drawn. Outside its covered area, the marker remains at an edge or becomes a small dot. A Map also does not know a safe route around mountains, water, or caves. Keep your coordinate note.
task.firsttorch.54a93af6c72b8d1e.title: Opened an Empty Map at my home
quest.firsttorch.maps.cartography.title: Use a Cartography Table
quest.firsttorch.maps.cartography.descri:
Goal: craft a Cartography Table and expand the area of your first Map once.

Place two Paper beside each other in the top row of the Crafting Table. Fill the two spaces directly below and the two spaces in the bottom row with any Wooden Planks. The result is a Cartography Table.

The automatic task observes that you hold a Cartography Table; it cannot tell whether you crafted it. Right-click the placed Cartography Table. Put your Filled Map on the left and one Paper in the second slot. A zoomed-out Map appears on the right; after taking it, the Map covers a larger area but shows less detail. A Map can be expanded no more than four times.

The other two combinations in the image are for later: Filled Map plus Empty Map creates an identical copy. Filled Map plus Glass Pane locks its current state; a locked Map does not record later changes to the world. Locking cannot be reversed.

Take the once-expanded Map and then set the checkmark. Check outside how much of the surroundings it now covers and store it safely afterwards.
task.firsttorch.76cb5c18e94daf30.title: Crafted a Cartography Table
task.firsttorch.07dc6d29fa5eb041.title: Expanded and checked my home Map once
trophy.firsttorch.farming.title: A renewable meal
trophy.firsttorch.farming.description: You planted Wheat, harvested it, and baked your first home-grown Bread.
chapter.firsttorch.farming.title: Your First Wheat Field
chapter.firsttorch.farming.description: Grow Wheat beside your home and turn it into renewable Bread.
image.firsttorch.stone_hoe.description: Recipe for a Stone Hoe: two Cobblestone across the top and two Sticks below the right-hand block.
image.firsttorch.farmland_9x9.descriptio: One central Water block hydrates a 9 × 9 field at the same height.
image.firsttorch.bread.description: Recipe for Bread: three Wheat side by side in one horizontal row.
quest.firsttorch.farming.seeds.title: Your First Wheat Seeds
quest.firsttorch.farming.seeds.descripti:
Goal: hold three Wheat Seeds in your inventory at the same time.

During daylight, look for short tufts of grass growing on Dirt or Grass Blocks. Aim the crosshair at the grass tuft and attack it with the left mouse button. Break the small plant, not the ground block underneath it.

Wheat Seeds do not drop from every grass tuft. This is normal: keep moving and break more tufts until you collect three Seeds. Walking over dropped Seeds picks them up automatically.

Keep all three Seeds. Next you will prepare a place where they can grow into a renewable supply of Wheat.
task.firsttorch.1d53f9b62e84ac07.title: Hold 3 Wheat Seeds in your inventory at the same time
quest.firsttorch.farming.hoe.title: A Hoe for the Field
quest.firsttorch.farming.hoe.description:
Goal: craft a Stone Hoe.

Place two Cobblestone beside each other at the top of the Crafting Table. Place two Sticks vertically below the right-hand Cobblestone.

A Hoe is meant for preparing Farmland. A Pickaxe and Axe remain the appropriate tools for breaking Stone and wood.
task.firsttorch.3f751bd840a6ce29.title: Craft a Stone Hoe
quest.firsttorch.farming.farmland.title: Water and Farmland
quest.firsttorch.farming.farmland.descri:
Goal: prepare at least three watered Farmland blocks.

Choose a bright, level area near your home. If you already have a Water Bucket, dig a one-block hole and leave still Water in it. If you do not have one yet, begin beside a natural still Water source instead.

Hold the Stone Hoe and right-click three Dirt or Grass Blocks directly beside the Water. Their tops become flat and ridged: this is Farmland. Near Water it soon becomes darker and remains Farmland.

One Water block hydrates Farmland at the same height up to four blocks away in every horizontal direction—including diagonally. Water in the centre covers a 9 × 9 area. The three blocks beside Water are enough to begin; later you can expand without more Water.

Do not jump on Farmland or place a block on it. Either action can turn it back into ordinary Dirt. Mark the checkmark once Water and at least three Farmland blocks are ready.
task.firsttorch.51973dfa62c8e04b.title: Water and at least 3 Farmland blocks are ready
quest.firsttorch.farming.plant.title: Plant Your First Wheat
quest.firsttorch.farming.plant.descripti:
Goal: plant at least one Wheat Seed.

Hold the Wheat Seeds in your main hand. Aim at an empty Farmland block and right-click. A very small green plant appears. Planting it is detected automatically.

Plant the remaining Seeds on empty Farmland blocks too. Each block can hold only one plant. If nothing can be planted, prepare the Dirt or Grass Block with the Hoe first.

Reward: Three Bone Meal help you carefully speed up growth. Right-click young Wheat with Bone Meal; green particles show it worked. One use does not always make Wheat ripe. You can also craft Bone Meal from a Bone, or use the future optional Composter and Safe Mob Drops lessons.
task.firsttorch.73b95f1c84ea026d.title: Plant a Wheat Seed on Farmland
quest.firsttorch.farming.wheat.title: Wait for Ripe Wheat
quest.firsttorch.farming.wheat.descripti:
Goal: harvest and hold three Wheat in your inventory at the same time.

Wheat grows through several stages and needs time and enough light. Young Wheat is small and green; ripe Wheat is tall and mostly golden. Attack only ripe Wheat with the left mouse button; it drops Wheat and new Seeds.

After harvesting, plant a Seed on the empty Farmland again. This turns the one-time discovery into a renewable food source.
task.firsttorch.15db713ea60c248f.title: Hold 3 harvested Wheat in your inventory at the same time
quest.firsttorch.farming.bread.title: Your First Home-Grown Bread
quest.firsttorch.farming.bread.descripti:
Goal: craft Bread from your Wheat.

Place three Wheat side by side in one horizontal row of the Crafting Table and take the Bread from the result slot.

Do not use your final Wheat Seed. Replant after every harvest and keep several spare Seeds in a Chest. Then accidentally damaging the field cannot end your farm completely.

Reward: 5 experience points for your first renewable food.
task.firsttorch.37fd9350c82e46a1.title: Craft Bread from Wheat you harvested
trophy.firsttorch.composting.title: Peaceful Bone Meal
trophy.firsttorch.composting.description: You made a Composter and turned plant leftovers into Bone Meal.
chapter.firsttorch.composting.title: Composting (Optional)
chapter.firsttorch.composting.descriptio: Turn plant leftovers into renewable Bone Meal without combat.
quest.firsttorch.composting.slabs.title: Side Path: Wooden Slabs for a Composter
quest.firsttorch.composting.slabs.descri:
Optional goal: hold seven wooden Slabs of any kind in your inventory at the same time.

A Composter needs seven wooden Slabs. Place three matching Wooden Planks next to each other in one horizontal row of the crafting grid. This makes six Slabs.

Repeat the recipe once. You will then have twelve Slabs, enough for the Composter. Wood types may be mixed for this task and in the Composter recipe.

This side path is optional and does not block your Wheat, animal-care, or storage paths.
task.firsttorch.2bd17c3fa648e509.title: Hold 7 wooden Slabs of any kind in your inventory at the same time
quest.firsttorch.composting.composter.de:
Goal: craft one Composter and hold it in your inventory.

Place three wooden Slabs in both the left and right columns of the Crafting Table. Put the seventh Slab in the bottom-centre slot. Leave the other two slots of the centre column empty.

The recipe looks like a U: both sides are completely filled and joined by the Slab at the bottom centre.

Reward: 32 Wheat Seeds let you test the Composter without harvesting your young field. Because each filling attempt is random, add other suitable plant leftovers if needed.
task.firsttorch.4df39e51c86a072b.title: Hold 1 Composter in your inventory
quest.firsttorch.composting.bonemeal.des:
Goal: fill the Composter and take one Bone Meal from it.

Place the Composter and hold a suitable plant item in your main hand, such as Wheat Seeds. Right-click the Composter. Green particles and a higher layer inside show a successful filling step.

Not every item raises the fill level. This is normal. Use more suitable plant leftovers until the Composter is full and a pale layer appears on top.

Right-click the full Composter again to take out one Bone Meal. The Composter is then empty and can be used repeatedly.

Mark the checkmark only after you have taken Bone Meal from the Composter yourself.

Reward: 5 experience points for your first peaceful Bone Meal production.
task.firsttorch.6f15b073ea8c294d.title: Collected Bone Meal from a full Composter yourself
trophy.firsttorch.animal_care.title: Your first animals
trophy.firsttorch.animal_care.descriptio: You built a safe pen and established a renewable breeding pair.
chapter.firsttorch.animal_care.title: Your First Animals
chapter.firsttorch.animal_care.descripti: Build a safe pen, lead animals home, and start a renewable herd.
quest.firsttorch.animals.parts.title: Parts for a Safe Pen
quest.firsttorch.animals.parts.descripti:
Goal: hold 15 wooden Fences and one Fence Gate in your inventory at the same time.

Animals can wander away while you are still building. Finish the entire pen before you lure an animal with food.

To make three Fences, place Planks, Stick, Planks in each of two rows. For a Fence Gate, swap the materials: Stick, Planks, Stick. Use one wood type within each recipe.

Five Fence recipes make 15 Fences. Together with one Gate, that is enough for the edge of a 5 × 5 block starter pen.
task.firsttorch.285ce3b719f46da2.title: Hold 15 wooden Fences in your inventory at the same time
task.firsttorch.396df4c82a057eb3.title: Hold 1 Fence Gate in your inventory
quest.firsttorch.animals.pen.title: Build the Pen
quest.firsttorch.animals.pen.description:
Goal: build a completely enclosed pen with a Gate beside your home.

Choose a bright, mostly level place. Build a closed Fence edge about 5 × 5 blocks across and replace one Fence with the Fence Gate. The inside is then 3 × 3 blocks, enough at first for two adults and their baby.

Right-click the Gate to open and close it. Check the whole edge: there must be no gap between Fence pieces and no raised block directly beside them that lets an animal walk out over the Fence.

Mark the checkmark only when you can stand inside, close the Gate behind you, and cannot walk out anywhere.

Reward: Four Torches so you can light the pen and its surroundings well.
task.firsttorch.5b8f16ea4c2790d5.title: The pen is completely enclosed and the Gate works
quest.firsttorch.animals.feed.title: Choose an Animal and Its Food
quest.firsttorch.animals.feed.descriptio:
Goal: find two matching adult farm animals and prepare at least two pieces of the right food.

Cows and Sheep follow Wheat. Chickens follow Wheat Seeds and other Seeds. Pigs follow Carrots, Potatoes, or Beetroot. For the easiest start, find Cows or Sheep and use Wheat from your farm—or find Chickens and use Wheat Seeds.

The task can only detect that you carry two possible food items. You must make sure both match your chosen animal. Find two animals of the same kind so they can have a baby later.

Do not feed the animals yet. Keep the food ready; you will use it to lure them in the next step.
task.firsttorch.7da1380c6e49b2f7.title: Prepare 2 matching food items for one animal kind
quest.firsttorch.animals.lure.title: Lure Two Animals into the Pen
quest.firsttorch.animals.lure.descriptio:
Goal: bring two matching adult animals into your pen and close the Gate.

Hold the correct food in your main hand and move near the first animal. While it can see the food, it looks at you and follows. Do not right-click the animal yet or you will feed it too early.

Walk slowly to the pen and check regularly that the animal still follows. Open the Gate, lead it inside, and close the Gate once you are both in. Leave through the Gate, then repeat the journey with a second adult of the same kind.

If an animal stops following, move closer and show it the food again. Do not run far ahead or switch to another item.

Mark the checkmark when both animals are inside and the Gate is closed.
task.firsttorch.1fc35a2e806bd419.title: 2 matching adult animals are inside the closed pen
quest.firsttorch.animals.breed.title: The First Baby Animal
quest.firsttorch.animals.breed.descripti:
Goal: breed your first animals. The new baby is detected automatically.

Enter the pen and close the Gate behind you. Hold the correct food in your main hand. Right-click the first adult once, then the second. This consumes one food item for each animal.

Hearts appear above both animals. When they are close enough, they move together and a small baby appears. The parents cannot breed again immediately; give them some time.

If no hearts appear, check the animal kind and food first. Babies cannot have babies of their own yet.
task.firsttorch.31e57c40a28df63b.title: Breed two animals and produce a baby
quest.firsttorch.animals.care.title: Protect Your Breeding Animals
quest.firsttorch.animals.care.descriptio:
Goal: establish a safe routine for food, space, and your breeding pair.

Always keep at least two adults of the same kind alive. They are your breeding pair and make the herd renewable. If you kill the final pair, you must find and lead new animals home again.

Keep matching food in a Chest as a reserve. Expand the pen before it becomes crowded, and close the Gate after every visit. Babies grow into adults by themselves over time.

Cows can provide Milk, Sheep can provide renewable Wool, and Chickens lay Eggs—not every useful resource requires killing an animal.

Mark the checkmark when at least two adults remain safe, the Gate is closed, and food has been stored for later.

Reward: 5 experience points and one Lead for your first renewable animal population.
task.firsttorch.53079e62c4af185d.title: Breeding pair, closed pen, and food reserve are secure
image.firsttorch.fence_and_gate.descript: Crafting recipes for a wooden Fence and Fence Gate.
chapter.firsttorch.storage.title: Storage and Organisation
chapter.firsttorch.storage.description: Give supplies permanent places and prepare for your next trip.
trophy.firsttorch.storage.title: Everything in Its Place
trophy.firsttorch.storage.description: You labelled and sorted your storage and established a return-home routine.
quest.firsttorch.storage.chests.title: Three Chests, Three Jobs
quest.firsttorch.storage.chests.descript:
Goal: hold three Chests in your inventory at the same time.

You already know the Chest recipe: eight Wooden Planks fill the outside of the 3 × 3 grid and the centre remains empty. Make more Chests until you can carry three together.

Do not place them before the task completes. The automatic check only counts Chests that are currently in your inventory.

Each separate Chest will receive one job in the next step. Later, you will know where an item belongs before opening anything.
task.firsttorch.762ac195f73d4b8e.title: Hold 3 Chests in your inventory at the same time
quest.firsttorch.storage.areas.title: Build Three Storage Areas
quest.firsttorch.storage.areas.descripti:
Goal: place three separate, easy-to-reach Chests at your home.

Give each Chest one job: one for blocks and building materials, one for food and farming supplies, and one for tools, armour, and valuable finds.

Leave at least one block between the Chests for now, or place them against different walls. Two Chests placed directly beside each other can join into a Large Chest with 54 spaces. That is useful later, but would mix your three categories now.

Leave enough space above every Chest for its lid to open. Open all three once and check that no block or item prevents a lid from moving.

Mark the checkmark when all three Chests remain separate and can be opened.

Reward: Three Item Frames. Later, you can also display one typical item for each category.
task.firsttorch.184ce3b7195f6da0.title: 3 separate and accessible Chests have been placed
quest.firsttorch.storage.signs.title: Signs for Clear Names
quest.firsttorch.storage.signs.descripti:
Goal: hold three wooden Signs of any wood types in your inventory at the same time.

Place six matching Wooden Planks in the top two rows of the Crafting Table. Put one Stick in the centre of the bottom row. The recipe makes three Signs—exactly one for each storage area.

Signs do not change what a Chest can hold. They simply give you a visible reminder of the organisation system you chose.
task.firsttorch.3a6e05d93b718fc2.title: Hold 3 wooden Signs in your inventory at the same time
quest.firsttorch.storage.sort.title: Label and Sort
quest.firsttorch.storage.sort.descriptio:
Goal: label the three storage areas and sort your supplies into them.

Place one Sign on a free block directly in front of or beside each matching Chest. A text box opens when you place it. Useful short names are 'Building', 'Food and Farm', and 'Equipment'.

Then open a Chest and move matching stacks into it. Shift + left-click quickly moves a stack between your inventory and the open Chest.

Some things could fit more than one category. That is not a mistake: choose one permanent place that you can remember. Organisation should shorten searches, not create new confusion.

Mark the checkmark when all three areas are labelled and every Chest contains at least one matching item.
task.firsttorch.5c8027fb5d93a1e4.title: All 3 storage areas are labelled and contain matching items
quest.firsttorch.storage.routine.title: Your Return-Home Routine
quest.firsttorch.storage.routine.descrip:
Goal: tidy your inventory and prepare your important supplies for the next trip.

Put collected blocks, farming supplies, and valuable finds into their labelled Chests. Keep your current tools, some cooked food, and Torches with you. Refill supplies you used from the Chests.

Leave several inventory spaces empty. This lets you collect new items while travelling and makes it easier to see what you just found.

Before leaving, check: suitable tools, food, Torches, and empty spaces. Mark the checkmark when your inventory is ready and every Chest is closed again.

Reward: 5 experience points and one Bundle for your first dependable organisation system. A Bundle lets you carry several small stacks in less inventory space.
task.firsttorch.7ea2491d7fb5c306.title: Inventory tidied, supplies refilled, and Chests closed
chapter.firsttorch.excursions.title: Excursions and Boats (Optional)
chapter.firsttorch.excursions.descriptio: Plan a safe day trip and practise travelling near shore.
trophy.firsttorch.excursions.title: Back at the Starting Shore
trophy.firsttorch.excursions.description: You planned a short boat trip and returned safely.
image.firsttorch.boat_controls.descripti: Boat controls at a safe shore.
quest.firsttorch.excursions.plan.title: What to Do in the Overworld?
quest.firsttorch.excursions.plan.descrip:
Goal: begin a planned Overworld excursion.

You already know how to mark your home, record coordinates, and protect yourself. You will now combine those skills into a safe exploration routine. Later, this routine will help you find Villages and meet their inhabitants.

This path is an additional Overworld lesson. It does not block the Nether, Stronghold, or End. Follow it at your own pace.

Exploring is not the same as walking onward without a plan. Establish a return route before departure, check supplies along the way, and turn around while returning is still easy.

Set the checkmark after understanding that difference and deciding to prepare a short daytime excursion first.
task.firsttorch.23f9b6d85041ace7.title: I plan the outward and return routes together
quest.firsttorch.excursions.equipment.de:
Goal: assemble safe basic equipment for an Overworld excursion.

Sleep in your Bed at home at least once and leave it there. Check the home coordinates recorded outside the world and your Lodestone Compass. A Compass still does not replace a safe route around cliffs or Water.

Bring a Pickaxe for stone, an Axe for wood, and a Shovel for soft ground. Wear at least Iron or better Armour, put the Shield in your offhand, and carry eight cooked foods.

Also pack 16 Torches and 32 Cobblestone. Cobblestone is a visible marker, short safe step, or emergency wall—not an invitation to bridge risky ravines.

Leave at least eight inventory slots empty. Store ores, rare loot, and anything else you do not need in a Chest at home. One death should not risk your entire collection as well.

Set the checkmark when the Bed and route home are checked, all three suitable tools are packed, and at least eight slots are free. The four item tasks complete automatically.
task.firsttorch.451bd8fa7263ce09.title: Hold 1 Shield in the inventory
task.firsttorch.562ce90b8374df1a.title: Hold 8 cooked foods in the inventory at the same time
task.firsttorch.673dfa1c9485e02b.title: Hold 16 Torches in the inventory at the same time
task.firsttorch.704e0b2da596f13c.title: Hold 32 Cobblestone in the inventory at the same time
task.firsttorch.05af1c3eb6a7024d.title: Bed, route home, tools, and empty slots are checked
quest.firsttorch.excursions.daylight.des:
Goal: leave home in good daylight while keeping the return in mind.

Sleep until morning or wait safely for the Sun to rise. Do not begin at dusk. A thunderstorm can make daytime dark and dangerous as well, so postpone this first practice excursion when one occurs.

Turn around after short sections and look at the return route. Notice distinctive hills, groups of trees, shore shapes, or your own sparse Cobblestone markers. Record intermediate coordinates when making a major change of direction if needed.

Turn back before the Sun is low or before food, Torches, or empty inventory slots run short. An early return is good planning, not a failed excursion.

Remain within sight of home for this step. Set the checkmark after walking one short safe section and returning to the entrance.
task.firsttorch.27c13e50d8c9246f.title: Walked a short daytime section and returned safely
quest.firsttorch.excursions.boat.title: Craft a Boat
quest.firsttorch.excursions.boat.descrip:
Goal: craft a Boat or Bamboo Raft.

Open the Crafting Table. Leave the top row empty. Put one Wooden Plank in the left and right slots of the middle row, then fill the entire bottom row with three more Planks of the same wood type. The shape resembles a U.

Boats made from Oak, Spruce, Birch, Jungle, Acacia, Dark Oak, Mangrove, Cherry, or Pale Oak count. Bamboo Planks make a Bamboo Raft in the same shape, which also counts.

A Boat is fast and useful on Water but moves only very slowly on land. Take it only to a safe, accessible shore near home for now.
task.firsttorch.49e35072faeb4681.title: Own an ordinary Boat or Bamboo Raft
quest.firsttorch.excursions.controls.des:
Goal: practise every important Boat control at a safe shore.

Hold the Boat in your main hand and right-click calm Water to place it. Right-click the placed Boat again to board it. W moves forward, A and D steer left and right, and S moves backward.

Do not enter waterfalls, Lava, unknown deep caves, or an ocean. Practise parallel to a safe shore first so you can reach land at any time.

Press Shift to leave the Boat. Dismount only at a flat, safe place; the game places you beside the Boat. An empty Boat can drift away on Water.

Attack the empty Boat with the left mouse button until it drops as an item, then collect it again. Set the checkmark only after placing, boarding, steering, leaving, and retrieving the Boat.
task.firsttorch.6b0572941c0d68a3.title: Tried every Boat control and collected the Boat again
quest.firsttorch.excursions.return.title: Return to the Same Shore
quest.firsttorch.excursions.return.descr:
Goal: travel one short known route and return with the Boat.

Mark a flat boarding place near home and check its coordinates. Travel about 100 blocks parallel to the known shore in daylight. Do not cross a large open ocean for this exercise.

Turn around before the shore becomes confusing. Return to the marker, leave safely, and collect the Boat again. Briefly check the inventory and route home afterwards.

Set the checkmark at the original shore with the Boat back in your inventory.

Reward: 5 experience points for a complete outward-and-return journey. In the next section, the same routine will be used to deliberately search for a Village.
task.firsttorch.0d2794b63e2f8ac5.title: Returned to the marked starting shore with the Boat
chapter.firsttorch.village.title: Discover a Village (Optional)
chapter.firsttorch.village.description: Find a Village with a safe return route and meet its inhabitants respectfully.
trophy.firsttorch.village.title: A Good Guest
trophy.firsttorch.village.description: You explored a Village, recorded its location and learned how to visit safely.
quest.firsttorch.village.search.title: Search for a Village with a Return Route
quest.firsttorch.village.search.descript:
Goal: discover a Village without abandoning the route home.

Villages generate only in suitable areas and not at regular distances. Finding none on the first short excursion is normal. Never continue until darkness or empty supplies force the return.

Choose one direction, record it beside the home coordinates, and explore in daylight. Follow visible terrain lines such as a shore or broad valley. A Boat can speed up rivers and coasts; use safe open routes on land.

Turn around regularly and inspect how the return route looks from that direction. Record intermediate coordinates at every major turn. Do not depend on individual Torches that may disappear among trees or hills.
