image.firsttorch.stronghold_iron_door.de: Left: one Stone makes one Stone Button. Right: the orange-marked Button beside the Iron Door opens it briefly.
image.firsttorch.stronghold_silverfish.d: Infested Stone Bricks can look like ordinary, Mossy or Cracked Stone Bricks. Breaking them can release a Silverfish.
image.firsttorch.end_portal_room.descrip: Top-down orientation: twelve Portal Frames surround the centre with Lava. The Silverfish Spawner is marked in orange.
image.firsttorch.end_portal_frame_states: An empty Portal Frame on the left and a frame with an inserted Eye on the right. Existing and missing Eyes must add up to twelve.
image.firsttorch.bow_and_arrows.descript: Left: the Bow recipe uses three Sticks and three Strings. Right: Flint, a Stick and a Feather make four Arrows.
image.firsttorch.end_portal_final_eye.de: The final empty frame and an outside standing position are marked in orange. Insert the final Eye from safe ground without entering the portal surface.
quest.firsttorch.interior.plan.title: Enter the Stronghold with a Plan
quest.firsttorch.interior.plan.descripti:
Goal: prepare a limited exploration with a clear stopping point.

Return through the marked surface entrance and lit staircase to the closable retreat room. Bring full Iron Armour or better, a Shield, an Iron Sword and Iron Pickaxe or better tools, a Water Bucket, 32 Torches, 32 Cobblestone, and 16 filling cooked foods.

Leave every Eye of Ender safely at home or in a clearly separate Chest at the entrance. This trip only finds and secures the portal room, preventing an accidental right-click from activating the portal.

Choose a firm return limit: turn back before less than half the food or Torches remain, the Pickaxe is close to breaking, or the safe route home becomes uncertain.

Set the checkmark when equipment, the Eye-free inventory, and the stopping rule are checked.
task.firsttorch.197e4a06d1b58f3c.title: Equipment, separated Eyes, and stopping rule checked
quest.firsttorch.interior.routes.title: Mark Every Outward Route
quest.firsttorch.interior.routes.descrip:
Goal: explore only routes that can be followed clearly back to the entrance.

While moving forward, place Torches consistently on the right-hand wall. Those Torches will be on the left while returning. Light every junction and add a Cobblestone marker or Sign there that points towards the secured entrance.

The rule helps but is not magic: Stronghold corridors can form loops, stairs cross several heights, and some doors reconnect known paths. Also record the coordinates and depth of important junctions.

Open only one new route at a junction. Return to the final safe marker before checking a second. Temporarily close checked dark dead ends with conspicuous Cobblestone.

Set the checkmark after the first short corridor is lit, marked, and followed backwards to the retreat room.
task.firsttorch.3b906c28f3d7a15e.title: First Stronghold route marked and return checked
quest.firsttorch.interior.doors.title: Open Iron Doors with a Button
quest.firsttorch.interior.doors.descript:
Goal: understand Iron Doors and carry two Stone Buttons to protect the return route.

A Wooden Door opens directly with right-click. An Iron Door does not respond that way: it needs a Redstone signal. Stronghold corridors often provide a small Stone Button on a neighbouring block for this purpose.

Right-click the Stone Button. The Iron Door opens only briefly and then closes automatically. Stand in the correct position before pressing, check the visible floor beyond the Door, and move through promptly without stopping in the doorway.

Immediately check whether a Button or another control is reachable on the other side. If not, place your own Stone Button on a solid block directly beside the Door. Do not enter another room until the return route can be opened from your side.

One Stone Button is crafted shapelessly from one ordinary Stone. Smelt Cobblestone in a Furnace first; one Stone makes one Button. Hold two Buttons at the same time so both sides can be made safe when a control is missing or removed.

The automatic task completes when two Stone Buttons are in your inventory at the same time.
task.firsttorch.4da17e3904e8b26f.title: Hold 2 Stone Buttons in your inventory at once
quest.firsttorch.interior.silverfish.des:
Goal: understand both hazards before opening more walls.

Dark Stronghold corridors can contain ordinary enemies such as Zombies, Skeletons, and Creepers. Light from a protected position, open doors from the side behind the Shield, and never run blindly into a new room.

Infested forms of Stone, Stone Bricks, Mossy Stone Bricks, and Cracked Stone Bricks can look like ordinary blocks. Breaking one releases a Silverfish. If a Silverfish is hurt without being defeated quickly, it can awaken more nearby infested blocks.

Do not mine whole Stronghold walls unnecessarily. If a Silverfish appears, retreat to the last narrow, lit passage, close the route with Cobblestone, and fight it alone with fully charged strikes. When several appear, retreat instead of chasing them.

Set the checkmark when darkness, ordinary enemies, and infested blocks are understood as separate hazards.
task.firsttorch.5db28e4a15f9c370.title: Stronghold hazards and safe retreat understood
quest.firsttorch.interior.library.title: Libraries Are Optional
quest.firsttorch.interior.library.descri:
Goal: decide whether to inspect a found Stronghold Library now or leave it marked for later.

Strongholds can contain Libraries with Bookshelves, Cobwebs, and Chests, but intersecting generation may also leave a Stronghold without one. A Library is not needed to find or activate the End Portal and never gates the main path.

Remain at the entrance, light visible areas, and check upper levels for enemies before entering. Bookshelves and wood burn: use neither Flint and Steel nor Lava here. Random Chest contents never justify an unsafe jump or fight.

Set the checkmark after deliberately skipping the Library or safely marking and leaving a room that was found. You do not need to find one.
task.firsttorch.7fd4a06c371be592.title: Library deliberately skipped or safely checked
quest.firsttorch.portal.find.title: Find the Portal Room
quest.firsttorch.portal.find.description:
Goal: reach the End Portal room entrance without rushing inside.

Explore the marked corridors one step at a time. The portal room is recognised by a raised arrangement of twelve greenish End Portal Frames around a square centre. The room also contains Lava and a Silverfish Spawner.

The original capture shows a portal room with Eyes still missing and the Silverfish Spawner still present. Doors and damaged walls may differ in your room; the twelve frames, Spawner, and portal centre are the important features.

Remain outside the room at first, behind an opening that can be blocked. Set the checkmark once the frames, Lava, and Spawner have been recognised from safety.
task.firsttorch.21f6c28e593d07b4.title: Portal room found and recognised from the safe entrance
quest.firsttorch.portal.secure.title: Secure the Portal Room
quest.firsttorch.portal.secure.descripti:
Goal: remove the immediate hazards before approaching the frames.

First build a small lit retreat room outside with a closable passage. Lure existing enemies there one at a time. Enter the portal room only when a solid wall can be reached immediately in danger.

Destroy the Silverfish Spawner with the Pickaxe as soon as the route is clear. A Spawner cannot be collected as a block in normal Survival mode; removing this one safely matters more. Retreat immediately if Silverfish appear.

Light the room and temporarily cover reachable open Lava from solid ground with Cobblestone. Never stand on Portal Frames or beside an unsecured Lava edge. Do not alter the twelve frames and continue to insert no Eyes; the later activation lesson explains which temporary cover must be removed again.

Set the checkmark when the retreat room, Spawner, lighting, and reachable Lava edges are controlled.
task.firsttorch.4318e4a07b5f29d6.title: Portal room secured but not activated
quest.firsttorch.portal.count.title: Count the Empty Frames
quest.firsttorch.portal.count.descriptio:
Goal: record how many of the twelve Portal Frames do not yet contain an Eye of Ender.

Walk slowly around the safe outside of the frame. An empty frame shows only its flat greenish top; a filled frame has a clearly raised Eye of Ender on it.

Count all twelve positions and separately record existing Eyes and empty frames. The two numbers must add up to twelve. Continue to hold no Eyes and right-click no frame.

Set the checkmark only after the number of required Eyes is written down. Inserting them follows the End expedition preparation.
task.firsttorch.653a06c29d714bf8.title: All 12 frames checked and missing Eye count recorded
quest.firsttorch.portal.return.title: Return Home with the Result
quest.firsttorch.portal.return.descripti:
Goal: leave the Stronghold by the marked route and prepare the later End journey at home.

Follow the markers backwards to the secured Stronghold entrance and climb to the surface. Check the coordinates again there, then return to base. Replace missing route lighting only from safe positions.

Store the Eyes of Ender together with the recorded empty-frame count. The portal remains inactive. Activation still needs a separate equipment check, an explanation of the first jump's one-way danger, and a plan for arriving in the End.

Set the checkmark when you are home, the route remained traceable, and the frame note lies beside the Eyes.

Reward: one Golden Apple is an emergency reserve for the later journey; ten experience points recognise the controlled Stronghold exploration.
task.firsttorch.075c28e4bf936d1a.title: Safely home with frame note and Eyes stored together
quest.firsttorch.end_prep.jump.title: Understand the First Jump
quest.firsttorch.end_prep.jump.descripti:
Goal: understand the consequences before the portal is even activated.

The first jump takes you to the End's main island. The portal behind you is not an ordinary return route there: the safe way home opens only after defeating the Ender Dragon. The other immediate exit is death, which drops carried items unless the keep inventory game rule is enabled.

The End consists of islands above the Void. Falling into the Void destroys you and every dropped item; Water cannot save you from the Void. Beds explode in the End as they do in the Nether. Water from a Bucket can be placed there and may help against falls or Endermen.

Endermen still attack only after you look directly at them or attack them. A Carved Pumpkin on the head prevents provocation by looking, but severely restricts vision and does not replace careful aim.

Set the checkmark only after understanding that entry is a prepared boss expedition, not a short scouting trip.
task.firsttorch.1a9f5b17e2c6904e.title: One-way danger, Void, Beds, and Water understood
quest.firsttorch.end_prep.bow.title: Bow and Arrows for the Crystals
quest.firsttorch.end_prep.bow.descriptio:
Goal: hold one Bow and 32 Arrows in the inventory at the same time.

A Bow is crafted from three Sticks and three Strings. String comes from sources including Spiders and Cobwebs. Hold right-click to shoot until the Bow is fully drawn, aim, and then release. A barely drawn shot travels only weakly and briefly.

Four Arrows are crafted from one Flint at the top, one Stick in the middle, and one Feather at the bottom. Flint is already familiar from Gravel; Chickens commonly drop Feathers.

The Bow will later be used mainly for the End Crystals that heal the Dragon. Do not waste the Arrows before then. If the Bow has Infinity, one ordinary Arrow in the inventory is enough to shoot; the first predictable attempt still prepares a normal reserve.

Reward: another 32 Arrows add to the 32 prepared personally for a reserve of 64; five experience points recognise the preparation.
task.firsttorch.3cb17d3904e8b270.title: Hold one Bow in the inventory
task.firsttorch.4dc28e4a15f9c381.title: Hold 32 Arrows in the inventory at once
quest.firsttorch.end_prep.pack.title: Pack for the End
quest.firsttorch.end_prep.pack.descripti:
Goal: prepare the complete minimum equipment and check its condition.

Hold these at the same time: an Iron Sword and Iron Pickaxe or something better for each, a Shield, Water Bucket, 64 Cobblestone, 16 filling cooked foods, and the prepared Bow and Arrows. Bring only additional items whose loss would be acceptable.

Wear full Iron Armour or better. Enchanted Diamond Armour is considerably safer but is not an automatic task, avoiding a long forced Diamond grind. Repair badly damaged equipment before leaving. Protection and Feather Falling are especially helpful; a Shield stops neither the Dragon's movement nor a fall into the Void.

The Water Bucket can break a fall onto solid ground and keep Endermen away. Cobblestone provides cover and safe paths. Neither helps after falling into the Void, so never fight directly beside an unsecured edge.

Set the additional checkmark after also checking Armour, durability, Bow, and Arrow reserve.
task.firsttorch.0166c28e593d07c5.title: Hold an Iron Sword or a better Sword
task.firsttorch.1277d39f6a4e18d6.title: Hold an Iron Pickaxe or a better Pickaxe
task.firsttorch.2388e4a07b5f29e7.title: Hold one Shield in the inventory
task.firsttorch.3499f5b18c603af8.title: Hold one Water Bucket in the inventory
task.firsttorch.45aa06c29d714c09.title: Hold 64 Cobblestone in the inventory at once
task.firsttorch.56bb17d3ae825d1a.title: Hold 16 suitable cooked foods in the inventory at once
task.firsttorch.67cc28e4bf936e2b.title: Armour, durability, Bow, and Arrows checked
quest.firsttorch.end_prep.return_point.d:
Goal: prepare a safe respawn and reserve point outside the portal room.

Place a Bed in the lit Stronghold retreat room and sleep in it once to set the respawn point there. Place a Chest beside it with spare food, some blocks, and simple replacement equipment. Store every valuable item that is not needed in the End.

The Bed remains in the Overworld. Never take it through the portal or try to sleep in it in the End, where it explodes. Also check that the route from the respawn point to the portal room is lit, closable, and free from open Lava edges.

Set the checkmark only after sleeping in the Bed, seeing the respawn-point message, and filling the reserve Chest.

Reward: four Bread add to the reserve without replacing the prepared expedition supplies.
task.firsttorch.09ee4a06d1b5904d.title: Respawn point set and reserve Chest prepared
quest.firsttorch.end_prep.return_equippe:
Goal: reach the secured portal room with complete equipment and an intact return route.

Follow the marked route from the surface to the portal room. Close damaged passages, replace missing Torches, and open Iron Doors only when they can be controlled from both sides.

Insert no Eye yet. First check the retreat room, Bed, reserve Chest, Bow, Arrows, Armour, Water Bucket, food, and blocks. Return to base if anything is missing or close to breaking.

Set the checkmark when fully prepared at the secured portal room and the known Overworld route back still works.
task.firsttorch.3c217d3904e8c370.title: Fully equipped at the portal room with return route checked
quest.firsttorch.end_prep.clear.title: Clear the Portal Centre
quest.firsttorch.end_prep.clear.descript:
Goal: prepare the portal centre without falling into Lava or inserting an Eye.

If the three-by-three area inside the Portal Frames was covered with Cobblestone while securing the room, mine that cover now from outside the frame. Never stand on a Portal Frame or jump into the centre. Keep the safe floor beside the frame clear.

Side Lava outside the portal centre may remain covered. Check all twelve frames once more and compare the empty positions with the note. Take exactly the required number of Eyes of Ender from storage; extra Eyes remain in the Chest as reserve.

Set the checkmark when the portal centre is clear, the safe standing position is prepared, and the empty-frame count is confirmed again.
task.firsttorch.5e439f5b260ae592.title: Portal centre clear and empty frames counted again
quest.firsttorch.end_prep.activate.title: Activate the Portal — Do Not Jump Yet
quest.firsttorch.end_prep.activate.descr:
Goal: fill the empty frames from safe ground and remain in the Overworld afterwards.

Stand outside the twelve frames on the prepared solid position. Hold an Eye of Ender and right-click every empty frame individually. Inserted Eyes cannot be removed again.

The original capture shows the result: all twelve Eyes are inserted, the portal surface is active, and the Silverfish Spawner has been removed. Side Lava remains exposed in the image; secure that hazard separately. As soon as the final Eye is inserted, the dark portal surface immediately replaces the clear centre. Any contact with that surface teleports you to the End.

Do not walk across the frames, jump, or press forward after the final click. Step backwards, inspect the active surface from a distance, and leave the End unentered for now. The first entry follows with its own arrival plan.

Set the checkmark only when the portal is active, you are still standing safely before it, and nobody has fallen in accidentally.

Reward: ten experience points recognise the patient activation. The portal itself is not yet an invitation to an unprepared jump.
task.firsttorch.7065b17d482c07b4.title: Portal activated without entering the surface
image.firsttorch.stronghold_iron_door_ca: Original capture: the orange frame and arrow mark the Stone Button to the right of the Iron Door. It opens the Door only briefly.
image.firsttorch.end_portal_room_capture: Original capture of an inactive End Portal with empty and already filled frames. The Silverfish Spawner stands at the front; exposed Lava remains at the sides.
image.firsttorch.end_portal_active_captu: Original capture of the active End Portal with all twelve Eyes and the Silverfish Spawner removed. Side Lava remains exposed and must be secured separately. Do not enter the portal surface yet.
quest.firsttorch.end.0a6fb17d482c07c5.de:
Goal: decide what to do immediately after the loading screen before entering.

You appear on a five-by-five Obsidian platform. It may float freely beside the main island or be partly enclosed in End Stone. Do not walk blindly forwards or jump after loading.

Before jumping, arrange Cobblestone, Pickaxe, Water Bucket, food, and Sword in familiar hotbar positions. Then hold the Cobblestone. After arrival, first stand still, hold Sneak, look slightly down, and inspect the platform, island edge, and Void.

The Ender Dragon is active immediately, but rushing is more dangerous than a short observation. Look at no Enderman face. If the platform is enclosed, keep the Pickaxe ready; if it floats freely, keep the Cobblestone ready.

Set the checkmark only after preparing the hotbar and exact order: stand still, Sneak, look down, inspect the surroundings.
task.firsttorch.5fb406c29d715c1a.title: Hotbar and the first four actions prepared
quest.firsttorch.end.1b70c28e593d18d6.de:
Goal: enter the End for the first time; arrival is detected automatically.

Check full Health, a filled Hunger bar, Armour, and Shield one final time. Confirm that the respawn point is set in the Stronghold retreat room and the reserve Chest waits closed.

Walk into the dark portal surface without a running start. Take your hands off the movement keys during the dimension change. As soon as the surroundings become visible, follow the prepared routine exactly: stand still, hold Sneak, lower the view, and inspect the position first.

The automatic task completes through the real dimension change into the End. It requires no combat yet.
task.firsttorch.60c517d3ae826d2b.title: Enter the End for the first time
quest.firsttorch.end.2c81d39f6a4e29e7.de:
Goal: leave the Obsidian platform with control and reach solid End Stone.

If the platform is enclosed in End Stone, use the Pickaxe to dig a walkable staircase diagonally upwards. Never dig straight up, and open only one block ahead so an edge is not crossed unexpectedly.

If the platform floats beside the island, remain crouched while building. Place Cobblestone against the visible block edge and build a two-block-wide route to the nearest safe End Stone surface. A wider route reduces the fall risk; do not sprint or jump on it.

The in-game capture shows a Cobblestone ascent from the Obsidian platform to the End island. Your distance and height difference may vary. Make your own route at least two blocks wide throughout and protect exposed sides with block railings. Keep Sneak held while building; do not sprint or jump above the Void.

Set the checkmark only from a broad End Stone surface at least several blocks from the nearest unsecured edge. Continue not to look directly at Enderman faces.

Reward: 16 Cobblestone replace part of a possible arrival route; five experience points recognise the safe landing.
task.firsttorch.71d628e4bf937e3c.title: Safely reached solid End Stone
quest.firsttorch.end.3d92e4a07b5f3af8.de:
Goal: prepare a clearly visible retreat point on safe ground.

Choose a flat position far from the island edge. Form a shallow hollow or short Cobblestone rim and empty the Water Bucket into it, making an easily reached Water area that does not flow towards the Void.

Endermen avoid Water and take damage in it. If one is provoked accidentally, do not run towards the island edge: enter the Water, keep the Shield ready, and wait until the route is controllable again. The Dragon can still attack there; this is an Enderman retreat, not invulnerable shelter.

Remember the Obsidian platform and Water area as two separate landmarks. Set the checkmark after the Water is safely reachable and none flows towards the Void.
task.firsttorch.02e739f5c0a48f4d.title: Water retreat prepared on safe End Stone
quest.firsttorch.end.0cb72d9f6a4e29e8.ti: Optional: Build an Enderman Shelter Roof
quest.firsttorch.end.0cb72d9f6a4e29e8.de:
Goal: optionally build a dry retreat that Endermen are too tall to enter.

Choose a broad, level End Stone area at the foot of an Obsidian pillar, far from the Void. Build a three-by-three roof from nine End Stone blocks. Its underside sits exactly two blocks above the ground: you can stand upright beneath it, but an almost three-block-tall Enderman cannot.

The top view marks the safe centre in orange. The side view shows the two clear blocks between ground and roof. Use the Obsidian pillar as an obvious rear wall and remove every temporary support from the interior before testing it.

After provoking an Enderman accidentally, lower the view and move beneath the roof to the centre square. Remain there instead of colliding with it at the edge. If defence is necessary, attack only its legs from inside with fully recovered strikes.

The roof protects only against Enderman height and melee reach. It does not protect against the Dragon, Dragon's Breath, knockback, or the Void. If purple Breath covers the entrance or the Dragon attacks, the roof is not a safe place to remain.

This side branch is entirely optional and does not block the Crystal path. Set the checkmark only if the roof really measures three by three blocks, has two clear blocks of interior height, and its centre can be reached safely.
task.firsttorch.1dc83ea07b5f3af9.title: Build an optional 3 × 3 shelter roof with a safe centre
quest.firsttorch.end.4ea3f5b18c604b09.de:
Goal: recognise the parts of the fight before firing the first Arrow.

End Crystals stand on the tall Obsidian pillars. Visible beams show that they heal the Dragon. Some Crystals are surrounded by Iron Bars. This healing makes attacking the Dragon directly inefficient, so a separate ordered Crystal plan comes first.

The Dragon flies above the island, knocks players away, and leaves purple Dragon's Breath that continues dealing damage on the ground. Leave a purple cloud sideways immediately and heal on safe ground. Do not walk backwards into the Void.

A Bedrock structure stands at the island centre. This is the later exit, but its portal surface appears only after victory. Do not stand unnecessarily beside it during the fight; the Dragon regularly perches there.

Endermen are an additional but avoidable hazard. Keep the view low, attack none, and use the prepared Water retreat after a mistake.

Set the checkmark when pillars, Crystals, Dragon's Breath, Bedrock centre, island edges, and the Water retreat can be distinguished. Shoot no Crystal yet.
task.firsttorch.13f84a06d1b5a05e.title: Battlefield recognised without attacking a Crystal
quest.firsttorch.end.5fa406c29d715c1b.de:
Goal: first destroy every End Crystal that is not surrounded by Iron Bars.

Choose a broad position inside the island and keep well away from the pillar base. Draw the Bow fully, aim at an exposed Crystal, and release the Arrow. One hit is enough, but the Crystal explodes: never shoot from immediate range and do not strike it with a Sword.

The image shows only this first part: hit a clearly exposed Crystal with a distance shot from the ground. Pillar height is shortened in the image.

Move sideways across safe ground after every shot. Check for Dragon's Breath, an approaching Dragon, Hearts, and Hunger before aiming again. Lower the view between shots so no Enderman receives accidental eye contact.

Repeat this only for clearly exposed Crystals. Set the checkmark when no uncaged pillar still holds a Crystal and Health is full or nearly full again.
task.firsttorch.24b95b17e2c6b160.title: Destroy every exposed Crystal from a safe distance
quest.firsttorch.end.60b517d3ae826d2c.de:
Goal: open and destroy the remaining caged Crystals without standing beside their explosions.

Mine 64 End Stone on broad ground without creating unsafe holes beneath your feet. End Stone is better here than carried Cobblestone: the Dragon cannot destroy End Stone. It can still hit or knock you from an exposed staircase.

This image belongs only to the cages: 1 — climb beside the cage and create an opening; 2 — descend completely and only then shoot through the opening from the ground. Pillar height is shortened.

Choose exactly one cage. Build a narrow rising End Stone staircase from the ground close against its Obsidian pillar. Remain crouched, never work above the Void, and go down several steps whenever the Dragon approaches. Do not run on the staircase.

Climb only until an Iron Bar can be reached from the side. Use the Pickaxe to remove only enough of one cage side for an Arrow to pass later. Never strike the Crystal and do not enter the cage. Return completely to the ground along the same staircase.

Move far enough back for a clear shot and destroy the Crystal with a fully drawn Bow through the opening. Repeat the entire sequence one cage at a time; never combine climbing and shooting into one action.

The item task detects 64 End Stone automatically. Set the checkmark only after every caged Crystal has been destroyed from safe ground distance and you stand on broad End Stone again.
task.firsttorch.35ca6c28f3d7c271.title: Hold 64 End Stone for safe climbs at the same time
task.firsttorch.46db7d3904e8d382.title: Open every cage separately and destroy its Crystal from the ground
quest.firsttorch.end.71c628e4bf937e3d.de:
Goal: verify the result and regroup before the actual Dragon fight begins.

Inspect all ten Obsidian pillars in turn. No End Crystal may remain on any top. If a healing beam still reaches the Dragon, one Crystal remains: do not attack the Dragon, but search the pillars systematically again.

Then return to the safe Water area. Eat until the Hunger bar is full, wait for healing, and inspect Armour, Shield, Bow, Pickaxe, Water Bucket, and remaining Arrows. Keep Dragon's Breath out of the route by waiting for the purple cloud to disappear; do not walk through it.

Set the checkmark only after confirming ten empty pillar tops, no visible healing beam, and restored Health. The next step explains the Dragon fight; do not deliberately attack it before then.

Reward: 16 Arrows replace some of the Crystal shots. Ten experience points recognise the completely disabled healing cycle.
task.firsttorch.57ec8e4a15f9e493.title: Confirm ten empty pillars, no healing, and a ready regroup

chapter.firsttorch.end_arrival.descripti: Arrive with control, reach safe ground, and learn the battlefield.
trophy.firsttorch.end_arrival.title: Safe Landing
trophy.firsttorch.end_arrival.descriptio: Completed every arrival lesson, including the optional shelter roof.
chapter.firsttorch.crystal_removal.title: End Crystals
chapter.firsttorch.crystal_removal.descr: Remove exposed and caged Crystals separately, then verify healing has stopped.
trophy.firsttorch.crystal_removal.title: Healing Disabled
trophy.firsttorch.crystal_removal.descri: Completed every Crystal lesson and regrouped before the Dragon fight.
image.firsttorch.end_arrival_platform.de: Original capture: Cobblestone ascent from the Obsidian platform to the End island. Build your route at least two blocks wide and protect exposed sides.
image.firsttorch.enderman_roof_shelter.d: Three-by-three shelter roof with two clear blocks of interior height.
image.firsttorch.end_battlefield.descrip: Original End battlefield capture with Obsidian pillars and the Bedrock centre.
image.firsttorch.end_crystal_exposed.des: Shoot an exposed End Crystal from safe ground distance.
image.firsttorch.end_crystal_removal.des: Open the cage from the side, descend completely, then shoot from the ground.
quest.firsttorch.end.12d739f5c0a48f4e.de:
Goal: hit the flying Ender Dragon at least once with a controlled Bow shot, then return to safety.

Remain on a broad area inside the island. Keep away from edges, pillar bases, and the Bedrock centre. Do not chase the Dragon blindly: wait until its flight path is clear, draw the Bow fully, and aim slightly ahead rather than at its current position.

Move sideways after every shot and check the surroundings again. Lower the view between shots to avoid provoking an Enderman. If the Dragon flies directly towards you, stop aiming and dodge sideways; the next hit matters less than safe ground.

Its purple projectile leaves a lingering Dragon's Breath cloud. Move sideways out of it immediately and remain outside until it has disappeared completely. Heal and eat before shooting again. The Water retreat helps against Endermen, but it does not protect against Dragon's Breath.

When the Dragon begins descending towards the Bedrock centre, stop shooting. The Sword is needed for the following perched phase. Set the checkmark only after at least one safe Bow hit, once you are back on clear End Stone and touching no Breath cloud.
task.firsttorch.23e84a06d1b5a05f.title: Made one controlled flight hit and dodged safely
quest.firsttorch.end.34f95b17e2c6b170.de:
Goal: use at least one perch for safe Sword strikes, then retreat with control.

The Dragon regularly perches above the Bedrock structure at the island centre. Arrows bounce off it during this phase. Switch to the Sword and wait outside any Breath clouds. Approach from behind; a wing strike can launch you far away when moving beside the wings, while its breath is an additional danger in front of the head.

Move beneath the tail or its base from behind. Jump briefly if necessary and strike with a fully recovered attack indicator; do not click rapidly. Hits there deal less damage than head hits, but avoid the dangerous side approach between the wings. Continue watching Endermen, Health, and Hunger.

As soon as the Dragon moves its wings and takes off again, stop attacking and retreat from the centre to broad End Stone. Heal there before beginning another flight phase. Patiently alternate between the Bow in flight and the Sword while perched.

Do not use Beds for this beginner fight. Trying to sleep makes a Bed explode violently in the End and may kill you or knock you into fire or the Void.

Set the checkmark after one complete perched phase: approached from behind, delivered at least one recovered jumping strike beneath the tail or its base, and retreated safely during take-off.
task.firsttorch.450a6c28f3d7c281.title: Used one perched phase safely and retreated in time
quest.firsttorch.end.561b7d3904e8d392.de:
Goal: defeat the Ender Dragon for the first time; victory is detected automatically.

Repeat the safe rhythm: shoot only fully drawn Arrows from a good position during flight, leave Breath clouds sideways, and approach from behind for recovered jumping strikes beneath the tail or its base while perched. Interrupt every attack when Health, Hunger, surroundings, or the retreat route becomes unsafe.

A long fight is not a mistake. Use the Water retreat or optional shelter roof only against Endermen, then return to clear, broad End Stone for the Dragon. Never approach an island edge for one extra hit.

After the final hit, the Dragon disintegrates, experience falls, and the exit portal opens in the Bedrock centre. The real Vanilla advancement completes this task automatically. Do not jump into the portal yet: the next step explains victory, the Dragon Egg, and a safe return separately.
task.firsttorch.672c8e4a15f9e4a3.title: Defeated the Ender Dragon for the first time
quest.firsttorch.end.013e8f5b26a0f5b5.de:
Goal: calm the situation after the fight and distinguish the exit portal from the Dragon Egg.

Wait until the Dragon's entire death animation has ended. Collect the falling experience orbs, but do not chase them to an island edge. The Dragon no longer attacks; Endermen and the Void remain dangerous. Keep the view low and move on broad ground.

A dark, star-like portal surface has now opened in the central Bedrock structure. Entering it returns you to the Overworld. A single Dragon Egg also appears on the central Bedrock. It is an optional, unique trophy block and is not required for returning.

The in-game image shows the open exit and Egg from a safe distance. Do not enter the dark surface yet if you want to complete the optional Egg branch first. Do not strike the Egg repeatedly without a plan: it can teleport and cannot be mined like a normal block.

Set the checkmark after collecting the experience and safely identifying both the portal surface and Egg. Then choose between the optional Egg branch and returning directly.
task.firsttorch.124f9a6c37b106c6.title: Collect experience and identify the exit portal and Dragon Egg
quest.firsttorch.end.2350ab7d48c217d7.de:
Goal: collect the Dragon Egg with the Torch method as an optional trophy; success is detected automatically.

Touch or strike the Egg exactly once. It teleports to a nearby position. Find it again with a lowered view and stand on safe, broad End Stone. Do not continue striking it, and take care not to send it towards the Void or exit portal.

Dig down beside the Egg, not through it. Initially leave the End Stone block directly beneath the Egg in place. Remove the block one level lower and put a Torch there, leaving only one supporting block between the Egg and Torch.

Now break the supporting block directly beneath the Egg. The Egg falls onto the Torch and becomes an item that can be collected. Pick it up immediately; when it enters the inventory, the real Vanilla advancement completes this task automatically.

This branch is optional and does not gate the return. If skipped, the Egg remains in the End and can be retrieved during a later visit.
task.firsttorch.3461bc8e59d328e8.title: Collect the Dragon Egg in the inventory for the first time
quest.firsttorch.end.4572cd9f6ae439f9.de:
Goal: leave the End through the open exit portal and confirm the return only in the Overworld.

Before entering, check that every wanted item has been collected. The Dragon Egg is not required. Stand on the Bedrock rim, look into the dark portal surface, and walk or jump in without a running start. Items and experience are retained during this portal transfer.

After the first victory, the End Poem and then the credits appear. You may watch them or skip with Esc; skipping loses no items. You then appear at the set respawn point. If it is no longer valid, you arrive at the world spawn point.

Wait until the Overworld is fully visible. Check Health, Hunger, experience, and inventory, then orient yourself before moving. Set the checkmark only then. The active Stronghold End Portal remains available for later visits to the End.
task.firsttorch.5683dea07bf54a0a.title: Return through the exit and check the inventory in the Overworld
chapter.firsttorch.dragon_victory.title: Dragon Fight and Return
chapter.firsttorch.dragon_victory.descri: Distinguish flight and perch, defeat the Dragon, and return safely. The Dragon Egg is optional.
trophy.firsttorch.dragon_victory.title: Mastered the End
trophy.firsttorch.dragon_victory.descrip: Completed all six combat, victory and return lessons, including optional Dragon Egg retrieval.
image.firsttorch.ender_dragon_flight.des: Shoot the flying Dragon with a Bow and dodge sideways on safe ground.
image.firsttorch.ender_dragon_perched.de: Approach the perched Dragon from behind beneath its tail and retreat in time.
image.firsttorch.end_exit_portal.descrip: Original capture of the open exit portal and Dragon Egg after victory.
image.firsttorch.dragon_egg_retrieval.de: Teleport the Dragon Egg once, place a Torch beneath its supporting block, then remove that block.
Goal: prepare a separate trip to the outer End islands without risking trophies or unnecessary valuables.

Store the Dragon Egg and other unneeded valuables in a Chest at home. Equip at least Iron Armour or something better, Shield, Sword, Bow, at least 32 Arrows, Pickaxe, Water Bucket, plenty of food, and Torches. Repair badly damaged equipment before leaving.

Take four Ender Pearls: one for the outward End Gateway, one for the later return, and two in reserve. A Pearl throw teleports you but costs Health. Never throw one with few Hearts and never use one as a rescue attempt across the Void.

Before departure, make a separate filled Milk Bucket for the later Shulkers: place three Iron Ingots in a V shape at a Crafting Table to make an empty Bucket, then use it on an adult Cow in the Overworld. Keep the Water Bucket separate; ordinary Cows do not live on the End islands.

Also take at least 64 End Stone for stairs, broad standing areas, and guard edges, plus two Cobblestone blocks and a Torch for the return marker. Put blocks, an Ender Pearl, food, Milk Bucket, Water Bucket, and weapon in familiar hotbar positions.

The three item tasks detect four Ender Pearls, 64 End Stone, and one Milk Bucket automatically. Set the checkmark only when the remaining equipment is complete and the respawn point beside the Stronghold retreat room still works.
task.firsttorch.08a5f0c29d176c2c.title: Hold four Ender Pearls for travel, return, and reserves at the same time
task.firsttorch.19b601d3ae287d3d.title: Hold 64 End Stone for access and safety work at the same time
task.firsttorch.30d823f5c04a9f60.title: Hold one filled Milk Bucket for later Shulkers
task.firsttorch.2ac712e4bf398e4e.title: Check equipment, store valuables, and prepare the hotbar
Goal: enter the End again and use the secured arrival route to reach the broad main island.

Follow the known markers to the Stronghold retreat room. Sleep there again, replace used supplies from the reserve Chest, and check Armour, Health, and Hunger. Then enter the still-active End Portal without a running start.

Take your hands off the movement keys while loading. Remain on the Obsidian platform, hold Sneak, lower the view, and inspect the route already built. Repair missing blocks before using it; do not sprint or jump across damaged sections.

The defeated Dragon remains gone. It returns only if you later summon it deliberately with four End Crystals at the exit portal. Do not place End Crystals there now.

Set the checkmark only on broad End Stone of the main island. Confirm the Water retreat, your shelter roof (if built), and home portal as landmarks before searching for the new Gateway.
task.firsttorch.4ce93406d15ba060.title: Return to the main island over the secured arrival route
Secure Access to the End Gateway

Goal: find the End Gateway created after the Dragon victory and build a safe throwing position before it.

Circle the main island with a lowered view and plenty of distance from the Void. Near the outer edge, look for a small, usually elevated Bedrock structure with one dark portal surface in its centre. This is not the large exit portal and is not entered on foot.

The in-game image shows a real Gateway and an existing access route. Build your own route from the prepared End Stone and add the stable standing area and protected sides described below.

Build a crouched End Stone staircase towards the structure. Widen its end into a stable standing area and protect open sides with edges at least one block high. Do not build straight upwards or attempt to jump onto the Bedrock.

Stand where the dark portal surface is fully visible and no Bedrock obstructs the throw. A clear retreat line to the main island must remain behind you. Continue keeping away from every unprotected edge.

Set the checkmark only when stairs, standing area, and side edges are complete. Do not throw the Ender Pearl yet; the next step explains the transfer.
task.firsttorch.6e0b5628f37dc282.title: Find the End Gateway and build a protected throwing position
Goal: reach the outer End islands for the first time; the real portal transfer is detected automatically.

Eat and heal completely. Put one Ender Pearl in the main hand; a second must remain in the inventory for returning. Stand centrally on the protected area, aim precisely at the dark portal block, and throw the Pearl with right click.

Throw only while standing still. If the Pearl hits Bedrock instead of the portal surface, it can teleport you to the impact point. After any missed throw, stop and inspect your footing and Health before aiming again. Do not follow it by walking or jumping. When it hits the portal surface, you are moved far out to the outer islands.

Take your hands off the movement keys during transfer. After loading: stand still, hold Sneak, lower the view, and first inspect the ground, Void, and corresponding return Gateway. The Pearl throw costs Health; move only after this check.

The exact Vanilla advancement detects successful entry automatically. It says only that the transfer worked — not that the arrival position is already safe.
task.firsttorch.102d784a159fe4a4.title: Travel through an End Gateway for the first time
Goal: turn the unknown arrival position into an unmistakable return point.

Initially remain crouched and check whether the arrival is on broad End Stone or near an edge. Secure a small standing area with End Stone before inspecting the surroundings. There is no Dragon here, but many Endermen and large gaps between islands remain.

Find the Bedrock return Gateway immediately beside the arrival. Build a clearly visible marker beside it — not in front — using two Cobblestone blocks and a Torch. Record its coordinates or take a screenshot. Never cover the dark portal surface.

For the journey home, later throw an Ender Pearl into this dark centre to return to the main island. Keep at least one Pearl separate from the active hotbar slot. Without one, a dangerous improvisation would be required.

Set the checkmark only after securing the standing area, visibly marking the return Gateway, and recording its position. Do not leave for another island before then.
task.firsttorch.324f9a6c37b106c6.title: Secure the arrival, mark the return Gateway, and record coordinates
chapter.firsttorch.outer_arrival.title: To the Outer End Islands
chapter.firsttorch.outer_arrival.descrip: Prepare a second visit, reach the Gateway, and secure the return route.
trophy.firsttorch.outer_arrival.title: A Secure Arrival
trophy.firsttorch.outer_arrival.descript: Completed all five lessons through securing the outer-island arrival.
image.firsttorch.end_gateway_access.desc: Original capture of an End Gateway and access route. Add a safe standing area and protected sides.
image.firsttorch.outer_end_arrival.descr: Secure the return Gateway arrival, mark it from the side, and record its coordinates.
chapter.firsttorch.chorus_city.title: Chorus and the End City
chapter.firsttorch.chorus_city.descripti: Harvest Chorus safely and find a marked route to an End City.
trophy.firsttorch.chorus_city.title: Chorus and the End City
trophy.firsttorch.chorus_city.descriptio: Complete every lesson in this chapter. A quest-book trophy, not an inventory item.
Harvest Chorus Fruit and a Flower

Goal: hold at least eight Chorus Fruit and one Chorus Flower at the same time.

Remain on the same broad island as the secured return point at first. Find a branching purple Chorus Plant that stands entirely on solid End Stone and does not grow immediately beside an edge.

The darker stems can be broken by hand or with a tool. Each destroyed stem drops either one Chorus Fruit or nothing, so eight Fruit will probably require several plant sections. Do not begin beneath an unsecured edge, and continue avoiding deliberate eye contact with Endermen.

Also break one bright purple Chorus Flower at a plant tip directly before destroying the supporting stem. Only the directly broken Flower is collected reliably as a Flower. Keep it: it can later be planted on End Stone and grow into a new Chorus Plant.

Both item tasks complete automatically while eight Fruit and one Flower are present in your inventory together. Do not eat a Fruit yet—its special effect is tested safely in the next lesson.
task.firsttorch.5460b8d3ae927f4c.title: Eight Chorus Fruit in the inventory together
task.firsttorch.6571c9e4bfa3805d.title: One directly harvested Chorus Flower in the inventory
Goal: eat exactly one Chorus Fruit on a broad, flat, and safe End Stone area.

Chorus Fruit restores hunger and can even be eaten with a full hunger bar. It then teleports you randomly by up to eight blocks to a valid standing position. You cannot control the destination.

Find level solid ground with at least eight blocks of room in every direction; ten blocks from every void edge provides extra reserve. Avoid cliffs, narrow ledges, tall Chorus Plants, and unfamiliar structures. Heal fully and remember your starting position.

Hold right-click to eat one Chorus Fruit. Take your hands away from the movement keys during the teleport. Immediately hold Sneak after arriving, lower your view, and orient yourself towards the marked return Gateway.

Chorus Fruit is not a reliable rescue tool: it chooses neither the destination you want nor a route home, and it can move you through walls or onto an unexpected ledge. Never use one deliberately beside the void.

Set the checkmark after testing exactly one Fruit safely, checking the new position, and confirming that you can still find the route to the return Gateway.

Reward: 5 experience points for the controlled first test.
task.firsttorch.0793eb06d1c5a27f.title: Tested one Chorus Fruit on safe ground and reoriented
Goal: build a safe crossing to the next island, cross it, and return over it once.

Carry at least 64 End Stone, two Ender Pearls, food, and a Pickaxe. The item tasks check the End Stone and Pearls automatically. The Pearls are reserves for known safe destinations—not an invitation to make a blind throw.

Choose a nearby island with a broad landing area that is completely visible. If you cannot clearly see both the destination and the island's underside, find a shorter crossing. An Ender Pearl may fall short or strike a side wall; Chorus Fruit chooses its destination randomly. Use neither for a blind jump over the void.

The in-game image shows a Cobblestone bridge between two islands. For this exercise, use your prepared End Stone and add the safe bridge ends and return marker described below.

Build the crossing two blocks wide. Hold Sneak, remain one block back from the open edge, and place one block forwards followed by a second block directly beside it. Repeat that pair without releasing Sneak. Stop regularly, realign yourself, and check both sides.

Place an obvious return marker on the new island immediately: two Cobblestone blocks stacked with a Torch on the side you came from. Widen both bridge ends into safe standing areas. If an Enderman approaches, stop building and retreat to broad ground or your Water refuge.

Cross the completed bridge in both directions. Set the checkmark only when it is two blocks wide throughout, both ends are secured, and the marker clearly points towards the return Gateway.

Reward: 5 experience points for the first verified island crossing.
task.firsttorch.2b9d1608e4f7a3c2.title: 64 End Stone in the inventory together
task.firsttorch.3cae2719f508b4d3.title: Two Ender Pearls held in reserve
task.firsttorch.4dbf382a0619c5e4.title: Tested the two-wide bridge in both directions
Goal: find an End City, approach it by a safe route, and confirm your way back without exploring its interior yet.

End Cities generate on the large outer islands, but not on every island or at a fixed distance. Eyes of Ender do not point towards them. Choose one main direction, record the return Gateway's coordinates, and leave a marker pointing back at every island crossing.

Travel across broad islands first and scan the horizon from elevated but safe ground. Do not change direction at every small gap. A clear route with a few well-built crossings is slower than running aimlessly, but it also leads you home again.

Recognise an End City by tall violet Purpur towers, pale End Stone Brick floors, narrow bridges, and white End Rod lights. Some cities are small. A floating End Ship belongs only to some large cities, so it is not a reliable search landmark.

Approach over solid ground. The automatic task completes when the game recognises your location as part of an End City. Remain outside the buildings afterwards: Shulkers, long falls, and narrow paths wait inside and will each be explained in the next lesson.

Look back and confirm that the last marker and your safe route towards the return Gateway are visible. Only then set the checkmark.

Reward: 10 experience points for finding the city while preserving a route home.
task.firsttorch.70e26b5d394cf817.title: Reached an End City
task.firsttorch.01f37c6e4a5d0928.title: Checked the safe return route before entering
chapter.firsttorch.shulker_city.title: Shulkers and city exploration
chapter.firsttorch.shulker_city.descript: Explore one protected room at a time and test your first Shulker Box.
trophy.firsttorch.shulker_city.title: Shulkers and city exploration
trophy.firsttorch.shulker_city.descripti: Complete every lesson in this chapter. A quest-book trophy, not an inventory item.
Goal: prepare a safe position outside the city and hold every item needed for the first Shulker encounter.

Do not enter the buildings yet. Shulkers are hostile creatures fixed to floors, walls, or ceilings. Their shells resemble Purpur blocks, and their projectiles can make you float upwards. A fall after that effect is often more dangerous than the first hit.

Bring the Milk Bucket packed during the earlier preparation, one Water Bucket, a Shield, and at least 32 End Stone. If the Milk Bucket was used or forgotten, first retreat safely through the outer Gateway to the main End island, then use the central exit portal to return to the Overworld and collect milk from an adult Cow with a separate empty Bucket. Keep the Water Bucket filled as a second tool; one Bucket cannot contain both liquids. Ordinary Cows do not live on the main End island or the outer islands.

On broad ground beside the lowest safe entrance, build a small covered staging point from End Stone. Give it a solid roof only two blocks above the floor, one rear wall, and a corner that completely breaks sight from the doorway. Keep the route from this cover to the open island clear and far from the Void.

Put the Shield in the offhand. Keep Milk, Water, End Stone, food, and a weapon in known hotbar positions. The four item tasks complete automatically. Set the checkmark only after the low roof, solid corner, clear retreat, and hotbar are ready.
task.firsttorch.6f8fb5cfa3bb0d00.title: One Milk Bucket for ending Levitation
task.firsttorch.02ff8330ce2c8439.title: One separate Water Bucket for a safe landing
task.firsttorch.3ab38b83060f9d89.title: One Shield for the first projectile encounter
task.firsttorch.1cc67ec6b0559bdf.title: 32 End Stone held together for cover and repairs
task.firsttorch.783d54dcd2748276.title: Covered staging point, retreat, and hotbar prepared
Goal: recognise a Shulker and rehearse the safe response before crossing the doorway.

A closed Shulker looks like a compact purple block and has strong extra armour. It opens its upper shell to look and fire, exposing the pale head. Attack only during an opening; do not stand in view waiting for it.

The left side shows exact front views of the closed and open Minecraft 26.1.2 Shulker model. The right side shows its pale homing bullet stopped by solid cover, followed by the Levitation symbol and the prepared Milk and Water Buckets.

A Shulker Bullet follows around corners in separate turns, but a solid block stops it. Step fully behind the prepared corner until the bullet hits a block. In clear space, one accurate Sword or Arrow hit can destroy the bullet. A raised Shield facing the incoming bullet is the backup when neither response is ready.

A successful bullet hit has a base damage of four points, or two hearts, before protection and gives ten seconds of Levitation. Do not seek a hit to test this. If hit unexpectedly, stop attacking and move gently beneath the nearest low ceiling while keeping a solid landing area below.

Milk removes Levitation immediately, but then you fall immediately. Drink it only while held against a low ceiling or directly above a safe floor or prepared Water landing. Place Water on solid floor when there is time and a clear target; never pour it into the Void. Do not use a Chorus Fruit or blind Ender Pearl as a rescue.

At the staging point, point to the solid corner, low roof, Milk slot, and Water slot in that order. Set the checkmark after rehearsing that response without deliberately entering a bullet's path.
task.firsttorch.17c988320fabf288.title: Rehearsed the bullet and Levitation response under cover
Goal: enter only the first ground-level room, handle one reachable Shulker with control, and return to the staging point.

Choose the lowest entrance reached entirely over solid ground. Mark its outside face with a Torch or one distinctive block so it remains recognisable. Do not begin with an exterior staircase, narrow bridge, tall tower, or End Ship.

Approach with the Shield raised and stop at the threshold. Look first at the floor, walls, and ceiling for a closed purple shell. Let only one Shulker see you. If several open or several bullets appear, step completely behind the outside corner and wait instead of advancing.

From the doorway, destroy incoming bullets or let them strike solid cover. When the selected Shulker opens, use one fully drawn Bow shot from cover. Lower the Bow and reassess after every shot. If it teleports after taking damage, do not chase it towards a ledge, ceiling opening, or upper floor.

Continue only while the floor and retreat remain clear. After the first nearby Shulker is defeated, check for every remaining bullet, mark or light the first room, and return directly to the covered staging point. Leave stairs, vertical shafts, loot rooms, and the ship for later lessons.

Set the checkmark outside after Health is restored, Milk and Water are accounted for, and the marked doorway still gives a clear route into and out of that first room.

Reward: 10 experience points for the first controlled entry and return.
task.firsttorch.73b374882251b9fb.title: Handled one Shulker in the first room and returned outside
Goal: reach only the first enclosed landing or room above ground level, secure it, and return down the same route once.

Bring at least 32 End Stone and eight Torches in addition to the Milk, Water, Shield, food, weapon, and Bow already prepared. The item tasks confirm the building and marking supplies. Refill them outside before climbing if either stack is short.

End City interiors vary. Choose an interior stair or tower opening that rises from the cleared ground-level room. If this part of the city has no upper section, return outside and choose another entrance reached over solid ground. Do not climb the exterior walls, cross a high open bridge, or approach an End Ship in this lesson.

Move one visible section at a time with the Shield ready. Stop before every stair bend, parkour gap, or vertical opening; inspect the floor, walls, and ceiling for Shulkers. Let only one see you. If several shells open or bullets arrive from different directions, retreat to the last solid corner and wait.

Repair every unsafe gap with End Stone before crossing it. At the first enclosed landing above ground level, add a small solid roof two blocks above a safe standing area and a corner that breaks sight from below and above. Put one Torch on the side that leads back down. Keep Water for an emergency landing instead of using it as the planned ascent.

After the area is quiet, descend the exact marked route to the ground-level room, then climb back to the covered landing. Set the checkmark there only when both directions work without jumping, every gap is secured, and the return Torch is unambiguous.
task.firsttorch.231a7cab2183b609.title: 32 End Stone held together for landings and gap repairs
task.firsttorch.0225cacbb251a551.title: Eight Torches held together for the marked route
task.firsttorch.1a1f8d7425cf1bbb.title: Secured one upper landing and tested the route in both directions
Secure One End City Loot Room

Goal: find one chest room inside the End City, secure its approach, and open one chest without continuing towards a ship.

End Cities are assembled differently, and a small city may contain no chest room at all. Continue only from the highest landing that already has a tested return route. If that branch ends without a chest, descend safely and try another ground-connected branch or another city. The checkmark requires a real chest room, but never a particular city shape.

Stop at the room entrance and inspect all surfaces before approaching a chest. Defeat or isolate every Shulker that can see the chest or your route back. Destroy lingering bullets, close exposed floor gaps with End Stone, and establish a low covered corner between the chest and the marked descent route.

Open one chest only after the room is quiet. The chest screen does not make nearby danger safe, so close it immediately if a Shulker opens or a bullet appears. Move the contents into your inventory only while the approach and retreat remain clear.

Chest contents are random. Possible finds include metal or gems, Beetroot Seeds, a Saddle, Horse Armour, enchanted Iron or Diamond equipment, and sometimes a Spire Armour Trim Smithing Template. No particular item is required. Elytra is not ordinary chest loot: it appears in an Item Frame aboard some End Ships and belongs to a later lesson.

Set the checkmark after opening one secured End City chest, collecting what you want, closing the chest screen, and confirming the marked route back down. Do not continue upwards just because inventory space remains.
task.firsttorch.383f01db43c46bc6.title: Secured and opened one ordinary End City chest
Return the First City Loot Outside

Goal: leave the loot room, descend safely, and return the first chest contents to the covered staging point outside.

Put the most valuable chosen items in normal inventory slots, not in the offhand or an active hotbar slot needed for the Shield, Milk, Water, blocks, food, or weapon. Leave low-value items behind when carrying them would remove a safety tool. Check Health and hunger before moving.

Follow the Torch markers down through every secured landing. Pause at each one, clear any new bullet, and check the next floor before descending. Do not jump down a shaft, use Chorus Fruit, or throw an Ender Pearl to shorten the return. If the route is no longer clear, rebuild cover and restore it before proceeding.

At ground level, pass through the marked doorway and return to the covered staging point outside. Account for the Milk and Water Buckets, restore Health and food, and separate the collected loot from the supplies for the next entry. Store valuables there only if the container is protected from accidental loss and you know how they will return home.

Set the checkmark outside after the loot is accounted for and the entire route from the chest room to the staging point has been completed safely. The next expedition starts from this recovered position rather than from the top of the tower.

Reward: 10 experience points for securing the first loot and bringing it back outside.
task.firsttorch.6c3ca1f2a59b96f8.title: Returned from the chest room with the first loot accounted for
Goal: collect and hold two Shulker Shells at the same time without leaving the secured city route.

A defeated Shulker may drop one Shell, but a drop is not guaranteed. The Looting enchantment increases the chance and is useful if your Sword already has it; it is not required. Two Shells may therefore take more than two carefully chosen encounters.

Return from the outside staging point with Milk, Water, Shield, food, Bow, and building blocks accounted for. Use only rooms and landings whose route back has already been tested. Before selecting a Shulker, close nearby floor gaps and confirm that a dropped item will land on solid blocks instead of beside the Void.

Engage one Shulker at a time from a doorway or solid corner. Attack when its shell opens, then reassess instead of chasing it if it teleports. After the defeat, wait until every bullet has broken and any Levitation has ended before walking to the drop. If no Shell appears, that encounter still followed the correct method; choose another reachable Shulker only after recovering.

The item task completes automatically when two Shulker Shells are together in your inventory. Return them to the covered staging point before starting the recipe.
task.firsttorch.292681f22352c745.title: Two Shulker Shells held together
Craft and Test a Shulker Box

Goal: craft the first Shulker Box, then test its storage behaviour on broad safe ground.

Use a Crafting Table at the covered staging point. In one vertical column of the three-by-three grid, place one Shulker Shell, one ordinary Chest, and the second Shulker Shell. A Trapped Chest, Ender Chest, or Copper Chest does not replace the ordinary Chest in this recipe.

Take the Shulker Box from the output. The item task completes automatically while it is in your inventory. It provides 27 portable storage slots and keeps its contents when the placed box is broken and collected. A Shulker Box cannot be stored inside another Shulker Box.

Test that safely: place the empty box far from every edge with the block directly above it clear, open it, insert one spare End Stone, and close it. Break the box with your Pickaxe, wait until Levitation and bullets are absent, pick it up, place it again, and reopen it. Confirm that the End Stone remained inside.

The contents survive normal collection, but they are lost if the dropped Shulker Box falls into the Void, burns, or is otherwise destroyed. Set the checkmark only after the box is back in your inventory with the test block still inside.
task.firsttorch.2e392a3f4da700d2.title: One crafted Shulker Box in the inventory
task.firsttorch.4edad7d40e987575.title: Placed, packed, collected, and reopened the Shulker Box safely
chapter.firsttorch.end_ship.title: End Ship and safe return
chapter.firsttorch.end_ship.description: Recover the Elytra without rushing into flight and bring it home safely.
trophy.firsttorch.end_ship.title: End Ship and safe return
trophy.firsttorch.end_ship.description: Complete every lesson in this chapter. A quest-book trophy, not an inventory item.
Secure an Approach towards an End Ship

Goal: locate an End Ship and secure the highest city room or balcony from which its deck can be approached, without crossing to the ship yet.

Only some larger End Cities have a floating ship. In the in-game image, the ship is separated from the city in the upper right. If your city has no ship, return along the marked island route and search for another End City. Do not treat a tall tower, open bridge, or empty horizon as proof that a ship must be nearby.

Before climbing again, hold at least 128 End Stone, two reserve Ender Pearls, and 16 Arrows. These automatic tasks establish a minimum, not a promise that every possible gap can be crossed with that amount. Keep the Pearls as reserves for a visible safe landing rather than planning a blind throw.

Pack earlier loot into the Shulker Box outside, but keep Shield, Milk, Water, food, Bow, Pickaxe, End Stone, and Arrows directly accessible. Climb through the interior one secured landing at a time. Continue marking the side that leads down, closing dangerous gaps, and isolating one Shulker at a time.

At the nearest room or balcony facing the ship, clear every Shulker that can see the position. Several blocks back from the edge, build a low covered corner and block accidental side exits. From cover, confirm that the intended deck or doorway is visible and that no part of the route depends on Chorus Fruit or an unseen Pearl landing.

Do not begin the bridge or board the ship in this lesson. First descend the complete marked route to the outside staging point and climb back to the ship-facing cover once. Set the checkmark there only when the return works in both directions, the three supply tasks are complete, and the ship remains clearly visible from solid cover.

Reward: 10 experience points for preparing the End Ship approach without rushing the crossing.
task.firsttorch.0c24a70b572395df.title: 128 End Stone held together for high access work
task.firsttorch.33798a78bf88632f.title: Two Ender Pearls kept as visible-landing reserves
task.firsttorch.6031d6db54dcd7af.title: 16 Arrows held together for distant Shulkers
task.firsttorch.541a44ee25ff8d48.title: Secured the ship-facing cover and tested its full return route
Build a Protected Route to the End Ship

Goal: connect the secured city position to the End Ship with a protected route, enter one enclosed ship space, and return across once.

Bring at least 256 End Stone and 16 Torches to the ship-facing cover. The item tasks establish a minimum reserve. A distant ship or an indirect route may require more; return for additional blocks before starting if the full destination is not clearly visible.

From cover, use fully drawn Bow shots to remove every visible Shulker on the hull, deck, and intended entry. Wait for all bullets to break. Keep the two Ender Pearls as emergency reserves for a visible solid landing; do not replace the planned bridge with a throw.

Build a corridor with a floor two blocks wide, solid walls two blocks high on both sides, and a complete roof. Hold Sneak while extending each pair of floor blocks. Add both walls and the roof before moving beyond the last completed section, so neither a bullet nor Levitation can push or lift you from the route. Place Torches inside with a consistent side pointing back towards the city.

Connect to a broad part of the deck or a visible side opening. Seal accidental gaps around the bridge end before opening a one-block-wide entry into the ship. Inspect floor, walls, and ceiling, handle only the first reachable Shulker from the corridor corner, and mark the city-facing side of the entrance.

Do not search for the Elytra yet. Return through the complete corridor to the city cover and cross back to the marked ship entrance once. Set the checkmark inside only when the route is enclosed throughout, both ends are sealed around the opening, and both crossings were controlled.
task.firsttorch.17b4deb5a8428aa8.title: 256 End Stone held together before the protected crossing
task.firsttorch.7fe2a06feb0df6ec.title: 16 Torches held together for the enclosed route
task.firsttorch.7a79b82f2ccc4e29.title: Boarded one enclosed ship space and tested the corridor both ways
Goal: find the ship room where Elytra is displayed in an Item Frame, secure the room, and stop before removing it.

Mark the bridge entrance and search only one enclosed ship section at a time. End Ships contain ordinary treasure chests and a Brewing Stand with healing potions as well as the Elytra room. Collecting those supplies is optional; never keep a container screen open while a Shulker or bullet remains active.

Recognise the goal by one Elytra displayed in an Item Frame between two Chests. A Shulker guards this room. Stop at the doorway, inspect every surface, and use the doorframe as solid cover. Attack when the shell opens, then retreat and reassess after every shot or strike.

After the Shulker is defeated, wait for all bullets and Levitation to end. Close any dangerous opening with End Stone, leave a low covered corner beside the doorway, and keep the route from the frame back to the bridge clear. Do not step onto an outside deck or the bow to collect the Dragon Head.

Set the checkmark while the Elytra is still visible in its frame, the room is quiet, and you can point to the marked doorway leading back through the protected corridor.
task.firsttorch.188e58ccc96170ba.title: Secured the framed Elytra and its route back to the city
Recover and Pack the First Elytra

Goal: remove the Elytra from its Item Frame, collect it, and pack it for the return without attempting a first flight.

Recheck the secured room and close the two Chest screens. Stand directly in front of the framed Elytra with solid floor beneath it. Press Attack once on the displayed item, then immediately pick up the dropped Elytra. Do not keep striking the empty frame or move towards an outside edge.

The item task completes automatically while the Elytra is in your inventory, and the Vanilla Sky's the Limit advancement should appear. Wait for the quest task to complete before storing the item. This confirms that the Elytra itself, rather than only the frame, was collected.

Do not equip the Elytra in the Chestplate slot and do not jump from the ship. Elytra only glide after a jump into open air, lose durability during flight, and do not provide the armour protection of a Chestplate. Those controls belong on a low protected practice platform after returning home.

Place the collected Elytra in the Shulker Box or a protected normal inventory slot. Keep the equipped Chestplate on, close every container, and confirm that Shield, Milk, Water, food, blocks, Pickaxe, and Pearls remain accessible. Set the checkmark only when the Elytra is packed and the marked exit is clear.
task.firsttorch.356f4d35e1e1772d.title: First Elytra collected into the inventory
task.firsttorch.2f3457d87f79cb5e.title: Elytra packed unequipped with the ship exit clear
Return the Elytra to the Overworld

Goal: carry the Elytra from the End Ship through the city, both Gateways, and the central exit portal to a protected Overworld location.

Leave the Elytra packed and keep the Chestplate equipped. Cross the enclosed ship corridor, descend the marked city route one landing at a time, and recover at the outside staging point. Then follow the established island markers back to the outer-island Gateway without using Chorus Fruit as a shortcut.

At the outer Gateway, stand on the secured platform and throw one Ender Pearl into the Gateway block. After returning near the main island, orient yourself before moving and follow the known route to the Bedrock exit fountain. Use the same safe access built after the Dragon fight and enter the starry exit surface.

You return to your valid respawn point or, if none remains, the world spawn. Move to protected ground before opening containers. Take the Elytra out of the Shulker Box to check that you brought it home; the automatic task only records possession, then store it in a protected Chest until the practice platform is ready.

Set the checkmark in the Overworld only after the Elytra item task is complete, the Elytra is safely stored, and all other expedition loot is accounted for. Do not equip it for an unplanned test from a roof, cliff, or tower.

Reward: 10 experience points for bringing the Elytra home without risking it on the return journey.

The automatic item check records possession and can already be complete before returning home. It does not verify your dimension or storage. Confirm the separate return task only after completing the journey and storing the Elytra as described.
task.firsttorch.5094b556a34332a6.title: Elytra collected into the inventory
task.firsttorch.58b24b045c620e3e.title: Returned home and stored the Elytra before the first glide
