Recipe: one Paper and one Gunpowder make three short, non-explosive Rockets.
quest.firsttorch.flight.7e16d835774fbb8b: Build a Low Elytra Practice Course

Goal: build a guarded launch only four blocks above a long, clear water landing. Bring the Elytra, 64 Cobblestone, eight Ladders, and a Water Bucket; keep the Elytra stored and Chestplate equipped while building. Choose calm water at least 12 blocks wide and 64 blocks long; avoid trees, cliffs, ice, Bubble Columns, Boats, and hostile creatures. Build a five-by-five Cobblestone floor four blocks above the water, with rear Ladder access, guards on the rear and sides, and a centred two-block opening over water. Light the shore and mark an exit. Confirm the entire platform, lane, and exit are clear.
task.firsttorch.1131cb8f5101928d.title: Elytra present but kept stored while building
task.firsttorch.4439e39cb10982eb.title: 64 Cobblestone held together before construction
task.firsttorch.322bf357452ea2dd.title: Eight Ladders held together for protected access
task.firsttorch.25f213727211cb07.title: One Water Bucket for repairing the landing area
task.firsttorch.17e6b24be366abe6.title: Built and inspected the four-block-high water course
quest.firsttorch.flight.0966d49700aa5e61: Goal: activate the Elytra once from the low platform and land in water without a Rocket. Start with full Health and Hunger; clear the water lane and store all Rockets away. Equip the Elytra, walk through the opening, and press Jump once after falling starts. Keep the view steady and make only a shallow straight descent. Water catches a missed activation. After landing, leave the water, restore the Chestplate, and inspect durability. Reward: 5 experience points.
task.firsttorch.25f226b6211434b8.title: Completed one straight unpowered glide into water
quest.firsttorch.flight.1b3d290417098234: Goal: repeat three unpowered launches with gentle corrections and a durability check after each landing. Stay straight first, then make one small turn to each side while remaining over the water centre. Do not climb, dive, turn sharply, or return to the platform. After every landing, leave the water, replace the Chestplate, and inspect the Elytra; stop when its bar is low. Phantom Membranes on an Anvil repair it; Unbreaking slows wear and Mending uses experience. Reward: 5 experience points.
task.firsttorch.48d3a3f10cc107a4.title: Completed three controlled glides with water landings and durability checks
quest.firsttorch.flight.2725d027767cbda7: Goal: craft the simple three-Rocket batch for the first assisted glide. Combine one Paper and one Gunpowder in any separate crafting slots. Use only this one-Gunpowder recipe. Extra Gunpowder gives longer flight duration; a Firework Star creates an explosion and can damage an Elytra user. The item task cannot distinguish explosive Rockets, so inspect all three tooltips for Flight Duration 1 and no explosion effects before confirming.
task.firsttorch.6727bd3897f03fdd.title: One Paper for the simple Rocket recipe
task.firsttorch.231e117827efc5b6.title: One Gunpowder for the shortest flight duration
task.firsttorch.44ed893d56a87827.title: Three Firework Rockets held together
task.firsttorch.5bae0e619d599cce.title: Confirmed Flight Duration 1 with no explosion effects
quest.firsttorch.flight.169041f4bcbcb2eb: Use One Rocket during a Safe Glide

Goal: use exactly one simple Rocket during an already active glide and land in the clear water lane. Recheck water, Health, Hunger, and durability. Store two Rockets and the Chestplate, equip the Elytra, activate the glide from the opening, then press Use once. Keep the view just below the horizon; do not pull up, dive, turn back, or chase the far shore. Land in water, restore armour on shore, inspect durability, and store the equipment. Reward: 10 experience points.
task.firsttorch.5391a84dd985f62a.title: Used one simple Rocket during a glide and landed safely in water
quest.firsttorch.flight.3eddd04cf6eefe1d: Goal: know when to stop flying, how repairs work, and why the Chestplate remains part of the kit. Inspect durability before launch and after landing; an Elytra stops working at one durability and a lost glide can be fatal. Repair damaged wings with Phantom Membranes on an Anvil; Unbreaking reduces wear and Mending uses collected experience. Elytra use the Chestplate slot and give no armour. Change equipment only on secure ground, never while gliding.
task.firsttorch.0fd7748ee22de66e.title: Elytra available for the maintenance check
task.firsttorch.326b559804aa02ca.title: Durability, repair, and Chestplate routine understood
quest.firsttorch.flight.2489570fa33801e3: Goal: prepare a short Overworld route with known destination, emergency landings, and return reserve. Pick a visible waypoint 250–500 blocks from home, record both coordinates, survey the route, and choose two safe landing areas. Bring 16 simple non-explosive Rockets, eight Bread, a Water Bucket, Elytra, and Chestplate; reserve at least half the Rockets for returning. Do not use this first route above the Void, Lava, tall mountains, dense unknown forest, or open ocean.
task.firsttorch.133eb2f483665786.title: 16 simple Firework Rockets held for the round trip
task.firsttorch.721821d64c148fef.title: Eight Bread held for the route
task.firsttorch.57f32a6dfeb3f6d4.title: One Water Bucket held for emergency ground safety
task.firsttorch.795d3a95140190cf.title: Coordinates, route, landings, and return reserve planned
quest.firsttorch.flight.58ae2c09c8263482: Goal: deliberately end a practice flight early instead of using more speed to rescue a poor approach. Use the familiar water course or surveyed route with full Health, Hunger, and sufficient durability. Use at most one simple Rocket; stop boosting as soon as direction, landing area, or return reserve is uncertain. Descend gently to broad Water or a clear field. After landing, restore the Chestplate and then check supplies. A safe early landing is success. Reward: 5 experience points.
task.firsttorch.2bd6ede9d13fb430.title: Ended one flight early and restored armour on safe ground
quest.firsttorch.flight.3e4d819ba0dff522: Goal: complete the prepared round trip. Fly in daylight along the surveyed route, using short separated boosts while a safe landing remains visible. Spend no more than eight of the 16 Rockets before the waypoint; abort and return on foot if the route or reserve becomes uncertain. At the waypoint, land, restore the Chestplate, check durability and reserve, and compare coordinates. Return only when supplies remain sufficient; land near home and store remaining Rockets. This completes the guided course. Reward: 10 experience points.
task.firsttorch.32bf3b243563e663.title: Completed the planned waypoint landing and safe return home
quest.firsttorch.and_now.3c3122df5c0ea19: You survived, built supplies, crossed the Nether, defeated the Dragon, returned from an End City, and learned safe flight. Minecraft has no single final task: choose a direction, prepare for hazards, record the way home, observe before acting, and retreat while you can. The following cards are optional reading, not a completion list. Set the checkmark when you are ready to choose your own goal.
task.firsttorch.72c95ccafc3f3a16.title: Ready to choose an independent goal
quest.firsttorch.and_now.009d0c967474731: Desert Pyramids can hide TNT beneath the centre: enter from the side and remove the pressure plate before opening Chests. Jungle Temples use Tripwires and Arrow Dispensers; disarm traps from cover. Trail Ruins are buried: make a controlled staircase and Brush Suspicious Gravel rather than breaking it. This card is optional reading; no visit is required.
task.firsttorch.25b14938b9673b9f.title: Read the temple and archaeology warnings
quest.firsttorch.and_now.419fc369ad62095: Shipwrecks and Ocean Ruins require air, visibility, food, a Boat, blocks, and a shore return. Dig Buried Treasure by a broad stair, not a trap-like hole. Ocean Monuments have Guardians and Elder Guardians; break beam line of sight and plan breathing, cover, milk, a marked exit, and retreat. This card is optional reading; no visit is required.
task.firsttorch.7aff2f0410bf29e9.title: Read the ocean exploration warnings
quest.firsttorch.and_now.5afe972108c13b4: Pillager Outposts expose you to Crossbows: observe from cover and keep a retreat. Do not drink an Ominous Bottle near a Village unless you choose a raid. Mansions are dark and confusing; Vindicators, Evokers, and Vexes need strong armour, Shield, range, light, food, blocks, marked junctions, and a distant safe Bed. This card is optional reading; no visit is required.
task.firsttorch.50225bfafb16f710.title: Read the raider and mansion warnings
quest.firsttorch.and_now.0bf75245596e694: Trial Chambers combine rooms, traps, Vaults, and Trial Spawners. Breezes use strong knockback, so edges and open entrances matter. Secure one room at a time, make a rest point outside the active room, and know the route out. Ordinary Trial Keys give individual Vault rewards. Save Ominous variants until the ordinary chamber is understood. This card is optional reading; no visit is required.
task.firsttorch.37c1c4c9a054b116.title: Read the Trial Chamber warnings
quest.firsttorch.and_now.30c7bd69eb7be64: Ancient Cities lie in the Deep Dark, where Sculk Sensors and Shriekers react to vibrations. Sneak and use Wool to dampen paths. The Warden is a survival danger, not a boss: its sonic attack reaches through blocks, so retreat before another warning. Bring Wool, food, healing, distractions, and a marked exit; the safest expedition may open no Chest. This card is optional reading.
task.firsttorch.0ab3d6e206dbd2dd.title: Read the Ancient City and Warden warnings
quest.firsttorch.and_now.23b4200152d3eae: A Wither can destroy nearby builds; never summon it at home. You can revisit End Cities, map biomes, learn Redstone, automate farms, build roads, collect music discs, or create a base. Keep First Torch habits: prepare to survive mistakes, change one thing at a time, preserve a way home, and stop when the situation is unclear. The course is already complete.
task.firsttorch.0acb79cc7f3defef.title: Chose a personal direction for the world

trophy.firsttorch.mob_drops.description: You completed the optional mob-drop practice.
image.firsttorch.hostile_mob_overview.de: Zombie, Skeleton, Spider, Creeper, and their common drops.
image.firsttorch.attack_indicator.descri: Partly charged and fully charged attack indicators.

quest.firsttorch.mob.prepare.title: Prepare a Safe Fight
quest.firsttorch.mob.prepare.description:
Optional goal: hold one Sword, one Shield, and two cooked foods in your inventory at the same time.

Mob is a general name for moving creatures in Minecraft. Hostile mobs attack you and may drop items when they die. These items are called mob drops.

If you do not have a Sword yet, the image shows an Iron Sword: place two Iron Ingots vertically and one Stick directly below them. Other Sword materials use the same shape; an existing Sword made from any ordinary material also counts.

Wear Armour, put the Shield in your offhand, and keep food ready. Clear a few inventory slots and choose a bright, open retreat to a door or another safe place before fighting.

Do not search for a group at night. Choose no more than one isolated enemy on open ground near your shelter. Abandon the fight if another enemy appears, your hearts fall, or the retreat becomes blocked.

Reward: Four Torches help keep the encounter area and retreat visible.
task.firsttorch.1e62c804bf375d1a.title: Hold 1 Sword made from an ordinary material
task.firsttorch.2f73d915c0486e2b.title: Hold 1 Shield
task.firsttorch.3084ea26d1597f3c.title: Hold 2 cooked foods
quest.firsttorch.mob.observe.title: Observe Before Deciding
quest.firsttorch.mob.observe.description:
Goal: learn the most common mob drops and dangers before choosing a fight.

Zombie: slow and dangerous only at close range. It usually drops Rotten Flesh. Zombies and Skeletons burn in direct daylight, but remain dangerous in shade.

Skeleton: shoots from a distance. It commonly drops Bones and Arrows, and occasionally a Bow. Raise the Shield toward the Skeleton and approach only when the route is safe.

Spider: fast, leaps while attacking, and climbs walls. It drops String and sometimes a Spider Eye. Eating a raw Spider Eye poisons you.

Creeper: approaches almost silently and explodes. It drops Gunpowder only when it dies without blowing itself up. Distance matters more than this drop.

The image shows a Zombie, Skeleton, Spider, and Creeper in that order. A common drop appears below each enemy; this does not mean that you must fight it now.

Attack with the left mouse button and briefly wait after each swing for the attack indicator to refill. Clicking continuously and rapidly deals much less damage with a Sword.

You may try each of the following four drop branches separately or skip dangerous ones. No main quest requires defeating all four enemies.

Reward: Two Bread as a reserve for optional practice.

The Zombie card shows the attack indicator and explains its two states.
task.firsttorch.63b71d59048ca26f.title: I know the danger and common drops of all four enemies
quest.firsttorch.mob.zombie.title: Zombie: Rotten Flesh
quest.firsttorch.mob.zombie.description:
Optional goal: collect one Rotten Flesh.

Choose only one isolated Zombie on open ground. Keep away from other enemies, attack with fully recovered swings, and step back between hits. The Shield helps when the Zombie comes close.

Eating Rotten Flesh may cause the Hunger effect, which drains your Hunger bar faster. Prefer your safe food and store the drop in a Chest for now.

The item in your inventory completes this optional task automatically. Do not follow the drop into a dark cave or toward a ledge.

On the left, the indicator is only partly filled: wait longer. On the right, the attack is fully ready; the small plus also appears while aiming at an attackable mob. If you cannot see this indicator, it may be disabled in the options or moved beside the hotbar.
task.firsttorch.26ea408c37bfd592.title: Own 1 Rotten Flesh
quest.firsttorch.mob.skeleton.title: Skeleton: Bones and Arrows
quest.firsttorch.mob.skeleton.descriptio:
Optional goal: collect one Bone.

Fight one isolated Skeleton where possible and use a wall, tree, or another solid object as cover. Raise the Shield toward the Skeleton while approaching. Lower it only briefly to attack, then raise it again.

Skeletons commonly drop Bones and Arrows; they sometimes leave a Bow too. Arrows visibly stuck in your character cannot be collected again.

One Bone in your inventory completes the task automatically and opens the Bone Meal step. Retreat instead of following a Skeleton across unknown ground.
task.firsttorch.480c62ae59d1f7b4.title: Own 1 Bone
quest.firsttorch.mob.spider.title: Spider: String and Spider Eyes
quest.firsttorch.mob.spider.description:
Optional goal: collect one String.

Fight a Spider only in a clear, visible area. Expect it to approach quickly, leap, and climb over low walls. Do not remain trapped in a tight corner.

Spiders drop String, which is later useful for Bows, Fishing Rods, and Wool among other things. A Spider Eye is a possible additional drop, but eating it raw poisons you.

One String in your inventory completes this optional task automatically.
task.firsttorch.6a2e84c07bf319d6.title: Own 1 String
quest.firsttorch.mob.creeper.title: Creeper: Gunpowder Without an Explosion
quest.firsttorch.mob.creeper.description:
Optional goal: collect one Gunpowder. No other quest depends on this one.

Attempt this only with one isolated Creeper on open ground and a clear retreat. Hit it once, immediately step back several blocks, and wait before approaching again. Do not run toward it while it hisses and flashes.

Create distance when the fuse begins. If escape is no longer enough, face the Creeper directly with the raised Shield; do not deliberately rely on surviving an explosion.

A Creeper that blows itself up leaves no Gunpowder. A defeated Creeper may drop Gunpowder, which is later used for Firework Rockets and other recipes.

One Gunpowder in your inventory completes this optional task automatically. Safety matters more than the checkmark.
task.firsttorch.0c51b7f3ae264d09.title: Own 1 Gunpowder
quest.firsttorch.mob.bone_meal.title: One Bone Becomes Three Bone Meal
quest.firsttorch.mob.bone_meal.descripti:
Goal: craft three Bone Meal from one Bone.

Open your inventory with E. Put one Bone in any slot of the small 2 × 2 crafting grid. The recipe is shapeless and does not require a Crafting Table.

Take the three Bone Meal from the result slot. They complete the task automatically and can accelerate the growth of suitable plants.

You now know two routes to the same item. Skeletons provide Bones quickly but require a dangerous fight. The Composter processes plant leftovers more slowly, but peacefully and renewably. Choose the route that suits your situation.

Reward: 5 XP points for your first fully understood mob drop.
task.firsttorch.2e73d915c0486f2b.title: Hold 3 Bone Meal in your inventory at the same time
chapter.firsttorch.bastion.title: Bastion Exploration (optional)
chapter.firsttorch.bastion.description: A dangerous optional Nether branch; it never unlocks later main-path lessons.
trophy.firsttorch.bastion.title: Bastion returned from
trophy.firsttorch.bastion.description: You completed the optional Bastion exercise.
image.firsttorch.bastion_remnant.descrip: A Bastion Remnant made of Blackstone.
quest.firsttorch.bastion.optional.title: Bastion Remnants Are Optional
quest.firsttorch.bastion.optional.descri:
Goal: consciously decide whether you want to begin the advanced Bastion path at all.

Bastion Remnants are large Blackstone structures with valuable but random loot. You need neither a Bastion for a Brewing Stand nor for Blaze Powder, Nether Wart, or the later path to the End.

Every Bastion contains Piglin Brutes. They always attack and no Gold Armour calms them. Ordinary Piglins initially remain neutral because of your Golden Helmet, but guarded containers and Gold blocks still make them angry together.

Bastions contain deep shafts, open bridges, Lava, and depending on their type also Hoglins or a Magma Cube Spawner. Their tangled structure makes a clear retreat substantially harder than inside a Nether Fortress.

You may leave this entire branch open permanently. Set the checkmark only if you understand that choice and want to at least read the following preparation step.
task.firsttorch.4ac7e176091c4381.title: I know that the Bastion is completely optional
quest.firsttorch.bastion.prepare.title: Prepare for the Bastion Journey
quest.firsttorch.bastion.prepare.descrip:
Goal: hold the minimum equipment for cautious Bastion exploration at the same time.

Bring a Sword and Pickaxe made from at least Iron or a better material, a Shield, 64 Cobblestone, and 16 substantial cooked foods. The automatic tasks consume nothing.

Continue wearing the Golden Helmet for ordinary Piglins. Chestplate, Leggings, and Boots must be at least Iron or better; Diamond equipment is strongly recommended for this advanced path. Heavily damaged pieces should be repaired or replaced.

A Bow with at least 64 Arrows and a Fire Resistance Potion are strongly recommended but not mandatory. Also bring Flint and Steel, at least 32 Torches, and additional Cobblestone for markers and fully enclosed cover.

Sleep before leaving, record portal and Bastion-route coordinates, begin with full Health and Hunger, and leave unnecessary valuables at home. Plan several short journeys instead of one long looting run.

Set the checkmark only while wearing the Golden Helmet plus at least an Iron Chestplate, Iron Leggings, and Iron Boots or better pieces, and after completing the additional checklist.
task.firsttorch.78afc92617a54283.title: Hold 1 Iron-or-better Sword
task.firsttorch.54148bc05ebd45d0.title: Hold 1 Iron-or-better Pickaxe
task.firsttorch.14d146623a394141.title: Hold 1 Shield
task.firsttorch.4e35081c01814be1.title: Hold 64 Cobblestone
task.firsttorch.15aa86345b664ddc.title: Hold 16 substantial cooked foods
task.firsttorch.63c39dfa6eec4313.title: Golden Helmet and at least Iron Armour worn; reserve checked
quest.firsttorch.bastion.recognise.title: Recognise a Bastion Remnant
quest.firsttorch.bastion.recognise.descr:
Goal: find a Bastion Remnant from a safe distance and distinguish it from a Nether Fortress.

Bastion Remnants are built mainly from black Blackstone, Polished Blackstone Bricks, and Gilded Blackstone. They look irregular and partly broken and may be deeply embedded in Netherrack. Nether Fortresses instead use dark-red Nether Bricks and long straight bridges.

The four types are Bridge, Hoglin Stables, Housing Units, and Treasure Room. You do not need to identify the type yet: each contains Piglin Brutes and each requires the same strict retreat rules.

Observe only from solid Cobblestone cover. Find a reachable outer edge with firm ground; do not drop inside from above or build an open bridge over Lava or a deep shaft.

Set the checkmark after you can distinguish Bastion and Fortress, have recorded the Bastion coordinates, and can show a completely marked route back to the portal shelter. Do not enter the structure yet.
task.firsttorch.3f9d7d5d79b54342.title: I found a Bastion from cover and checked the retreat
quest.firsttorch.bastion.edge.title: Secure the Outer Bastion Edge
quest.firsttorch.bastion.edge.descriptio:
Goal: build a closed Cobblestone room at the outer Bastion edge and then enter only the secured edge area.

Connect the room directly to your marked route home. It needs firm ground, a roof, full walls, a lit interior, and an exit that can immediately be closed with a full block. Record its coordinates.

Check the floor, ceiling, and both sides of the first area through a small opening. If you see or hear a Piglin Brute, a Hoglin, several Piglins, or Lava, close the opening and postpone entry.

Enter only a few safe blocks of the Bastion and immediately return to the room. The automatic advancement confirms that the game recognised the Bastion structure; the checkmark confirms your protected retreat room.

Set the checkmark inside the closed room. Do not explore a shaft, Treasure Room, or unknown side route yet.
task.firsttorch.06b993147a0c4e1c.title: Enter a Bastion Remnant for the first time
task.firsttorch.402abf971fe94b86.title: I am back inside the secured retreat room
quest.firsttorch.bastion.brutes.title: Brutes and Guarded Blocks
quest.firsttorch.bastion.brutes.descript:
Goal: before every loot attempt, explain which Piglins and blocks make the Golden Helmet ineffective.

The image again shows an adult ordinary Piglin, a Piglin Brute, a Baby Piglin, and a Zombified Piglin. The second enemy matters especially inside a Bastion: the dark-clothed Brute carries a Golden Axe and attacks immediately despite your Golden Helmet.

In Minecraft 26.1.2, Blocks of Gold, Raw Gold Blocks, Gilded Blackstone, and all Gold Ores are guarded. Barrels, Ender Chests, ordinary, Trapped, and Copper Chests, and Shulker Boxes are guarded too.

Nearby ordinary Piglins become angry when you open or break one of those blocks. The Golden Helmet does not prevent this reaction. A visible Chest is therefore never automatically a safe invitation.

Do not attack an enemy while your retreat is open. Fight an unavoidable Brute only alone from solid cover and never beside an edge. If several appear, close the route completely and return home.

Set the checkmark inside the retreat room when you can explain the difference between an ordinary Piglin and a Brute and name at least four types of guarded blocks.
task.firsttorch.50f984274598419e.title: I know Piglin Brutes and guarded blocks
quest.firsttorch.bastion.chest.title: Open at Most One Secured Chest
quest.firsttorch.bastion.chest.descripti:
Goal: optionally open exactly one Bastion Chest only after completely securing it.

This quest does not order you to reach a dangerous Chest at any cost. If there is no short route with firm ground and enclosed cover, leave it unopened and return on a later journey.

Build a closed Cobblestone area with a roof around yourself and the Chest. No Piglin or Hoglin may be inside it. Connect it to your retreat room through a passage that can be sealed, and keep Sword, Shield, blocks, and food ready.

Open the Chest with a right click and take only items for which you have inventory space. Bastion loot is random; no particular item is guaranteed. Do not mine Gold or Gilded Blackstone as additional loot.

After opening it, assume that ordinary Piglins outside are angry. Remain fully enclosed, close the route behind you, and return through the secured passage. Do not open a second Chest on the same journey.

Set the checkmark only inside the outer retreat room. If the protection was incomplete, the attempt does not count and you should return home immediately.
task.firsttorch.232d9aa60a8e408c.title: I opened exactly one completely secured Bastion Chest
quest.firsttorch.bastion.leave.title: Leave the Bastion Deliberately
quest.firsttorch.bastion.leave.descripti:
Goal: return safely through the retreat room, marked route, and original portal.

Check equipment, Health, and Hunger inside the outer room. Open the route home only if no enemy is waiting immediately outside. Close the room behind you and follow your Cobblestone markers without a shortcut.

Store the random loot at home. Keep the Bastion coordinates, but plan every later visit as another short journey with a fresh equipment check.

Set the checkmark in the Overworld only after returning safely. Ten experience points recognise the optional advanced exercise without bypassing later crafting lessons.
task.firsttorch.301286261c404a31.title: I returned safely from the Bastion to the Overworld
chapter.firsttorch.redstone_basics.title: Redstone Basics
chapter.firsttorch.redstone_basics.descr: A safe first circuit: power, distance, and three simple inputs.
trophy.firsttorch.redstone_basics.title: First circuit understood
trophy.firsttorch.redstone_basics.descri: You built and tested a simple Redstone circuit.
quest.firsttorch.redstone_basics.bench.d:
Goal: prepare a small, flat, well-lit Redstone test bench before building a circuit.

Reason: Redstone is easiest to understand when you can see every part and change only one thing at a time. Choose a safe place near your base, away from drops, water, fire, and monsters.

Steps: Make a flat floor from full solid blocks. Light the area, leave walking space around it, and keep your first circuit dry. Redstone Dust is the red line that carries a signal; it is not a machine by itself.

Common problem: Dust on uneven ground or beside half blocks is harder to read. Start again on one flat row of full blocks instead of trying to repair a confusing layout.

Proof: Set the checkmark after you have a safe, dry, lit, flat test bench with a clear row for the circuit.

Allow at least 19 blocks of length and three blocks of width on safe ground so the longer wire and a walking lane fit later. This entire Redstone chapter is optional; you do not need to complete more adventures for it.
task.firsttorch.20a0b0c0d0e00001.title: I prepared a safe, dry, lit, flat test bench
quest.firsttorch.redstone_basics.dust.de:
Goal: own 20 Redstone Dust.

Reason: Dust carries power between simple parts and lets you see how far a signal reaches.

Steps: Mine Redstone Ore with an Iron Pickaxe or a better Pickaxe in a safe, already-known mine, then collect the drops. A Stone or Wooden Pickaxe cannot harvest it. Bring light and use the marked route you already know.

Common problem: Do not make a dangerous new deep dive only for this lesson. If your route feels unsafe, return and use Redstone you already stored or come back after preparing properly.

Proof: 20 Redstone Dust in your inventory completes this task automatically.
task.firsttorch.20a0b0c0d0e00002.title: Own 20 Redstone Dust
quest.firsttorch.redstone_basics.parts.t: Craft a Lever and a Redstone Lamp
quest.firsttorch.redstone_basics.parts.d:
Goal: own one Lever and one Redstone Lamp.

Reason: A Lever is a switch that keeps a signal on or off. A Redstone Lamp makes that signal visible without needing any machinery.

Steps: In a Crafting Table, place one Stick directly above one Cobblestone to craft a Lever. For a Redstone Lamp, place Glowstone in the centre and one Redstone Dust on each of its four cardinal sides: above, below, left, and right. Four Glowstone Dust in a 2 × 2 square make one Glowstone block. Use safe Glowstone Dust or Glowstone already stored from Nether supplies; do not mine overhead Glowstone where a fall or Lava could kill you.

Common problem: Diagonal Dust does not make the lamp recipe. Check that the Glowstone is in the centre and the four Dust pieces touch its four sides.

Proof: One Lever and one Redstone Lamp in your inventory complete the two tasks automatically.

The Lamp recipe uses four of your 20 Dust. The remaining 16 are enough for the range test. Existing components also count; there is no need to craft duplicates.
task.firsttorch.20a0b0c0d0e00003.title: Own 1 Lever
task.firsttorch.20a0b0c0d0e00004.title: Own 1 Redstone Lamp
quest.firsttorch.redstone_basics.short_l: Light a Lamp Through Three Dust

Goal: build and test a short visible Redstone line.

Reason: This is the smallest useful circuit: an input sends power through Dust to an output.

Steps: On the same row of full solid floor blocks, place a Lever at x0, Redstone Dust at x1, x2, and x3, and a Redstone Lamp at x4. Turn the Lever on, then off. The Dust and Lamp should change together.

Common problem: The Lamp must touch the last Dust in the row; a gap, a different height, or a non-solid support breaks this simple test.

Proof: Set the checkmark only after your Lever → 3 Dust → Lamp row lights when the Lever is on and goes dark when it is off.

Reward: 5 XP points for the first working circuit.

Here x0 through x4 only number spaces in your row, not world coordinates: start at your bench and count from 0. Place the parts on the floor with the right mouse button and right-click the Lever to operate it. Switch on, observe the brighter red wire and lit Lamp, then switch off. Wait briefly for the Lamp to go dark. Close the quest book during the test so single-player time can run.
task.firsttorch.20a0b0c0d0e00005.title: I tested Lever → 3 Dust → Lamp: on lights it, off darkens it
quest.firsttorch.redstone_basics.range.d:
Goal: see that a Redstone signal weakens along Dust and reaches only 15 Dust pieces from a source.

Reason: Knowing this limit prevents a long line from failing mysteriously.

Steps: Extend the row: Lever at x0, Dust at x1 through x16, Lamp at x17. Turn the Lever on. The first Dust has strength 15 and the last Dust has strength 0, so the Lamp does not light. Then remove the Dust at x16 and move the Lamp to x16, directly beside Dust x15. It now lights from Dust x15 at strength 1.

Common problem: Do not leave the old Dust x16 under or beside the moved Lamp. Count from the Lever, not from the Lamp.

Proof: Set the checkmark only after you saw the Lamp stay dark at x17 and then light after removing Dust x16 and moving the Lamp to x16.
task.firsttorch.20a0b0c0d0e00006.title: I saw the 16th Dust fail, then the Lamp light beside Dust 15
Compare a Lever, Button, and Pressure Plate

Goal: compare a continuous switch, a short pulse, and a player-operated floor input.

Reason: Circuits need the right kind of signal. A Lever stays on; a Stone Button sends only a short pulse; a Stone Pressure Plate is on while a player stands on it.

Steps: Craft one Stone Button from one regular Stone; this recipe is shapeless. Craft one Stone Pressure Plate from two regular Stone placed horizontally. For each experiment, reset the Lever to off and remove the old source before placing the next one. Put each input directly adjacent to, or on, the same Redstone Lamp so no Dust or machinery is needed. Click the Lever and observe continuous power. Click the Button and observe its brief lamp flash. Place the Pressure Plate on the floor beside a Lamp at the same level, step on it, then step off. Use sneak/crouch only when you need to place a block rather than interact with the Lamp or input.

Common problem: If the lamp remains powered, an old Lever or another source is still connected. Turn it off and remove it before testing the next input.

Proof: Own the Button and Pressure Plate, then set the checkmark only after you observed the Lever stay on, the Button pulse, and the floor Plate turn the adjacent Lamp on while you stand on the Plate and off after you step away.

Reward: 5 XP points for choosing inputs by behaviour.

Smelt Cobblestone in a Furnace to obtain ordinary Stone; Smooth Stone is a different item. For an unambiguous setup, first place the Lever on top of the Lamp and right-click it. Remove it, attach the Button to the side of that Lamp and right-click the Button. Then remove the Button and place the Pressure Plate on a full floor block immediately beside the Lamp. The Plate sits at the Lamp's floor level, not on top of it. Observe every experiment with the quest book closed.
task.firsttorch.20a0b0c0d0e00007.title: Own 1 Stone Button
task.firsttorch.20a0b0c0d0e00008.title: Own 1 Stone Pressure Plate
task.firsttorch.20a0b0c0d0e00009.title: I tested continuous Lever, Button pulse, and Plate under my feet
chapter.firsttorch.redstone_repeaters.de: Extend a signal, control its direction, and choose a deliberate delay.
trophy.firsttorch.redstone_repeaters.des: You directed, refreshed, and delayed a Redstone signal with Repeaters.
quest.firsttorch.redstone_repeaters.craf:
Goal: hold two Redstone Repeaters in your inventory.

A Repeater renews a weak signal, sends it in one direction and adds an adjustable delay.

For two, you need 6 ordinary Stone, 6 Redstone Dust and 4 Sticks in total. First craft four Redstone Torches: one Dust above one Stick each. This uses four Dust and leaves two. Then, for each Repeater at a Crafting Table, put three ordinary Stone across the bottom row, two Redstone Torches at the left and right of the middle row, and one remaining Dust between them.

Smelt Cobblestone to obtain ordinary Stone. Smooth Stone is a different item and does not work here. Existing Repeaters count too; you do not need duplicates.

Proof: two Repeaters in your inventory are detected automatically.
task.firsttorch.21a0b0c0d0e00001.title: Hold 2 Redstone Repeaters
quest.firsttorch.redstone_repeaters.dire:
Goal: see that a Repeater accepts a signal only at its back and sends it from its front.

Reason: direction prevents a line from feeding backward or receiving an accidental side input.

Steps: on one same-level solid floor row, place a Lever at relative place 0, a Repeater at 1, and a Lamp at 2. The Repeater's fixed Torch end faces the Lamp; its sliding Torch end faces the input Lever. Right-click the Lever: the Lamp lights. Turn the Repeater around, test that it has no output, then return it to the correct direction. Do not attach a side input.

Common problem: the two Torch ends look similar. The fixed Torch points toward the Lamp; the movable/sliding Torch points toward the Lever.

Proof: mark complete after you tested correct direction, reverse direction, and restored correct direction. These are relative place numbers, not world coordinates.

To reverse it, break the Repeater, move to the opposite side and place it again while facing the opposite way. Right-clicking an already placed Repeater changes its delay, not its direction. Close the quest book while observing. All following position numbers count spaces along your test row, not world coordinates.
task.firsttorch.21a0b0c0d0e00002.title: I tested the Repeater forwards, backwards, then forwards again
quest.firsttorch.redstone_repeaters.rang:
Goal: use a powered Repeater to restore a signal for another 15 Dust.

Reason: Dust alone fades after 15 pieces; a Repeater starts a fresh full-strength section.

Steps: make a 22-long, 3-wide, dry, lit, safe solid-floor area. On one row place Lever 0, Dust 1–15, Repeater 16, Dust 17–19, Lamp 20. Turn on the Lever and see the Lamp light. Replace the Repeater with Dust: it fails. Restore the powered Repeater and see the Lamp light again.

Common problem: an uneven carrier block or an old extra connection hides the result. Keep this one straight row and compare only the Repeater with one Dust.

Proof: mark complete after seeing failure with Dust at 16 and success with the powered Repeater. Place numbers are relative to this exercise, not world coordinates.
task.firsttorch.21a0b0c0d0e00003.title: I compared Dust failure with a powered Repeater restoring the line
quest.firsttorch.redstone_repeaters.dela:
Goal: observe and choose the Repeater delay.

Reason: a delay lets a circuit wait visibly; it is not a clock or a loop.

Steps: align Lever 0, Repeater 1, Repeater 2, Lamp 3. Start with both Repeaters at their short/default one-tick setting. Toggle the Lever on and off and wait for the Lamp to settle. Then right-click each Repeater three times from its new default, making each four ticks; the slider spacing moves farther apart. Toggle again and compare about 0.2 s total with about 0.8 s at nominal 20 TPS (one Redstone tick is 0.1 s).

Common problem: if you lose track, break and replace a Repeater to reset it, then count three clicks. Do not build loops or clocks.

Proof: mark complete after both comparisons, then leave the Lever off. Reward: 5 experience.

For these timings compare switching ON from a fully unlit Lamp. On switching off the Lamp itself adds a short wait; that is not another Repeater. Timings assume normal game speed. Start with two freshly placed Repeaters and wait for each change to settle before switching again. Observe with the quest book closed.
task.firsttorch.21a0b0c0d0e00004.title: I compared the short and four-tick Repeater delays and left the Lever off
Read a Chest's contents and build one precise status display.
trophy.firsttorch.redstone_comparators.d: You used a Comparator to read a Chest and display this exercise's two-stack status.
quest.firsttorch.redstone_comparators.cr:
Goal: hold one Comparator, one Chest, and 15 Redstone Dust.

Reason: the Comparator reads a container's fullness and can pass that strength into Dust.

Steps: craft the Comparator with 3 Stone along the bottom, Nether Quartz in the centre, and Redstone Torches at upper-centre, middle-left, and middle-right. Craft a Chest with 8 Planks in a ring, leaving the centre empty. Use already stored Nether Quartz; do not make a new hazardous trip for it.

Common problem: the Comparator needs three Torches, not two, and the Chest centre stays empty.

Proof: all three inventory tasks complete automatically.
task.firsttorch.22a0b0c0d0e00001.title: Hold 1 Redstone Comparator
task.firsttorch.22a0b0c0d0e00002.title: Hold 1 Chest
task.firsttorch.22a0b0c0d0e00003.title: Hold 15 Redstone Dust
quest.firsttorch.redstone_comparators.re: Read One Item from a Chest

Goal: see a Comparator read a Chest's very small fullness signal.

Reason: a Comparator can turn stored contents into a Redstone strength.

Steps: place Chest 0, Comparator 1, Dust 2, Dust 3, Lamp 4 in a straight same-level row. The Comparator's rear two Torches face the Chest; its front single Torch faces the Lamp. Keep comparison mode: the front small Torch is OFF (right-click toggles it). Add no side inputs and no old Lever. With an empty Chest output is 0. Add one Cobblestone: output is 1, so first Dust is on, second Dust is off, and the Lamp stays off.

Common problem: a lit front small Torch means subtraction mode, not comparison mode. Right-click to turn it off.

Proof: mark complete after observing empty 0 and one Cobblestone's one-Dust signal.

Use one ordinary single Chest with 27 slots and no second Chest directly beside it. Support every component with full solid floor blocks; leave room above the Chest to open it. Sneak while placing the Comparator on the floor beside the Chest to avoid opening the Chest instead. Check the Torch direction afterwards. Remove old wires and signal sources. Close the Chest and quest book after each content change so you can see the wire and game time runs.
task.firsttorch.22a0b0c0d0e00004.title: I observed empty output 0 and one Cobblestone lighting only the first Dust
quest.firsttorch.redstone_comparators.fu:
Goal: compare one and two full Cobblestone stacks in one ordinary single 27-slot Chest.

Reason: this display depends on stack fullness, not merely item count.

Steps: hold 128 Cobblestone. Put only Cobblestone in the Chest: 64 in one slot gives output 1; 128 in two full slots gives output 2. Then Dust 2 and Dust 3 are on and the Lamp is on. Remove every item: output is 0 and the Lamp is off. Do not use loot, another Chest adjacent to it, or any other items; you do not need to fill the whole Chest.

Common problem: two stacks do not necessarily mean 128 items. Check their quantities and use two stacks of 64 for the comparison.

Proof: mark complete after seeing 64 → 1, 128 → 2 with both Dust and Lamp on, then empty → 0.

Remove the single Cobblestone from the previous exercise before the 64-item comparison: the totals must be exactly 64, then exactly 128. The two Dust pieces weaken the signal: at output 2 they have strength 2 and 1, so a signal still reaches the Lamp. Splitting the same total of the same item across slots does not change fullness; full stacks simply make counting easier.
task.firsttorch.22a0b0c0d0e00005.title: Hold 128 Cobblestone
task.firsttorch.22a0b0c0d0e00006.title: I tested empty, one full stack, two full stacks, then empty again
quest.firsttorch.redstone_comparators.di:
Goal: verify your small supply indicator and leave the test area switched off.

Repeat with the same single Chest: empty → exactly 128 Cobblestone → empty. The Lamp must show off → on → off. Then retrieve every item and remove wires and switches you no longer need.

Important: this is not a universal empty/full indicator. A partly filled Chest can already light it. With Cobblestone only, this setup turns on at 124 items; 128 is simply our easy-to-count test amount. Different items, especially those with other stack limits, or a double Chest change its meaning.

Proof: confirm all three states worked, you can explain the meaning, and the Chest is empty again. Reward: 5 XP points.
task.firsttorch.22a0b0c0d0e00007.title: I reset the Chest empty and can state this lamp's exact two-full-stack meaning
chapter.firsttorch.redstone_pistons.desc: Push and pull one block safely with a controlled Redstone input.
trophy.firsttorch.redstone_pistons.title: Motion Controlled
trophy.firsttorch.redstone_pistons.descr: You safely pushed and pulled one block with Pistons.
Goal: hold one Piston.

Reason: a Piston moves blocks when powered.

Steps: at a Crafting Table place 3 Planks across the top, Cobblestone at middle-left and middle-right, an Iron Ingot in the centre, then Cobblestone, Redstone Dust, Cobblestone across the bottom.

Common problem: this is a safe one-block lesson, not a blind attempt to move a valuable build.

Proof: one Piston in your inventory completes automatically.
task.firsttorch.23a0b0c0d0e00001.title: Hold 1 Piston
quest.firsttorch.redstone_pistons.push.d:
Goal: use a Piston to push one Cobblestone block once.

Reason: a powered Piston extends and moves the block directly in front of its wooden face.

Steps: use a dry, lit, flat solid floor with no entities, homes, Chests, or valuable blocks nearby. In one relative row place Piston base 0 with its wooden head toward 1, Cobblestone 1, and leave 2 clear. Put a Lever on TOP of the base by sneaking and right-clicking. Stand aside; right-click the Lever on to push the block to 2, then off. It stays at 2.

Common problem: a Piston must be horizontal. Before powering, inspect its wooden face; break and replace it until it faces 1. Placement normally faces the player, so stand in front of 2, look toward base 0 at eye level, and place it. Right-click does not rotate an already placed Piston.

Proof: mark complete after this single block reaches 2 and remains there with the Lever off. The place numbers are relative to this test, not world coordinates. A Piston can push at most 12 blocks, and not every block is movable; do not make an unsafe blind attempt.

If the Piston faces upward, remove it while unpowered and place it again from at least three blocks away in front of the intended wooden face. Check the actual wooden face before attaching the Lever. Close the quest book for the experiment so game time runs.
task.firsttorch.23a0b0c0d0e00002.title: I safely pushed one Cobblestone block and left the Lever off
quest.firsttorch.redstone_pistons.sticky:
Goal: hold one Sticky Piston.

Reason: its green Slime head can pull back the block it pushed.

Steps: at a Crafting Table place one Slimeball directly above one Piston. The recipe uses one of each. Your earlier Piston objective stays completed even though this recipe consumes that Piston.

Common problem: small Slimes can drop Slimeballs, but not every kill does; larger Slimes split first. Do not let them swarm you. Use stored Slimeballs when possible, wait for a safe source if none is available, and do not force a Nether trip for this optional lesson.

Proof: one Sticky Piston in your inventory completes automatically.
task.firsttorch.23a0b0c0d0e00003.title: Hold 1 Sticky Piston
quest.firsttorch.redstone_pistons.pull.d:
Goal: compare a Sticky Piston's return movement with an ordinary Piston.

The ordinary Piston left the Cobblestone behind. In this experiment the green face pulls it back because we operate the Lever slowly and deliberately.

Remove the previous Piston and Lever with the power off. Place the Sticky Piston at position 0 with its green face horizontal towards 1. Place one Cobblestone at 1 and leave 2 clear. Place the Lever on top of the Piston base. Stand beside the movement lane and right-click it on. Wait at least one second: the Cobblestone is now at 2. Switch off and wait again; the block returns to 1.

Important: a very short pulse can produce different Sticky Piston behaviour and leave a block behind. That is why we use a maintained Lever state here, not an Observer yet. Remove other power sources and keep the movement lane clear.

Proof: confirm both the outward and return movement. Leave the Lever off. Reward: 5 XP points. Observe with the quest book closed.
task.firsttorch.23a0b0c0d0e00004.title: I waited for extension and saw the Sticky Piston pull Cobblestone back to 1
chapter.firsttorch.redstone_observers.de: Detect a nearby block change and read its brief output pulse.
trophy.firsttorch.redstone_observers.des: You used an Observer to detect a block change without making a loop.
quest.firsttorch.redstone_observers.craf:
Goal: hold an Observer in your inventory.

An Observer notices changes to the block directly in front of its face and sends a short Redstone pulse from the opposite side. It is not a motion detector for players walking nearby.

At a Crafting Table, fill the top and bottom rows with three Cobblestone each. In the middle row put Redstone Dust, Redstone Dust and Nether Quartz from left to right. You need 6 Cobblestone, 2 Redstone Dust and 1 Nether Quartz in total. Use safe existing supplies; this optional lesson does not require an unprepared Nether trip.

Do not confuse Cobblestone with the ordinary Stone used for Repeaters. An existing Observer also counts.

Proof: the Observer is detected automatically in your inventory.
task.firsttorch.24a0b0c0d0e00001.title: Hold 1 Observer
quest.firsttorch.redstone_observers.watc:
Goal: identify the watching face and the output side unambiguously.

On safe level full-block flooring, build a row: Cobblestone at position 0, Observer at 1, Redstone Lamp at 2. These numbers are spaces in your row, not world coordinates. The face with two eyes looks at the Cobblestone; the red dot on the back points at the Lamp. Break a wrongly oriented Observer and place it again from the opposite side. Right-clicking does not rotate it.

Remove old Levers and wires. Do not connect a Piston yet. Close the quest book and wait after construction until the Lamp has been dark for at least a second; placement can already cause a pulse.

From the side, break the existing Cobblestone at 0. The Lamp flashes briefly. Wait until it is dark again. Right-click to replace the Cobblestone at 0: another flash. Leave this block in place for the next task.

If nothing lights, first check the face and red dot, and that the Lamp directly touches the back. The watching face needs no Lever or wire.

Proof: confirm the two separate flashes on removal and replacement, with a dark pause between them.
task.firsttorch.24a0b0c0d0e00002.title: I saw one Lamp flash for placing and one for removing watched Cobblestone
quest.firsttorch.redstone_observers.chan:
Goal: distinguish a watched block-state change from a player simply moving nearby.

Steps: with the stable 0 → 1 → 2 setup, walk past the Observer face without changing block 0: the Lamp stays dark. Then remove Cobblestone 0 and wait for one flash; replace it and wait for one flash.

Common problem: this is not a claim that an Observer detects every world event or a farm lesson. It watches the block state directly in front of its face.

Proof: mark complete after no flash for walking and one settled flash for each block change.

Start with the Cobblestone from the previous lesson at 0 and a dark Lamp. Walk on the floor beside the row without operating switches or placing anything. Close the quest book for every observation and wait for the Lamp to go dark after each block change.
task.firsttorch.24a0b0c0d0e00003.title: I saw no flash for walking past, then flashes for removing and replacing Cobblestone
quest.firsttorch.redstone_observers.puls: Leave a Short Pulse Test Safe

Goal: distinguish a short pulse from a continuously switched-on Lever and leave the test area quiet.

An Observer does not keep the Lamp lit merely because a block stands in front of it. It briefly signals a detected change. Test one block change again, then wait without building: the Lamp turns off by itself.

Finally leave solid Cobblestone at 0, exactly one Observer at 1 and the dark Lamp at 2. If flashing continues, remove the Observer first and check other signal sources. Two suitably opposed Observers can repeatedly trigger each other. Do not build feedback yet: that means a connection whose output changes its own watched block again.

Remove the Observer first before rebuilding. Pistons and Observers remain separate experiments here; a proper machine comes later. Observe with the quest book closed.

Proof: confirm the single short pulse and the unchanged setup staying dark afterwards. Reward: 5 XP points.
task.firsttorch.24a0b0c0d0e00004.title: I left one stable Observer, a dark Lamp, and no feedback loop
chapter.firsttorch.redstone_door.title: Automatic Iron Door (Optional)
chapter.firsttorch.redstone_door.descrip: Build a safe two-way pressure-plate door in an open practice space.
trophy.firsttorch.redstone_door.title: Doorway Tested
trophy.firsttorch.redstone_door.descript: You built, tested, and safely cleared an automatic Iron Door practice setup.
quest.firsttorch.redstone_door.materials: Craft the Door and Two Plates

Goal: hold one Iron Door and two Stone Pressure Plates.

Reason: an Iron Door opens from Redstone power, and one plate on each side makes this practice doorway usable in both directions.

Steps: at a Crafting Table, place 6 Iron Ingots in two full vertical columns of three; this makes 3 Iron Doors. For each Stone Pressure Plate, place 2 regular Stone horizontally; two plates use 4 Stone total. Smelt Cobblestone to make regular Stone; Smooth Stone is different.

Common problem: the finished door and plates are checked, not consumed. Existing doors and plates count, so do not craft duplicates just to satisfy this lesson.

Proof: one Iron Door and two Stone Pressure Plates in your inventory complete automatically.
task.firsttorch.25a0b0c0d0e00001.title: Hold 1 Iron Door
task.firsttorch.25a0b0c0d0e00002.title: Hold 2 Stone Pressure Plates
quest.firsttorch.redstone_door.site.titl: Make a Safe Open Door Practice Site
quest.firsttorch.redstone_door.site.desc:
Goal: choose and build a safe practice doorway before adding pressure plates.

Reason: an automatic door should be easy to inspect from either side, not trap you or protect your home by itself.

Steps: use solid, flat, well-lit ground with open walking space all around. Leave two clear blocks of height for the Iron Door. Put it on a full solid floor block, with room to walk around both sides. This is a practice opening, not your sole exit and not a secure home entrance.

Common problem: do not build into a wall, a narrow tunnel, water, a drop, or a monster area. An Iron Door needs Redstone power; never use a Lever that leaves it permanently powered for this exercise.

Proof: close the quest book, place the door in the open practice site, and confirm you can safely walk around it on both sides.
task.firsttorch.25a0b0c0d0e00003.title: I made an open, two-block-high, walk-around practice doorway
quest.firsttorch.redstone_door.walk.titl: Open the Door from Both Sides
quest.firsttorch.redstone_door.walk.desc:
Goal: make the Iron Door open as you approach from either side.

Steps: place one Stone Pressure Plate immediately in front of the closed door and one immediately behind it, each on a full solid floor block. The three floor positions form a straight line: plate, door, plate. Do not put them beside the hinges or leave a gap. Close the quest book, step on one plate, walk through the open door, then step on the other plate and walk back. Repeat once slowly so you see each plate power the door while something living stands on it. Step fully off both plates and wait a moment: the door should close after the plate releases.

Reason: two adjacent plates prevent this simple doorway from working only one way. Stone Pressure Plates detect living entities, including mobs; dropped items do not activate them.

Common problem: if the door does not open, first check that both plates are immediately in front of and behind the door and supported by full solid floor blocks. Remove old Levers, Dust, Buttons, and other signal sources before changing the layout.

Proof: confirm that you walked through and back, with each side's plate opening the door.
task.firsttorch.25a0b0c0d0e00004.title: I used both adjacent plates to walk through the door in both directions
quest.firsttorch.redstone_door.safe_fini: Troubleshoot and Leave the Door Safe

Goal: understand the limits of this small automatic door and leave the practice site safe.

Troubleshoot: if a plate does nothing, verify its full solid support and direct adjacency to the door. If the door stays open after you step fully off both plates and wait, check for animals on either plate and remove any Lever or other continuous power source. Do not add Observer pulses: a brief pulse is not a reliable way to hold a door open.

Mob safety: because Stone Pressure Plates detect living entities, a mob can open this door too. It is therefore never a secure home entrance, a sole exit, or a safety lock. Keep the surrounding practice space lit and open.

Cleanup: walk around both sides once more, collect stray Redstone parts, and leave no permanent power source or confusing old circuit. You may keep the simple two-plate door only in this safe open practice area.

Proof: confirm the door works, you can explain the mob limit, and the site is clear. Reward: 5 XP points.
task.firsttorch.25a0b0c0d0e00005.title: I checked the plates, removed permanent power, and left a safe clear practice site
chapter.firsttorch.field_animals.title: Field Guide: Animals
chapter.firsttorch.field_animals.descrip: Optional reading cards about animals and companions. Gold references open related lessons; use Back to previous quest to return to the entry.
trophy.firsttorch.field_animals.title: Animals noted
trophy.firsttorch.field_animals.descript: You read the animal reference cards.
quest.firsttorch.field_animals.cow.title: Cow
quest.firsttorch.field_animals.cow.descr:
Habitat and behaviour: ordinary adult Cows roam grassy Overworld areas and follow Wheat. Use an empty Bucket on an adult for Milk; this does not harm it.

Danger and safe approach: they are peaceful. Keep a pen and a clear exit rather than chasing animals over unknown ground.

Drops without Looting: an adult ordinary Cow always gives 1–3 Beef and may give 0–2 Leather when killed; babies give no adult loot. Fire can cook meat, but do not burn animals for this.

Usefulness: Beef is food, Leather supports books and gear, and Milk clears status effects, including helpful ones. Looting changes ordinary death drops, not milk.

This is information only: read it, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.26a0b0c0d0e00001.title: I have read the Cow entry
quest.firsttorch.field_animals.sheep.des:
Habitat and behaviour: Sheep roam grassy Overworld areas and follow Wheat. They are peaceful.

Danger and safe approach: approach calmly and keep a fenced, well-lit pen; do not force a trip through cliffs or hostile terrain.

Drops without Looting: an adult gives 1–2 Mutton when killed. Wool is only dropped on death if the Sheep is unsheared; babies give no adult loot.

Usefulness: Shears collect Wool without killing the Sheep. After eating grass, a sheared Sheep regrows its Wool, making it sustainable. Looting affects ordinary death drops, not shearing.

This is information only: read it, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.26a0b0c0d0e00002.title: I have read the Sheep entry
quest.firsttorch.field_animals.pig.title: Pig
quest.firsttorch.field_animals.pig.descr:
Habitat and behaviour: Pigs are peaceful Overworld animals. They follow Carrots, Potatoes, or Beetroot.

Danger and safe approach: lead them only along a known, safe route into a pen; do not turn an ordinary food animal into a reason to travel at night.

Drops without Looting: an adult ordinary Pig always gives 1–3 Porkchops when killed. Babies give no adult loot. Fire can cook meat, but do not burn animals for this.

Usefulness: Porkchops are food; breeding a protected pair provides a renewable supply. Looting can change ordinary death-drop counts.

This is information only: read it, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.26a0b0c0d0e00003.title: I have read the Pig entry
quest.firsttorch.field_animals.chicken.d:
Habitat and behaviour: Chickens are peaceful Overworld animals and follow Wheat Seeds and other Seeds.

Danger and safe approach: use a secure pen with room to collect items; avoid chasing a Chicken into danger.

Drops without Looting: an adult gives 1 Chicken and 0–2 Feathers when killed; fire can make the meat drop already cooked. Babies give no adult loot. Eggs are a separate live-animal resource, not a death drop.

Usefulness: Thrown Eggs can hatch chicks, and Eggs are also used in recipes; Feathers help make Arrows. A living flock can lay Eggs without being killed. Looting affects ordinary death drops, not eggs.

This is information only: read it, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.26a0b0c0d0e00004.title: I have read the Chicken entry
quest.firsttorch.field_animals.wolf.desc:
Habitat and behaviour: Wolves roam in some Overworld biomes. A tamed Wolf is your dog; there is no separate vanilla dog species. Wild Wolves normally do not attack unless provoked.

Safe handling: hold Bones and use them on a calm Wolf until hearts appear and it gains a collar; this may take several Bones. Use an empty hand and the Use control to make it sit safely at home before travel, so it does not follow you into a cave, water, or a fight.

Food and care: Wolves accept suitable meat and fish as food, but Bones are for taming, not ordinary feeding. Keep the distinction clear when preparing supplies.

Drops: Wolves have no natural item drops. Worn equipment is separate.

Usefulness: a dog can be a companion, but safety comes before bringing it on an expedition. Read, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.26a0b0c0d0e00005.title: I have read the Wolf entry
quest.firsttorch.field_animals.cat.title: Cat
quest.firsttorch.field_animals.cat.descr:
Habitat and behaviour: Cats can be found around villages. Move slowly toward one; rushing makes it back away. Do not confuse a Cat with an Ocelot, which is a different animal.

Safe handling: hold Raw Cod or Raw Salmon and let the Cat approach patiently. Feed it with the Use control; several fish may be needed. When hearts appear, the Cat is tamed; you can ask it to sit, which is useful at a safe home before you travel. Keep paths clear and do not corner it near danger.

Food and care: Raw Cod and Raw Salmon are the relevant taming foods. A tamed Cat is a companion, not a guaranteed source of presents; do not plan supplies around gifts.

Drops without Looting: an ordinary Cat may drop 0–2 String when killed. Looting does not increase this String amount.

Usefulness: a patient village companion is enough reason to keep it safe. Read, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.26a0b0c0d0e00006.title: I have read the Cat entry
quest.firsttorch.field_animals.horse.des:
Habitat and behaviour: Horses roam plains and savannas. They are useful mounts, but the first step is calm handling, not speed.

Safe handling: use an empty hand to mount repeatedly. A Horse may throw you off until hearts appear; then it is tamed. Put on a Saddle to control where it goes. Practise on level, familiar ground and dismount before steep edges.

Food and care: keep a safe enclosure and do not ride an untested route into ravines, deep water, or hostile ground. A fast mount can carry you into danger faster too.

Drops without Looting: an ordinary Horse may drop 0–2 Leather when killed. Looting can increase the Leather amount. Equipment is not part of those ordinary drops.

Usefulness: a tamed, saddled Horse makes planned travel easier. Read, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.26a0b0c0d0e00007.title: I have read the Horse entry
quest.firsttorch.field_animals.camel.des:
Habitat and behaviour: Camels are found in desert villages. A Saddled Camel can carry two riders, which makes it different from an ordinary Horse ride.

Safe handling: unlike a Horse, a Camel does not need repeated mounting to tame it. Add a Saddle when you are ready to ride, then practise on open, familiar ground before a longer trip. Keep a clear route and avoid drops or hostile areas.

Food and care: Cactus is used for Camel breeding. Keep planted Cactus away from the Camel pen and walking path, because its spines can hurt nearby creatures.

Drops: Camels have no natural item drops. A fitted Saddle is equipment, not natural loot.

Usefulness: a two-rider mount can help a pair travel together, but it still needs a safe route. Read, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.26a0b0c0d0e00008.title: I have read the Camel entry
quest.firsttorch.field_animals.axolotl.d:
Habitat and behaviour: Axolotls live in water in lush caves. They are aquatic animals and are not tamed like Cats or Wolves. Use a bucket for safe transport.

Safe handling: use a Water Bucket to capture and transport one. Prepare a filled-water habitat before releasing it; avoid leaving an Axolotl on dry land. Keep the route short and the water ready.

Food and care: a Bucket of Tropical Fish is for breeding Axolotls. Loose Tropical Fish are not the breeding item, so bring the filled bucket if breeding is your goal.

Drops: Axolotls drop no items when they die.

Usefulness: Axolotls attack fish, so keep them in a separate aquarium from fish you want to keep. Read, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.26a0b0c0d0e00009.title: I have read the Axolotl entry
chapter.firsttorch.field_overworld.title: Field Guide: Overworld Hostiles
chapter.firsttorch.field_overworld.descr: Optional reading cards about Overworld monsters. Gold references open related lessons; use Back to previous quest to return to the entry.
trophy.firsttorch.field_overworld.title: Overworld threats noted
trophy.firsttorch.field_overworld.descri: You read the Overworld hostile-mob reference cards.
Habitat and behaviour: Ordinary adult Zombies are slow melee enemies in dark Overworld areas. Baby Zombies are faster. Sunlight can burn Zombies, but shade or a helmet protects them: do not rely on daytime.

Danger and safe approach: use open ground, a clear retreat, and cover. Do not enter a crowd for drops.

Drops without Looting: Rotten Flesh may be 0–2. When the kill is credited to you, a rare Iron Ingot, Carrot, or Potato is possible, never guaranteed. This is a usual-drop summary, not every special variant.

Usefulness: Rotten Flesh is emergency food with risk; rare crop drops can start farming. Looting affects ordinary death drops.

This is information only: read it, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.27a0b0c0d0e00001.title: I have read the Zombie entry
quest.firsttorch.field_overworld.skeleto:
Habitat and behaviour: Skeletons are common hostile Overworld mobs that attack from range.

Danger and safe approach: use solid cover and raise a Shield toward the shooter; retreat instead of crossing unknown ground under arrows.

Drops without Looting: Bones and Arrows may each be 0–2. Equipment such as a Bow is possible, not guaranteed.

Usefulness: Bones make Bone Meal; Arrows support a Bow. Looting affects ordinary death drops.

This is information only: read it, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.27a0b0c0d0e00002.title: I have read the Skeleton entry
Habitat and behaviour: this entry is for an ordinary Spider, not a Cave Spider. It moves quickly, climbs walls, and is hostile in darkness; brightness is not a guaranteed safe approach.

Danger and safe approach: meet one only on clear ground with a retreat, never assume a low wall contains it.

Drops without Looting: String may be 0–2. A Spider Eye is only a possible player-credited drop.

Usefulness: String supports Bows, Fishing Rods, and Wool; raw Spider Eyes poison you. Looting affects ordinary death drops.

This is information only: read it, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.27a0b0c0d0e00003.title: I have read the Spider entry
quest.firsttorch.field_overworld.creeper:
Habitat and behaviour: Creepers are common hostile Overworld mobs that approach quietly and explode when close.

Danger and safe approach: distance and an open retreat matter more than any drop. Do not build a dangerous farm just for this entry.

Drops without Looting: Gunpowder may be 0–2 only if the Creeper is killed before it explodes. A Skeleton-family kill can conditionally produce a music disc.

Usefulness: Gunpowder helps make Firework Rockets and other recipes. Looting affects ordinary death drops.

This is information only: read it, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.27a0b0c0d0e00004.title: I have read the Creeper entry

chapter.firsttorch.field_nether.descript: Optional reading cards about Nether creatures. Gold references open related lessons; use Back to previous quest to return to the entry.
trophy.firsttorch.field_nether.title: Nether threats noted
trophy.firsttorch.field_nether.descripti: You read the Nether hostile-mob reference cards.
quest.firsttorch.field_nether.blaze.desc:
Habitat and behaviour: Blazes are dangerous flying enemies in Nether Fortresses, not Bastions. They use fireballs and melee attacks.

Danger and safe approach: take full cover behind a solid wall during fireballs; do not risk a bridge or a crowd.

Drops without Looting: when the kill is credited to you, a Blaze Rod may be 0–1; tamed-wolf credit counts. Looting can increase this.

Usefulness: Rods make Blaze Powder for brewing and Eyes of Ender.

This is information only: read it, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.28a0b0c0d0e00001.title: I have read the Blaze entry
quest.firsttorch.field_nether.wither_ske:
Habitat and behaviour: Wither Skeletons are tall melee enemies in Nether Fortresses. Their hits inflict Wither, not fire.

Danger and safe approach: a two-block-high retreat opening stops their taller body. Fire Resistance does not cure Wither; keep a marked route and return when damaged.

Drops without Looting: Bones may be 0–2 and Coal may be 0–1, so either can be absent. A Wither Skeleton Skull is a rare player-credited drop. Looting affects these ordinary drops.

Usefulness: Bones make Bone Meal; skulls are a later, hazardous goal, never a required fight here.

This is information only: read it, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.28a0b0c0d0e00002.title: I have read the Wither Skeleton entry
quest.firsttorch.field_nether.ghast.desc:
Habitat and behaviour: Ghasts are large flying Nether enemies that launch explosive fireballs. This means the hostile Ghast, not the friendly Happy Ghast.

Danger and safe approach: use a roof and solid Cobblestone cover; do not make a fight mandatory. A returned fireball can give player credit, but trying it is optional.

Drops without Looting: a Ghast Tear may be 0–1 and Gunpowder may be 0–2. Drops can be lost in Lava.

Usefulness: Tears support brewing; Gunpowder supports Rockets. Looting affects ordinary death drops.

This is information only: read it, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.28a0b0c0d0e00003.title: I have read the Ghast entry
quest.firsttorch.field_nether.magma_cube:
Habitat and behaviour: Magma Cubes are bouncing Nether enemies that split into smaller cubes. Even small cubes can damage you.

Danger and safe approach: keep firm ground and a retreat; do not treat the smallest size as harmless.

Drops without Looting: medium and large cubes may drop Magma Cream; small cubes drop none, even with Looting.

Usefulness: Magma Cream is a brewing ingredient. It can also be crafted from Blaze Powder and a Slimeball, so do not force a risky hunt. A Frog can eat a small Magma Cube and make Froglight, but this entry does not require transport.

This is information only: read it, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.28a0b0c0d0e00004.title: I have read the Magma Cube entry
chapter.firsttorch.field_end.title: Field Guide: End and Approach
