trophy.firsttorch.field_end.description: You read the End reference cards.
quest.firsttorch.field_end.enderman.desc:
Habitat and behaviour: Endermen are common in the End and also occur in the Overworld and Nether. Looking into their eyes or attacking can make them hostile.

Safety: avoid eye contact and stay on solid ground. A shelter with two blocks of clear headroom keeps their tall body outside; stay back from its edge. Never chase one towards the void.

Drops without Looting: 0–1 Ender Pearl, so a Pearl is not guaranteed. Looting can increase the amount; a carried block is separate.

Use: Pearls support travel and crafting Eyes of Ender. No fight is required: read, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.29a0b0c0d0e00001.title: I have read the Enderman entry
quest.firsttorch.field_end.shulker.title: Shulker
quest.firsttorch.field_end.shulker.descr:
Habitat and behaviour: Shulkers hide in End Cities. Their projectiles cause Levitation, which can leave you falling from a dangerous height.

Safety: prepare cover and a safe landing area before approaching. Milk removes Levitation but does not prevent fall damage; removing the effect high in the air is not a safe landing method.

Drops: each Shulker has a 50% base chance to drop one Shulker Shell. Looting raises that chance, not the number of shells from one Shulker.

Use: two shells and a Chest make a Shulker Box. Read, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.29a0b0c0d0e00002.title: I have read the Shulker entry
quest.firsttorch.field_end.silverfish.de:
Habitat and behaviour: Silverfish can emerge from infested blocks and a Stronghold portal-room spawner. They belong to the approach to the End, not its ordinary wildlife.

Safety: keep a retreat clear. Attacked Silverfish can bring more out of nearby infested blocks, so do not keep breaking blocks blindly in a crowded corridor.

Drops: no natural item drops. Recognising the threat is useful; fighting or farming them is not required for this card.

Read, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.29a0b0c0d0e00003.title: I have read the Silverfish entry
quest.firsttorch.field_end.endermite.des:
Habitat and behaviour: using an Ender Pearl can occasionally spawn a hostile Endermite. This is possible, not guaranteed, and can happen outside the End too.

Safety: choose a broad, secure landing site and check your surroundings after teleporting. Do not waste Pearls trying to create an Endermite or retreat towards a cliff when surprised.

Drops: no natural item drops. Its appearance is a travel hazard, not a resource requirement.

Use: knowing this possibility helps you plan a safer Pearl landing. Read, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.29a0b0c0d0e00004.title: I have read the Endermite entry
chapter.firsttorch.field_water.title: Field Guide: Aquatic Life
chapter.firsttorch.field_water.descripti: Optional water-creature reference cards. Some cards include clickable related references; use Back to return to the previous quest.
trophy.firsttorch.field_water.title: Aquatic life noted
trophy.firsttorch.field_water.descriptio: You read the aquatic reference cards.
quest.firsttorch.field_water.squid.title: Squid
quest.firsttorch.field_water.squid.descr:
Habitat and behaviour: Squid are peaceful animals in rivers and oceans.

Safety: watch your air supply and keep a clear route to the surface. Do not chase a Squid into deep or enclosed water just for its drops.

Drops without Looting: 1–3 Ink Sacs; Looting can increase the amount.

Use: Ink Sacs make Black Dye for decorative work. The animal does not need to be killed for this reading card. Read, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.2aa0b0c0d0e00001.title: I have read the Squid entry
Habitat and behaviour: Glow Squid are peaceful animals in dark underground water. Their bright appearance does not raise the surrounding light level or prevent hostile spawning.

Safety: use your own lighting and keep a route to air. Do not enter an underwater cave merely because a Glow Squid looks like a light source.

Drops without Looting: 1–3 Glow Ink Sacs; Looting can increase the amount.

Use: Glow Ink makes sign text easier to see and can make Glow Item Frames. These are visual effects, not room lighting. Read, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.2aa0b0c0d0e00002.title: I have read the Glow Squid entry
quest.firsttorch.field_water.dolphin.des:
Habitat and behaviour: Dolphins are social ocean animals. Do not hit them: nearby Dolphins can retaliate together.

Safety: Dolphins need water and access to surface air. Never seal one inside an entirely underwater tank or leave it stranded on land. Your own air matters too: Dolphin's Grace improves swimming but is not Water Breathing.

Drops without Looting: 0–1 Cod, with possible Looting increases. This is no reason to harm a useful living animal.

Use: swimming near Dolphins can help you move faster. Keep your route to the surface. Read, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.2aa0b0c0d0e00003.title: I have read the Dolphin entry
quest.firsttorch.field_water.turtle.desc:
Habitat and behaviour: Turtles live at beaches and move between sand and water. Protect their eggs from trampling and hostile creatures rather than rushing through a nesting area.

Safety: leave room for the animals and keep your own return route clear.

Drops without Looting: an adult can drop 0–2 Seagrass; Looting can increase it. Turtle Scutes instead come from baby Turtles growing into adults, not from killing Turtles.

Use: Scutes make a Turtle Shell helmet. Patient care, not hunting, produces this material. Read, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.2aa0b0c0d0e00004.title: I have read the Turtle entry
chapter.firsttorch.field_special.title: Field Guide: Special Encounters
chapter.firsttorch.field_special.descrip: Optional cards for unusual friendly or shy creatures. Some cards include clickable related references; use Back to return to the previous quest.
trophy.firsttorch.field_special.title: Special encounters noted
trophy.firsttorch.field_special.descript: You read the special encounter cards.
quest.firsttorch.field_special.bee.title: Bee
quest.firsttorch.field_special.bee.descr:
Habitat and behaviour: Bees visit flowers and return to a Bee Nest or Beehive. Pollen-carrying Bees can help crops grow.

Safety: do not hit Bees, break their home or harvest carelessly; they can become hostile and sting. Leave the colony undisturbed until you have prepared a safe harvesting setup.

Resources: Bees have no natural death drops. Honey and Honeycomb are harvested from a full nest or hive, not from killing Bees.

Use: a living colony supports crops and renewable materials. This card asks only for reading, not harvesting. Read, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.2ba0b0c0d0e00001.title: I have read the Bee entry
quest.firsttorch.field_special.fox.title: Fox
quest.firsttorch.field_special.fox.descr:
Habitat and behaviour: Foxes are shy Taiga animals; snowy areas have a white variant. They may carry food or another item in their mouth.

Safety: move slowly, leave an escape route and keep vulnerable farm animals protected. A Fox is not tamed with Bones like a Wolf.

Drops: no natural item drops. An item already carried in its mouth is separate, not a guaranteed resource produced by every Fox.

Use: observing its habits helps you protect animals and understand missing dropped items. No capture or breeding is required here. Read, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.2ba0b0c0d0e00002.title: I have read the Fox entry
quest.firsttorch.field_special.frog.desc:
Habitat and behaviour: Frogs live in Swamps and Mangrove Swamps. They can eat small Slimes and small Magma Cubes.

Safety: watch from firm ground and plan a safe route around water. This card does not ask you to transport Frogs into the Nether.

Resources: Frogs have no natural death drops. Eating a small Slime produces a Slimeball; eating a small Magma Cube produces a Froglight. These are feeding results, not loot from killing a Frog.

Use: Froglights are decorative light blocks. Learn the distinction without arranging a dangerous encounter. Read, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.2ba0b0c0d0e00003.title: I have read the Frog entry
quest.firsttorch.field_special.allay.des:
Habitat and behaviour: Allays can be imprisoned at Pillager Outposts or Woodland Mansions. Not every structure contains them.

Safety: these sites have dangerous inhabitants. This reference does not require a rescue trip; prepare the route and retreat before approaching one.

Use: give an Allay an example item, such as one Cobblestone. It collects matching dropped items nearby. It does not mine blocks, empty containers or duplicate your item.

Drops: no natural item drops; an item you gave it is separate. Its value is helping collect existing items, not creating new supplies. Read, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.2ba0b0c0d0e00004.title: I have read the Allay entry
quest.firsttorch.field_animals.goat.desc:
Habitat and behaviour: Goats live in mountain biomes. They can ram, so a calm-looking Goat can still knock a player away from an edge.

Safety: watch from level, open ground and keep well back from cliffs. Do not force an encounter or stand in a ramming lane just to get a horn.

Resources: Goats have no ordinary item drops on death. A Goat Horn comes from a Goat ramming a suitable block, such as Stone or a natural Overworld Log, not from killing it. On stable ground, use an empty Bucket on an adult Goat to collect Milk.

Usefulness: a Goat Horn is an instrument. Milk is a separate renewable resource. Read, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.26a0b0c0d0e0000a.title: I have read the Goat entry
quest.firsttorch.field_overworld.witch.d:
Habitat and behaviour: Witches are hostile Overworld mobs. They throw harmful potions and drink defensive ones, so a fight can change quickly.

Safety: use solid cover and a clear retreat; do not chase one into unknown ground for ingredients. Milk can clear status effects, including helpful ones, so use it deliberately.

Drops without Looting: a Witch guarantees 4–8 Redstone. Additional ordinary ingredients are randomly selected from Glowstone Dust, Sugar, Spider Eyes, Glass Bottles, Gunpowder, or Sticks and can be absent. Looting may increase ordinary drops.

Usefulness: these ingredients support Redstone and brewing, but no fight is required for this card. Read, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.27a0b0c0d0e00005.title: I have read the Witch entry
chapter.firsttorch.field_chambers_garden: Field Guide: Trial Chambers and Pale Garden
Optional cards about three unusual hostile encounters. Reading them requires neither a fight nor a structure visit.
You read the Trial Chambers and Pale Garden reference cards.
quest.firsttorch.field_chambers_garden.b:
Habitat and behaviour: Breezes are Trial Chambers enemies from Trial Spawners. They jump and use wind attacks that can knock you back.

Safety: do not rely on arrows; their deflection makes ranged shots unsafe as a plan. Keep firm ground, cover, and a fall-safe retreat before entering a chamber.

Drops without Looting: a player-credited death gives 1–2 Breeze Rods. Looting can increase the amount. A Heavy Core is not a Breeze drop; it is Ominous Vault loot.

Usefulness: Breeze Rods support Wind Charges and the Mace; the Heavy Core is separate. This card requires only reading, never combat. Read, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.2ca0b0c0d0e00001.title: I have read the Breeze entry
quest.firsttorch.field_chambers_garden.b:
Habitat and behaviour: Bogged are hostile skeleton variants in Swamps and Mangrove Swamps, and can also come from some Trial Spawners. Their arrows inflict Poison.

Safety: use solid shelter and plan a fall-safe escape; Poison plus a sudden retreat near a drop is especially dangerous. Do not make a visit for drops.

Drops without Looting: Bones and Arrows may each be 0–2. With player credit, 0–1 Poison Arrow is possible. Looting can increase ordinary drops.

Usefulness: Bones make Bone Meal and arrows are ammunition. No encounter is required for this card. Read, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.2ca0b0c0d0e00002.title: I have read the Bogged entry
quest.firsttorch.field_chambers_garden.c:
Habitat and behaviour: Creakings appear in a natural Pale Garden at night and are linked to a Creaking Heart hidden in Pale Oak. They freeze while you look at them. A Carved Pumpkin prevents that eye-freeze, so do not wear one as protection if your plan relies on watching the Creaking.

Safety: an attack does not normally kill the linked Creaking; destroying its Heart ends it. Do not search dangerously at night: withdraw to safe shelter, wait for daytime (Torch light is not a substitute), and return prepared if you choose to investigate.

Resources: Creakings have no ordinary item drops on death. The Heart and Resin are separate block mechanics, so this card does not promise either as a drop.

Usefulness: recognising the link explains why ordinary combat is not the solution. Read, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.2ca0b0c0d0e00003.title: I have read the Creaking entry
chapter.firsttorch.mechanics_blocks.desc: Optional cards about useful vanilla block transformations.
trophy.firsttorch.mechanics_blocks.title: Block changes noted
trophy.firsttorch.mechanics_blocks.descr: You read the changing-block reference cards.
quest.firsttorch.mechanics_blocks.concre:
Practical reference

Trigger: place Concrete Powder beside flowing or source water; it changes into Concrete. Rain and a Water Bottle do not cause this change.

Result: the coloured powder becomes the matching solid Concrete block.

Safety: test one block on small, flat ground away from important builds and water that could carry you or items away.

Optional experiment: place one powder block next to safe water and compare it with a dry one.

Read confirmation: this card requires reading only; no experiment is required. Read, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.2da0b0c0d0e00001.title: I have read the Concrete Powder entry
quest.firsttorch.mechanics_blocks.mud.de:
Practical reference

Trigger: use a Water Bottle on ordinary Dirt to turn it into Mud. Use it on the top face of Dirt, not a Grass Block. The water is used up, leaving an empty Glass Bottle. A Water Bucket does not cause this transformation.

Result: the Dirt block becomes Mud, a different block for building and later processing.

Safety: choose one unimportant block on small, level ground, not a valuable home floor or dangerous edge.

Optional experiment: change a single Dirt block and notice the Glass Bottle left behind.

Read confirmation: the observation is optional. Read, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.2da0b0c0d0e00002.title: I have read the Mud entry
quest.firsttorch.mechanics_blocks.sponge:
Practical reference

Trigger: put a Wet Sponge in the top Furnace slot and fuel in the bottom slot to dry it. A Sponge absorbs nearby water, not lava.

Result: after smelting, the Furnace returns a reusable Sponge.

Safety: keep the Furnace experiment to one block in a safe Overworld workspace; no Nether trip or lava test belongs to this card. Do not drain water that protects a route or farm.

Optional experiment: wet one Sponge in shallow water, then dry it with one Furnace fuel source.

Read confirmation: this is reading only, so no experiment is required. Read, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.2da0b0c0d0e00003.title: I have read the Sponge entry
chapter.firsttorch.mechanics_names.title: Reference: Special Names
chapter.firsttorch.mechanics_names.descr: Optional cards about three cosmetic Name Tag effects.
trophy.firsttorch.mechanics_names.title: Special names noted
trophy.firsttorch.mechanics_names.descri: You read the special-name reference cards.
quest.firsttorch.mechanics_names.dinnerb:
Optional discovery

Trigger: rename a Name Tag exactly Dinnerbone or Grumm in an Anvil, then use it on an animal. Renaming costs experience and can wear out the Anvil. Naming the animal consumes the Name Tag in Survival.

Result: the creature appears upside down. This is cosmetic: health and behaviour do not change.

Safety: naming is optional. If you try it, use a safe animal at home, not a hostile mob. Naming does not tame an animal.

Optional experiment: name one calm animal with the exact spelling.

Read confirmation: this card requires reading only. Read, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.2ea0b0c0d0e00001.title: I have read the Dinnerbone and Grumm entry
quest.firsttorch.mechanics_names.jeb.des:
Optional discovery

Trigger: rename a Name Tag exactly jeb_ in an Anvil, then use it on a Sheep. The lowercase letters and underscore matter; renaming costs experience and can wear out the Anvil. Naming the animal consumes the Name Tag in Survival.

Result: the Sheep's appearance cycles through rainbow colours. Its wool drop stays the Sheep's stored wool colour, not rainbow wool.

Safety: naming is optional. Use a safe home Sheep if you test it, and do not name hostile creatures for a cosmetic effect.

Optional experiment: observe the colour cycle without shearing.

Read confirmation: no experiment is required. Read, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.2ea0b0c0d0e00002.title: I have read the jeb_ Sheep entry
quest.firsttorch.mechanics_names.toast.d:
Optional discovery

Trigger: rename a Name Tag exactly Toast in an Anvil, then use it on a Rabbit. Renaming costs experience and can wear out the Anvil. Naming the animal consumes the Name Tag in Survival.

Result: the Rabbit gains the black-and-white Toast appearance. It is cosmetic only and does not change health or behaviour.

Safety: you do not need to find or name a Rabbit for this reading card. If you test it, use a Rabbit in a safe home enclosure and avoid naming hostile creatures.

Optional experiment: name one safely kept Rabbit with the exact capital T spelling.

Read confirmation: reading is the only required action. Read, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.2ea0b0c0d0e00003.title: I have read the Toast Rabbit entry
chapter.firsttorch.mechanics_bees.title: Reference: Bee Mechanics
chapter.firsttorch.mechanics_bees.descri: Optional cards about pollination and safe hive harvesting.
trophy.firsttorch.mechanics_bees.title: Bee mechanics noted
trophy.firsttorch.mechanics_bees.descrip: You read the bee-mechanics reference cards.
quest.firsttorch.mechanics_bees.pollinat:
Practical reference

Trigger: a Bee carries pollen from a flower back to its Bee Nest or Beehive and flies over growing crops such as Wheat.

Result: pollination can boost the growth of crops it flies over, but access must stay open and growth is not guaranteed immediately.

Safety: leave flowers, crops, and the flight path clear. Do not hit Bees or block their home merely to force an observation.

Optional experiment: watch a Bee visit a flower, carry pollen, and return home beside a small crop patch.

Read confirmation: this is an optional observation, not a required growth test. Read, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.2fa0b0c0d0e00001.title: I have read the Bee Pollination entry
quest.firsttorch.mechanics_bees.honey_bo: Honey Bottle from a Full Hive

Practical reference

Trigger: wait until a Bee Nest or Beehive is full, with honey visible on the front, then use a Glass Bottle. A Water Bottle does not collect honey.

Result: you receive a Honey Bottle.

Safety: use a lit Campfire two blocks below the Nest or Hive, with a carpet directly on the fire between them. Otherwise keep the vertical path between the fire and Nest clear. This protects Bees from fire; smoke cannot calm Bees already angry. Do not break its home for this experiment.

Optional experiment: prepare a safe, full hive and collect one Honey Bottle.

Read confirmation: harvesting is never required. Read, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.2fa0b0c0d0e00002.title: I have read the Honey Bottle entry
quest.firsttorch.mechanics_bees.honeycom:
Practical reference

Trigger: when a Bee Nest or Beehive is full, with honey visible on the front, use Shears to collect Honeycomb.

Result: a harvest gives three Honeycomb.

Safety: use a lit Campfire two blocks below the Nest or Hive, with a carpet directly on the fire between them. Otherwise keep the vertical path between the fire and Nest clear. This protects Bees from fire; smoke cannot calm Bees already angry. Do not break its home for this experiment; doing so can anger Bees and destroy their home.

Optional experiment: prepare a protected full hive, then shear it once.

Read confirmation: no harvest is required; this card records reading only. Read, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.2fa0b0c0d0e00003.title: I have read the Honeycomb entry
quest.firsttorch.field_animals.rabbit.de:
Habitat and behaviour: Rabbits are shy Overworld animals found in places such as deserts and snowy areas. Approach slowly and watch from safe ground.

Safety: do not chase them towards cliffs or into unknown terrain. This reading card requires neither catching nor killing a Rabbit.

Adult drops without Looting: 0–1 Rabbit Hide and 1 Raw Rabbit. Fire can make the meat drop already cooked. Looting can increase hide and meat quantities.

Rare drop: a player-credited death also has a 10% chance of a Rabbit's Foot. Looting adds 3 percentage points per level, reaching 19% with Looting III. A foot is not guaranteed.

Usefulness: Rabbit Hide can be crafted into Leather, the meat is food, and a Rabbit's Foot is an ingredient for a Potion of Leaping. The related name reference explains the cosmetic name Toast. Read, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.26a0b0c0d0e0000b.title: I have read the Rabbit entry
chapter.firsttorch.mechanics_archaeology: Optional cards about careful excavation and archaeology finds.
You read the archaeology reference cards.
quest.firsttorch.mechanics_archaeology.b:
Practical reference

Archaeology starts with looking closely: some ruins and desert structures contain Suspicious Sand or Suspicious Gravel. Their textures differ only slightly from ordinary blocks.

In the comparison: 1 = ordinary Sand, 2 = Suspicious Sand, 3 = ordinary Gravel, 4 = Suspicious Gravel. The suspicious blocks have not been brushed yet.

Do not mine a suspicious block or remove its support. Breaking or falling destroys the find; Silk Touch does not save it. First establish firm footing and safe surroundings.

Safe optional observation: compare blocks 1 and 2 in the illustration, then 3 and 4. Notice the different markings without touching or breaking any block in the world.

The next step explains uncovering the find with a Brush. This questline requires reading only, not a trip to a ruin. Read, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.5da0b0c0d0e00001.title: I have read how to recognise suspicious blocks
quest.firsttorch.mechanics_archaeology.f:
Practical reference

After recognising the suspicious block and securing its surroundings, use a Brush rather than a Shovel.

Craft a Brush by placing a Feather, Copper Ingot and Stick in a Crafting Table, vertically in that order from top to bottom.

Aim the Brush at the suspicious block and hold the use button. The find first becomes partly visible. Keep brushing until it drops out and the block becomes ordinary Sand or Gravel.

Leave its support in place and protect yourself from enemies and falls. The Brush loses durability; no find is worth putting yourself in danger.

Optionally brush a block that you can already reach safely. This is not needed for the checkmark. Next, learn what the find means. Read, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.5da0b0c0d0e00002.title: I understand how to uncover a find safely
quest.firsttorch.mechanics_archaeology.f:
Practical reference

Trigger: a fully brushed suspicious block can reveal a find from the possibilities for that site.

Result: the result is random, so a particular item is never promised. Pottery Sherds can be used when crafting a Decorated Pot.

Safety: do not chase a desired find through a dangerous ruin or cave. Keep any result safely.

Optional observation: inspect a Pottery Sherd or a Decorated Pot when you find one.

Read confirmation: no specific loot is required. Read, then confirm.
task.firsttorch.5da0b0c0d0e00003.title: I have read the Finds entry
chapter.firsttorch.mechanics_music.title: Reference: Music Discs
chapter.firsttorch.mechanics_music.descr: Optional cards about safe music playback and disc sources.
trophy.firsttorch.mechanics_music.title: Music noted
trophy.firsttorch.mechanics_music.descri: You read the music-disc reference cards.
quest.firsttorch.mechanics_music.jukebox: Play a Disc in a Jukebox

Optional discovery

Trigger: use a Music Disc on a Jukebox.

Result: the track plays once and then stops. Using the Jukebox again ejects the disc; playback does not consume it.

Safety: test at home or another safe place, and keep the disc away from lava, fire, and dangerous edges.
